export const meta = {
  name: 'map-devenv-codebases',
  description: 'Deep-read every repo in /Users/suhaan/devenv and return structured maps',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Core repos', detail: 'Opus xhigh deep read: cli, entire.io, entiredb, entire-api', model: 'opus' },
    { title: 'Aux repos', detail: 'Sonnet medium: branch clones, mocktests, root bootstrap', model: 'sonnet' },
  ],
}

const REPO_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  required: ['name', 'purpose', 'stack', 'architecture', 'key_modules', 'entry_points', 'build_test_run', 'recent_work', 'relations', 'notable'],
  properties: {
    name: { type: 'string' },
    purpose: { type: 'string', description: 'What this product/service is, 2-4 sentences' },
    stack: { type: 'string', description: 'Languages, frameworks, major deps, infra' },
    architecture: { type: 'string', description: 'How the code is organized and flows, 1-3 paragraphs' },
    key_modules: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', required: ['path', 'role'], properties: { path: { type: 'string' }, role: { type: 'string' } } } },
    entry_points: { type: 'string' },
    build_test_run: { type: 'string', description: 'How to build, test, run locally' },
    recent_work: { type: 'string', description: 'What recent commits/branches focus on' },
    relations: { type: 'string', description: 'How this repo connects to the other entire repos (cli, entire.io web, entiredb, entire-api)' },
    notable: { type: 'string', description: 'Gotchas, unusual patterns, config, state worth knowing' },
  },
}

const BRANCH_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  required: ['name', 'branch', 'purpose', 'diff_summary', 'status'],
  properties: {
    name: { type: 'string' },
    branch: { type: 'string' },
    purpose: { type: 'string', description: 'What this branch is building' },
    diff_summary: { type: 'string', description: 'What changed vs main: files, features, size' },
    status: { type: 'string', description: 'WIP/done/stale, ahead/behind main, uncommitted changes' },
  },
}

const AUX_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  required: ['items'],
  properties: {
    items: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        required: ['name', 'purpose', 'contents', 'notable'],
        properties: {
          name: { type: 'string' },
          purpose: { type: 'string' },
          contents: { type: 'string' },
          notable: { type: 'string' },
        },
      },
    },
  },
}

const CORE = [
  { dir: '/Users/suhaan/devenv/cli', hint: 'entireio/cli on main — the Entire CLI product. Likely Go or TS. Map commands, TUI, agent integration.' },
  { dir: '/Users/suhaan/devenv/entire.io', hint: 'entirehq/entire.io on branch feat-cursor-image-gallery — the web platform/viewer. Note: memory says session viewer renders externalized images (PR #2746). Map app structure, routes, viewer, API client.' },
  { dir: '/Users/suhaan/devenv/entiredb', hint: 'entirehq/entiredb on main — database layer. Map schema/migrations, what stores sessions/checkpoints, how consumed by api/web.' },
  { dir: '/Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-api', hint: 'entirehq/entire-api on main — API service. Map endpoints, auth, storage, how cli and web talk to it.' },
]

const CORE_PROMPT = (r) => `Deep-read the git repo at ${r.dir} and return a structured map. Context: ${r.hint}

Method:
1. Read README/docs, package.json / go.mod / pyproject / Cargo.toml etc.
2. Map the source tree 2-3 levels deep (ignore node_modules, vendor, dist, build, .git, .next, target).
3. Read the main entry points and the 5-10 most load-bearing source files (routers, schema, command registry, core domain logic).
4. Run: git -C ${r.dir} log --oneline -20 ; git -C ${r.dir} status --short | head -30 ; git -C ${r.dir} branch -a | head -20
5. Note env/config files, CI, deploy setup.

Be thorough and specific — real paths, real names. Your final output is consumed by an orchestrator building a full mental model of the Entire product suite (cli + web + db + api).`

const CLI_BRANCHES = [
  { dir: '/Users/suhaan/devenv/cli-image', branch: 'feat-why-tui' },
  { dir: '/Users/suhaan/devenv/cli-passive-v1', branch: 'feat-agent-help-passive-v1' },
  { dir: '/Users/suhaan/devenv/cli-soph-fixes', branch: 'soph-review-fixes' },
]

const BRANCH_PROMPT = (b) => `The repo at ${b.dir} is a separate clone of entireio/cli checked out on branch ${b.branch}. Determine what this branch is building and its state.

Run:
- git -C ${b.dir} fetch origin main 2>/dev/null (skip if no network); git -C ${b.dir} log --oneline main..HEAD 2>/dev/null || git -C ${b.dir} log --oneline -15
- git -C ${b.dir} diff main...HEAD --stat 2>/dev/null | tail -30
- git -C ${b.dir} status --short | head -20

Then read the 3-6 most-changed files enough to describe the feature. Report purpose, what changed vs main, and status (WIP/complete/stale, uncommitted work).`

const MOCKTEST_PROMPT = `Survey these 4 small local-only git repos (no remotes) under /Users/suhaan/devenv:
- entire-image-mocktest (branch img-test)
- entire-codex-image-mocktest (branch codex-img-test)
- entire-cursor-image-mocktest (branch cursor-img-test)
- entire-gemini-image-mocktest (branch gemini-img-test)

For each: list files, read the key ones, run git log --oneline -10. They appear to be test fixtures for image handling across different AI coding agents (Claude/Codex/Cursor/Gemini). Report one item per repo: purpose, contents, notable differences between them.`

const ROOT_PROMPT = `Survey the devenv bootstrap root at /Users/suhaan/devenv (the repo itself, NOT the sub-repos cli*/entire*/experts*). Read:
- README.md, MACBOOK_QUICKSTART.md, Onboarding.md, Brewfile, mise.toml, setup-repos.sh, start-dev.sh (note: start-dev.sh has uncommitted modifications — run git -C /Users/suhaan/devenv diff start-dev.sh)
- entire-experts-agent-context.md (7KB context doc — summarize fully, it explains the experts feature)
- skills-lock.json, .gitignore
- Directory listings of .entire/ and .agents/ plus their small files
- experts-command-only/ and experts-local-demo/ (tiny dirs — read their contents)
- Skim entire.log first/last 30 lines for what it captured

Report one item per artifact group: purpose, contents, notable. This is the dev-environment bootstrap repo for the Entire team — explain how a new machine gets set up and what services start-dev.sh runs.`

phase('Core repos')
const [coreResults, auxResults] = await parallel([
  () => parallel(CORE.map(r => () =>
    agent(CORE_PROMPT(r), { label: `deep:${r.dir.split('/').pop()}`, phase: 'Core repos', model: 'opus', effort: 'xhigh', schema: REPO_SCHEMA })
  )),
  () => parallel([
    ...CLI_BRANCHES.map(b => () =>
      agent(BRANCH_PROMPT(b), { label: `branch:${b.branch}`, phase: 'Aux repos', model: 'sonnet', effort: 'medium', schema: BRANCH_SCHEMA })),
    () => agent(MOCKTEST_PROMPT, { label: 'mocktests', phase: 'Aux repos', model: 'sonnet', effort: 'medium', schema: AUX_SCHEMA }),
    () => agent(ROOT_PROMPT, { label: 'devenv-root', phase: 'Aux repos', model: 'sonnet', effort: 'medium', schema: AUX_SCHEMA }),
  ]),
])

const [branchResults, mocktests, rootSurvey] = [auxResults.slice(0, 3), auxResults[3], auxResults[4]]
log(`Core: ${coreResults.filter(Boolean).length}/4, branches: ${branchResults.filter(Boolean).length}/3, aux: ${[mocktests, rootSurvey].filter(Boolean).length}/2`)
return { core: coreResults.filter(Boolean), branches: branchResults.filter(Boolean), mocktests, root: rootSurvey }

# Entire Product Suite — Codebase Map

> Synthesized 2026-07-09 from deep reads of every repo in this devenv. Update when architecture shifts.

## What Entire is

Entire captures AI coding-agent sessions (prompts, responses, files touched, tokens, tool calls) as **checkpoints** indexed alongside git commits, then renders them for search, review, provenance ("why did this code change"), and rewind. It never commits to the working branch — all session metadata lives on a separate `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. Supported agents: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Copilot CLI, Factory AI Droid (+ Vogon test agent).

## The four tiers

### 1. `cli/` — entireio/cli (Go 1.26.4, client tier)

The `entire` CLI + `git-remote-entire` (git remote helper for `entire://` URLs). Cobra + Charm (bubbletea/huh/lipgloss) stack.

- **Command surface**: ~200 flat files in `cmd/entire/cli/` (`<noun>_group.go` / `<noun>_<verb>.go` naming, `hideAsAlias` for legacy shortcuts). Registry in `cmd/entire/cli/root.go` (`NewRootCmd`).
- **Agent plugin system**: `cmd/entire/cli/agent/agent.go` defines `Agent` + ~18 optional capability interfaces (HookSupport, TranscriptAnalyzer, Launcher, …); each agent self-registers via `init()` in `agent/registry.go`. Hooks installed into each tool's native config call back into hidden `entire hooks <agent> <verb>` commands (`hook_registry.go`), which drive `lifecycle.go`'s `DispatchLifecycleEvent` (~1500 lines, the orchestration heart).
- **Strategy** (`strategy/`): manual-commit — per-commit/worktree shadow branches (`entire/<hash>-<worktreeHash>`), condensed into `entire/checkpoints/v1` on user commits, linked via `Entire-Checkpoint:` git trailers. Git hooks: prepare-commit-msg, post-commit, post-rewrite, pre-push. Two checkpoint backends: `branch` and `refs` (`--checkpoint-backend`).
- **Redaction** (`redact/`): 7-layer at condense + optional OPF (OpenAI Privacy Filter) 8th layer at pre-push. Security-critical — checkpoints branch may be public; shadow branches may hold unredacted data and must not be pushed.
- **Two backend planes**: control plane via `internal/coreapi` (ogen-generated Core API client — orgs/projects/repos/grants/mirrors); data plane via per-jurisdiction entire-api cells (`cell_target.go`/`cell_fanout.go`: repo→one cell, user→home cell, repo-set→fan-out-merge). `entire api` = gh-style authenticated passthrough.
- **Gotchas**: go-git v6 only for in-memory tree building — never checkout/reset (deletes ignored dirs; use `HardResetWithProtection`). Settings only via `settings` package. Every TUI flow needs a non-interactive equivalent (agent-safe). Vogon E2E canary parses prompts with hardcoded regexes — rerun after prompt-wording changes. `mise run check` = required pre-commit gate.

### 2. `entiredb/` — entirehq/entiredb (Go, git storage backend — NOT a generic DB)

Two planes, one repo, module `entire.io`:

- **Data plane** (`cmd/entiredb` → `internal/entireserver`): git smart-HTTP + REST git-read API (`server/repoapi/`, huma/OpenAPI). Refs in **PostgreSQL** (`refstore/`, CAS via `CheckAndSetReference`); objects content-addressed in **BadgerDB** replicated over a **Kademlia DHT** keyed by RepoID (quorum ≥2 providers across ≥2 AZs, no Raft — correctness from content-addressing + CAS + quorum). Ports: 8080 (h2c public), 8280 (mTLS gRPC peer transfer), 8281 (mTLS core→node), 9999 (memberlist gossip).
- **Control plane** (`cmd/entire-core` → `internal/entirecore`): identity, OAuth/OIDC/JWKS, RFC-8693 STS token exchange, SpiceDB authz, org/project/repo lifecycle — on **CockroachDB**. Serves `/api/v1` product-lifecycle API (`core/coreapi/`) consumed by CLI + web. Modes: standalone/global/regional.
- **Event spine**: every ref change → NATS JetStream `repo_refs_v1` via transactional outbox (`refevents/outbox.go`) — this is how entire-api and search stay in sync.
- **Terminology trap**: "sessions"/"checkpoints" here = OAuth login sessions (`core/authn`) and git refs/trailers — NOT the product entities (those live in entire-api). Product transcripts are NOT stored in entiredb except as git content on the checkpoints branch.
- Migrations: per-domain goose sets, separate version tables, FK-dependency order via `entire-core migrate --scope global|regional`; data plane self-migrates at boot. `refs.ref_name` is `COLLATE "C"` (keep `internal/migrations` and `refstore.InitSchema` in sync). Pre-production posture per its CLAUDE.md: no backwards-compat, rename/delete freely. Direction: ADR `docs/adrs/20260622-entire-api-product-layer.md` — entiredb narrows to pure git data plane, product surface moves to entire-api.

### 3. `entire-api/` — entirehq/entire-api (Go, per-jurisdiction product API "cell")

One module, three processes (single distroless image, command per k8s Deployment):

- **`cmd/api`**: unified HTTP server (huma/v2 over chi). Serves product surface at `/api/v1` AND absorbs the old api-gateway (`internal/gateway`): merges OpenAPI specs of cell services (entiredb git plane under `/api/v1/git/*`, peregrine `/search`, entire-search `/semantic-search`) and reverse-proxies them. No NATS, no workers.
- **`cmd/repo-activity`**: JetStream ingester on `repo_refs_v1` → chunked index jobs (one Repo-API page per message) → repo store + `repo_author_day` rollups; forwarder publisher ships residency-safe per-user metadata directly to the author's home-region NATS; checkpoint-analysis consumer (Anthropic SDK — on workspace cap 400, parks job as `labels_state=deferred`, recover via `replay-deferred-analysis`).
- **`cmd/user-activity`**: consumes `user_activity_v1` → user store `my_activity` (month-range-partitioned; partitions provisioned out-of-band BEFORE traffic or inserts fail).
- **Storage**: one Postgres per region, two schemas (`repo`/`usr`) isolated by DB roles + search_path (ADR 0001). Repo store is NOT a git replica — content read through to entiredb at request time, cached by branch tip. Residency-safe pointers only (repo_id, sha, checkpoint_id).
- **Authz**: SpiceDB read-only (vendored from entiredb `core/authz`, re-sync on merge), fail-closed, authz-before-existence (403/503 before any 404), deny re-checked at fully_consistent. Read `CONTEXT.md` before touching the auth/authz seam.
- **Residency**: server never makes cross-region calls; multi-region aggregation is client-side fan-out via `GET /api/v1/experimental/me` jurisdiction list. `ACTIVITY_SINGLE_REGION=true` required for single-region deploys.
- Replaces entire.io BFF's activity endpoints (cache.ts/me.ts/recap.ts) per its README. Optional second inbound mTLS listener (:8281) for entire-mcp — mTLS is the pipe, bearer auth still required.

### 4. `entire.io/` — entirehq/entire.io (TS monorepo, web tier)

pnpm workspaces + mise; three deployables:

- **`api/`** — the BFF, Cloudflare Worker "partial-to-api" (service `web-bff-api`): Hono 4, Kysely over PlanetScale MySQL via Hyperdrive (106 migrations), KV cache (shape-versioned keys), R2 (transcripts/attachments/images), Queues (webhooks, repo-sync, search-index, sandbox runs, session-name gen), Durable Objects (EditorDocument, RunnerScheduler, TrailWatch, RepoWatch, AnthropicRateLimiter), crons. Giant route modules: `routes/cache.ts` ~218KB (repo/commit/checkpoint/session reads + gallery) and `routes/trails.ts` ~231KB (PR-like review objects) — grep, don't read whole. `GitSource` layer (`lib/git-source/`) routes git reads GitHub-vs-`go-git-api` (VPC binding) to migrate off GitHub.
- **`frontend/`** — React 19 + Vite + TanStack Router/Query, feature domains under `src/domains/platform/*`, file routes under `src/routes/` (`_app/_repo/gh/$org.$repo.*`). Talks to API via generated SDK (`src/gen/api-sdk/` from `docs/openapi.json`) + hand-written CSRF-cookie client. `SessionTimelineView.tsx` (~2355 lines) renders transcripts + image gallery.
- **`website/`** — marketing/blog.
- **Images**: CLI externalizes inline images to `entire-asset:assets/img-<hex>.<ext>` placeholders + blobs; `api/src/lib/transcript-image-assets.ts` reverses that via R2 (best-effort, never 500s, skips caching on failed lookup) — PR #2746. Current branch `feat-cursor-image-gallery`: Cursor "sidecar" images (staged but not inline-referenced) surfaced as gallery strip; gallery images returned as URLs (`SessionGalleryImage {name, mediaType, url}`), not base64.
- Route mount ORDER in `app.ts` matters (public routes before wildcard-auth runner/trail routes). Generated code (api-sdk, schema.ts, routeTree.gen.ts) never hand-edited.

## End-to-end data flow

```
agent session (Claude Code/Codex/Cursor/…)
  → native hooks → entire hooks <agent> <verb> → DispatchLifecycleEvent
  → shadow branch (entire/<hash>-<worktreeHash>)
  → condense on user commit (redact 7-layer) → entire/checkpoints/v1 branch (+ Entire-Checkpoint trailer)

  → readers: entire.io BFF + entire-api /api/v1 (content read-through to entiredb Repo API)
  → frontend viewer (transcripts, checkpoints, trails; images hydrated from R2 / asset URLs)
```

Auth spine: entire-core IdP → RFC-8693 token exchange → per-jurisdiction identity tokens. ## Token accounting (state as of 2026-07-09)

Canonical type: `types.TokenUsage` (cli `cmd/entire/cli/agent/types/token_usage.go`) — InputTokens (fresh), CacheCreationTokens, CacheReadTokens, OutputTokens, APICallCount, recursive SubagentTokens. No cost, no reasoning tokens, no model, no service tier. Agents map into it via `TokenCalculator` (7 implementers; Cursor via stop-hook payload). Persisted in checkpoint metadata (`api/checkpoint/metadata.go`: Metadata.TokenUsage/Model/SessionMetrics), ingested by entire-api into Postgres BIGINT columns, surfaced by overview panels (checkpoint-metrics, agent-activity, contributor-tokens) and frontend raw k/M/B counts. Diagnostic commands: `entire session tokens`, `entire checkpoint tokens [--compare]`, hidden `entire tokens profile`.

Known dropped data (parsed then discarded): Codex `reasoning_output_tokens`, Gemini `thoughts`, OpenCode `reasoning` + `cost` float, Cursor hook `cost`. Input-vs-cache conventions reconciled ad hoc per agent (Codex/Cursor subtract cache from total input; others treat input as fresh). Zero pricing/USD math anywhere in the suite. Transcript-level signals available but unparsed: Claude `usage.speed` ("fast"/"standard" — direct /fast detection) + per-turn `message.model`; Codex `turn_context.model` + `rate_limits` (used_percent, plan_type, rate_limit_reached_type — quota/overage signal). Pi emits token counts only, no cost. Seed for agent-reported out-of-band usage: unmerged `feat/antigravity-tokens` (status-snapshot deltas).

## PRs + trails on token analytics

**Open (cli):**
| # | Title | State |
|---|---|---|
| #1666 | live token counts for claude and codex reviewers | open, = **trail #788** (phase: reviewing) |
| #1394 | preserve Claude subagent token totals during condensation | open bug |
| #1388 | pin down Cursor token-usage condensation gap | open test |
| #1570 | codex subagent tracking (parity w/ Claude) | open |
| #956 | Claude token usage always 0 (flush sentinel timeout) | open issue |

**Merged:** cli #1263 (Cursor tokens), #1393/#1400/#1417/#1558 (Codex token diagnostics series), #1356 (antigravity native tokens), #1021 (Codex normalization fix), #1482 (TokenUsage detangle). entire.io #377 (checkpoint token display), #1347 (overview redesign), #1604 (recap), #2719+#2792 (Anthropic calls → Cloudflare AI Gateway = server-side cost observability). entire-api #38/#209/#241 (analysis pipeline + call pacing + gateway).

**Unmerged branches:** cli `feat/antigravity-tokens` (out-of-band status-snapshot capture — the seed pattern for agent-reported usage), `feat/gemini-session-token-tracking`, `rwr/refactor-calculateTokenUsage`; entire.io `add-token-usage-overview` (user-dashboard token card, today-only, stalled).

**Trails:** `entire trail list` works — 10 open trails on entireio/cli; #788 maps 1:1 to PR #1666.

## The 4 bullets — feasibility (verified against real transcripts on your machine)

**1. Show costs / guesstimate.** Nothing in suite has cost today — zero pricing tables, zero USD. Two corrections to the premise: **Pi does NOT provide cost** (`pijsonl.Usage` is token-counts only, verified in code + no local Pi sessions exist) — but **OpenCode DOES provide a `cost` float and Cursor's stop-hook has `cost` too, and both are currently parsed-then-discarded**. Cheapest win: stop dropping those. For Claude/Codex estimation: per-turn model IS available (`message.model` / `turn_context.model`), so token×price works — needs a maintained price table with Claude cache multipliers (write 1.25×, read 0.1×).

**2. More analysis tools.** Base exists: `entire session tokens`, `checkpoint tokens --compare`, hidden `tokens profile` — all token-pressure heuristics, explicitly "not a cost model". entire-api already stores cache/api_call columns it never surfaces (contributor-tokens + agent-activity expose input+output only). Model column exists on checkpoints/sessions, **never used in any aggregation** — per-model breakdown is free real estate.

**3. Normalization.** No shared normalizer — each agent hand-corrects conventions independently: Codex/Cursor report input as total-including-cache (code subtracts), Claude/Gemini/Pi report fresh input. Reasoning tokens have **no schema slot** — Codex `reasoning_output_tokens`, Gemini `thoughts`, OpenCode `reasoning` all silently dropped; Claude folds thinking into output (asymmetry to document, not fix). Codex/Gemini have no cache_creation concept. Fix = extend `types.TokenUsage` (reasoning, cost, cost_source) + one shared normalizer package replacing per-agent math.

**4. Claude /fast + overage detection.** **Feasible, direct signal exists**: Claude transcripts carry `usage.speed` = `"fast"`/`"standard"` per turn — verified in a real session (1862 fast + 516 standard turns on opus-4-8 in one session; `service_tier` is a separate field, always "standard", NOT the signal). CLI's claudecode parser currently reads only the 4 token fields — one struct field away. Overage: Claude has no explicit quota field → infer (speed frequency, model shifts). Codex conversely exposes it directly: `rate_limits.{used_percent, window_minutes, plan_type, rate_limit_reached_type}` on every token_count event.

## Suggested build order

1. Correctness first: land #1394 + #1388 (tokens being lost today)
2. Schema: TokenUsage += ReasoningTokens; Metadata += CostUSD/CostSource + per-turn speed counts in SessionMetrics — all optional JSON, back-compat
3. Stop dropping: OpenCode/Cursor cost, Codex reasoning + rate_limits, Gemini thoughts, Claude `usage.speed`
4. Pricing table (versioned model→price, cache multipliers) + estimated-vs-reported labeling
5. Shared normalizer package; document asymmetries
6. Pipeline: new columns in entire-api, cost + per-model breakdown in overview panels

## Requirements

# Cost Reporting / Estimation — CLI-Core Implementation Plan

## Design decisions (recommended + justified)

### (a) Schema: `CostUSD *float64` + `CostSource string` INSIDE `types.TokenUsage`; float64 USD

**Put cost fields inside `types.TokenUsage`, not a sibling struct.** The three summation functions and the `SubagentTokens` recursion already walk this struct; a scalar added here plumbs through accumulate → aggregate → reaggregate → subagent recursion with edits to only those 3 functions. A sibling struct would need parallel plumbing through every path (StepContext, SessionState, WriteOptions, Metadata, CheckpointSummary, e2e mirror) — far more churn and divergence risk.

**Use `*float64` (pointer), not `float64`.** Requirement 3 mandates "unknown model → absent cost, never zero/guessed." A pointer makes "no estimate available" (nil) distinguishable from a genuine computed `$0`, exactly the established nil-vs-zero pattern behind `Metadata.GetCompactTranscriptStart` (`*int`, metadata.go:342/402). `omitempty` on a nil pointer omits the field, giving free back-compat with old checkpoints.

**float64 USD, not integer micro-USD.** `Attribution.AgentPercentage` is already `float64` in the persisted schema (metadata.go:530), so float in metadata JSON is precedented. Per-message costs are ~1e-4 USD; float64 (~15-16 sig digits) summed over thousands of messages keeps error ≪ 1 cent. Micro-USD would force per-message rounding of `rate × tokens × 0.1` and introduce a rounding bias the backend can't undo. Document the value as estimate-grade (~cent precision); the backend re-quantizes.

```go
// types/token_usage.go — added fields
CostUSD    *float64 `json:"cost_usd,omitempty"`
CostSource string   `json:"cost_source,omitempty"` // "reported" | "estimated" | "mixed"
```
```go
const (
    CostSourceReported  = "reported"
    CostSourceEstimated = "estimated"
    CostSourceMixed     = "mixed"
)
```

### (d) Estimation runs in a CENTRALIZED post-parse hook fed by per-model token buckets

The parsers must be touched regardless (recon shows every one needs a model field threaded into its token loop). Given that, the real choice is: price inside each of 8 parsers, or have each parser emit a **per-model token tally** and price once centrally. **Centralize.** The versioned pricing lookup, Anthropic multipliers, unknown-model handling, and cost-source labeling live in ONE place instead of 8 copies. Each parser's change is mechanical: accumulate into a `map[model]TokenUsage` instead of a single `*TokenUsage`. This also naturally produces the per-model breakdown (b) needed for correctness under mixed models.

Mechanism: a new **optional** capability interface (parsers that can attribute per model implement it; others fall back to a single bucket keyed by the session-level `state.ModelName`):

```go
// agent/agent.go
type ModelUsageCalculator interface {
    DeclaredCaps  // gate like TokenCalculator
    CalculateModelUsage(transcriptData []byte, fromOffset int) ([]types.ModelUsage, error)
}
```
Buckets carry tokens only (cost nil), EXCEPT OpenCode which fills `CostUSD` from the reported `MessageInfo.Cost` sum with `CostSource=reported`. The dispatcher (`agent.CalculateTokenUsage` gains a cost-aware sibling `agent.CalculateUsageWithCost(ctx, ag, data, offset, subagentsDir, table)`) prices each unpriced bucket via `pricing.Estimate`, labels source, and folds buckets into the flat `*TokenUsage` (which flows through all existing plumbing unchanged, now with cost populated) plus returns the `[]ModelUsage` slice for (b).

### (b) Per-model breakdown: `Metadata.ModelUsage []ModelUsage`, accumulated in `SessionState`, shipped as the FINAL chunk

Needed because the backend wants per-model analytics and the session-level `Model` scalar + summed `CostUSD` cannot reconstruct which model cost what when models mix (verified: opus-4-8 + fable-5 in one Claude session). Build the per-model tally in the parser/estimator layer from **day one** (required for correct mixed-model cost anyway), but **persist the flat cost first (chunks 1-4) and add `ModelUsage` persistence as chunk 5** so the two schema changes (cost scalar; model breakdown) are independently reviewable and flat cost ships even if the breakdown slips. Accumulate in `SessionState.ModelUsage map[string]*TokenUsage` (checkpoint-scoped, reset alongside `CheckpointTokenUsage`), serialized to a sorted `[]ModelUsage` at condensation. Subagent per-model usage merges into the same top-level buckets (mirrors how `SubagentTokens` nests into the flat total), so per-model totals reconcile with the flat total.

```go
// types/token_usage.go
type ModelUsage struct {
    Model      string     `json:"model"`
    TokenUsage TokenUsage `json:"token_usage"` // embeds CostUSD + CostSource
}
```

### (c) Pricing package: `cmd/entire/cli/pricing/`

Mirror `runnerdefaults`: `//go:embed models/*.json` → `embed.FS`. Leaf package importing only `agent/types` + stdlib (so `settings` can import `pricing` with no cycle).

JSON shape (per file, one per provider):
```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "models": [
    {
      "id": "claude-opus-4-8",
      "provider": "anthropic",
      "aliases": ["claude-opus-4-8-*", "anthropic/claude-opus-4-8"],
      "input_per_mtok": 5.0,
      "output_per_mtok": 25.0,
      "effective_date": "2026-06-24"
    }
  ]
}
```
- **Cache rates:** optional `cache_read_per_mtok` / `cache_write_per_mtok`. When absent, fall back to Anthropic-convention multipliers `cache_read = 0.1×input`, `cache_write = 1.25×input` (package constants `AnthropicCacheReadMultiplier=0.1`, `AnthropicCacheWriteMultiplier=1.25`). Anthropic entries stay terse and correct; non-Anthropic providers that price cache differently set explicit rates. This encodes requirement 3's multipliers as data + one documented default, not scattered code.
- **Cost function** (provider-agnostic): `cost = (in·inRate + cacheR·cacheReadRate + cacheW·cacheWriteRate + out·outRate) / 1e6`, taking a `types.TokenUsage` (InputTokens is fresh/non-cached per the verified uniform contract).
- **Lookup semantics:** exact `id` → normalized (lowercase) alias/glob match → **miss = `(nil,false)` = no estimate.** Recommend AGAINST an implicit `claude-opus-*`→opus fallback (a future opus with different pricing would be silently mispriced, violating "never guessed"); family breadth is expressed only as explicit curated `aliases` globs, so every resolution maps to curated data.
- **Seed data:** `models/anthropic.json` (from the authoritative claude-api skill: Opus 4.8/4.7/4.6 $5/$25, Fable 5 $10/$50, Sonnet 5 $3/$15, Sonnet 4.6 $3/$15, Haiku 4.5 $1/$5), plus best-effort `models/openai.json` and `models/google.json` for Codex/Pi (OpenAI) and Gemini CLI (Google) models. Non-Anthropic rates are the weak point; the versioned table + settings override + unknown→no-estimate guarantee contain the blast radius.
- **Override merge (settings):** new nested pointer block mirroring `Redaction`/`Checkpoints`:
```go
// settings/settings.go
Pricing *PricingSettings `json:"pricing,omitempty"`
type PricingSettings struct {
    Models            []pricing.ModelRate `json:"models,omitempty"`  // replace-by-id or add
    DisableEstimation *bool               `json:"disable_estimation,omitempty"`
}
```
Merge (in a `mergePricing` helper like `mergeRedaction` settings.go:1114): user entries replace embedded entries by `id`, else append. `pricing.LoadTable(overrides)` layers overrides on the embedded FS. A `config.go`-layer bridge `LoadPricingTable(ctx)` reads `settings.Pricing` and builds the `pricing.Table`, honoring `DisableEstimation` (suppresses estimation; reported cost still flows). Keeps the settings-package-only rule intact.

### (e) Codex `turn_context` parsing

The token loop (transcript.go:269-330) currently diffs cumulative `total_token_usage` baseline-vs-last. To attribute deltas to the current turn's model:
```go
type turnContextPayload struct { Model string `json:"model"` } // rolloutLine.Type == "turn_context"
```
Interleave in the single scan: track `currentModel`, updated on each `turn_context` line (which precedes that turn's `token_count` events). Walk `token_count` snapshots in order after the offset; for each, `delta = snapshot - prevSnapshot` (prev starts at the baseline snapshot ≤ offset), and attribute `delta.{input,cacheRead,output}` to `currentModel`, applying `freshInput = input - cacheRead` (floor 0) per bucket. Flat total stays `last - baseline` (preserves current behavior); buckets sum to it. **Negative delta (counter reset on new turn) → clamp and re-baseline from 0** — strictly more robust than the current monotonic assumption.

### (f) factoryaidroid / no-model / subagents

- **factoryaidroid:** session-level only (sidecar `settings.json`). Emit a single bucket keyed by `state.ModelName` from the sidecar's session totals — the one agent where within-session model variance isn't observable, so session-scalar estimation is acceptable and correctly labeled `estimated`. No sidecar model/tokens → nil cost.
- **Unknown/empty model:** bucket contributes tokens but nil cost; flat `CostUSD` is the sum of PRICED buckets only, labeled `estimated` (or `mixed` if reported buckets also present, or if some tokens went unpriced — `mixed` documents "not uniformly one source, or partial coverage"). The per-model breakdown (b) is the authoritative coverage signal (unpriced bucket shows nil cost); the flat scalar is a convenience.
- **Subagents:** cost rides `SubagentTokens` because `CostUSD` is inside `TokenUsage`; the existing recursion in all 3 sum functions folds subagent cost into the parent automatically. Subagent per-model usage merges into the top-level `ModelUsage` map.

# Cost Display & Estimation for Entire Token Analytics (Full Stack)

## Context

Entire captures per-checkpoint token usage from 8 coding agents but shows raw token counts only — zero pricing/USD anywhere in cli, entire-api, or entire.io. Team priority: "show costs if agent provides them, or guesstimate them for codex/claude." Research findings driving this design:

- Only **OpenCode** reports cost (`MessageInfo.Cost float64` per-message, currently parsed-then-discarded). Cursor/Pi report tokens+model but NO cost (earlier premise "Pi provides cost" is false — verified in code).
- Model **varies within a session** (verified real transcript: opus-4-8 + fable-5 in one Claude session) → cost must be computed per-message at parse time, not post-hoc from the single session-level `Metadata.Model`.
- All agents already normalize to the same 5-field `types.TokenUsage`; `InputTokens` = fresh non-cached uniformly (Cursor/Codex subtract cache themselves).
- User decisions: **full stack now** (cli → metadata → entire-api → entire.io), **embedded pricing table + settings override**.

Outcome: `entire session/checkpoint tokens` show `$X (estimated|reported|mixed)`; cost persists in checkpoint metadata; entire-api ingests + aggregates; entire.io panels display it.

## Part A — CLI (entireio/cli)

### Schema decisions

- **`CostUSD *float64` + `CostSource string` INSIDE `types.TokenUsage`** (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/types/token_usage.go`). Rides the existing recursion in all three sum functions (`accumulateTokenUsage` strategy/manual_commit_git.go:313, `aggregateTokenUsage` checkpoint/persistent.go:960, `addCheckpointTokenUsage` checkpoint_tokens.go:359) and `SubagentTokens` nesting automatically.
- Pointer = nil-vs-zero discrimination (unknown model → absent, never $0) — same pattern as `Metadata.GetCompactTranscriptStart`. `omitempty` gives back-compat free.
- float64 USD (precedent: `Attribution.AgentPercentage`); ~cent precision documented; backend re-quantizes.
- `CostSource` constants: `reported | estimated | mixed`.
- **Per-model breakdown** `types.ModelUsage {Model string; TokenUsage TokenUsage}` — sibling `Metadata.ModelUsage []ModelUsage` (omitempty). Required: flat scalar can't reconstruct which model cost what.

### Pricing package (new `cmd/entire/cli/pricing/`)

Mirrors `runnerdefaults` embed pattern (`runnerdefaults/embed.go:14`): `//go:embed models/*.json`, leaf package (imports only `agent/types`).

- JSON per provider: `{schema_version, models: [{id, provider, aliases (globs), input_per_mtok, output_per_mtok, cache_read_per_mtok?, cache_write_per_mtok?, effective_date}]}`
- Cache rates optional → default Anthropic multipliers: read 0.1×, write 1.25× of input rate (package constants).
- Lookup: exact id → normalized alias/glob → **miss = no estimate** (no implicit family fallback — mispricing risk).
- Seed: `models/anthropic.json` (Opus 4.8 $5/$25, Fable 5 $10/$50, Sonnet 5 $3/$15, Haiku 4.5 $1/$5 per MTok), best-effort `openai.json`, `google.json`.
- Settings override: `EntireSettings.Pricing *PricingSettings {Models []pricing.ModelRate; DisableEstimation *bool}` (settings/settings.go:63 area, nested-pointer-block convention); user entries replace embedded by id else append; `DisableEstimation` suppresses estimation only, reported cost survives.

### Estimation point: centralized dispatcher, per-model buckets from parsers

New optional capability interface in `agent/agent.go`:

```go
type ModelUsageCalculator interface {
    DeclaredCaps
    CalculateModelUsage(transcriptData []byte, fromOffset int) ([]types.ModelUsage, error)
}
```

Parsers emit per-model token buckets (tokens only; OpenCode also fills reported cost). New `agent.CalculateUsageWithCost(...)` in `agent/token_usage.go` prices each unpriced bucket via `pricing.Estimate`, labels source, folds buckets into the flat `*TokenUsage`. Fallback for non-implementers: single bucket keyed by session `state.ModelName`. Wire at both estimation sites: `lifecycle.go:920-923` (incl. Cursor hook path — price from `event.TokenUsage` + `event.Model`) and `strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:646,930,972`; `config.LoadPricingTable(ctx)` bridges settings→table.

Per-agent model threading (recon-verified):
| Agent | Change |
|---|---|
| pi | model already per-message (`entry.Message.Model`) — bucket in existing loop |
| geminicli | add `Model json:"model"` to `geminiMessageWithTokens` (types.go:108) |
| claudecode | add `Model` to `messageWithUsage` (types.go:96); model rides the max-output dedup struct |
| codex | **new `turn_context` payload struct** (currently ignored, transcript.go:30); interleave in scan: track currentModel, per-snapshot delta attribution; clamp negative delta (counter reset) and re-baseline |
| opencode | add `ModelID json:"modelID"` to `MessageInfo`; sum `Cost` → `CostSource=reported` |
| copilotcli | `session.shutdown ModelMetrics` already keyed by model (transcript.go:216-236) — stop collapsing |
| cursor | hook path: tokens+model arrive together per turn |
| factoryaidroid | session-level sidecar model only → single bucket (acceptable, labeled estimated) |

### PR-sized chunks (CLI)

1. **`pricing` package standalone** — embed, table, lookup, Estimate (+multiplier tests), seed JSONs. Zero wiring.
2. **Cost fields + sum plumbing** — token_usage.go, 3 merge sites (`addCostUSD`/`mergeCostSource` helpers), e2e mirror `e2e/testutil/metadata.go:5-11`. JSON round-trip + back-compat tests (old JSON → nil).
3. **Estimation + parser threading** — 3a dispatcher/wiring + pi/gemini/cursor; 3b claudecode/codex (hardest: turn_context); 3c opencode(reported)/copilot/factorydroid. Mixed-model fixture (opus+fable) asserts split + buckets-sum-to-flat.
4. **Display** — session_tokens.go / checkpoint_tokens.go (`--compare` cost delta) / tokens_profile.go; show only when present, suffix `(estimated)`/`(reported)`/`(mixed)`.
5. **Per-model persistence (fast-follow)** — StepContext.ModelUsage → SessionState.ModelUsage map (checkpoint-scoped reset) → WriteOptions → `Metadata.ModelUsage` + summary merge; vogon e2e.

### Edge cases (CLI)
Unknown model → unpriced bucket, flat = priced sum, source mixed/estimated; multi-session checkpoint mixing reported+estimated → `mixed`; override precedence by id; Codex counter reset clamp; Cursor input already fresh (no double count); `disable_estimation` keeps reported.

## Part B — Backend + Web pipeline (entire-api, entire.io)

_(section completed from pipeline design below)_

- CLI gate: `mise run check`; targeted `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/pricing/... ./cmd/entire/cli/agent/...`; vogon canary `mise run test:e2e:canary`.
- Hand-check: known token counts × Anthropic rates, confirm 1.25×/0.1× multipliers.
- Real transcripts: OpenCode fixture (`reported`), mixed-model Claude transcript (per-model split), then `entire session tokens --json` / `checkpoint tokens --json` / `tokens profile --json`.
- End-to-end (after Part B): seed → ingest → panel → UI.

# Implementation Plan: Per-Checkpoint Cost Data (entire-api + entire.io)

## Key architecture findings that shape the plan

- **The BFF proxy is a byte-shape passthrough** (`proxyEntireApiForSession` in `api/src/lib/entire-api/proxy.ts`, gated by `route-gate.ts`). Once the Go handler adds cost to its JSON, the proxied response carries it with **zero BFF route code**. This is why entire-api lands first.
- **The overview panels use hand-written FE types + fetchers** (`frontend/src/domains/platform/repo-overview/api.ts`), *not* the generated SDK. So the frontend panels need type edits, **no `openapi:generate`/`api:sdk` regen**. (The generated SDK is only in play for endpoints the SDK hooks consume — verify the checkpoint/session **detail** pages before assuming; see PR7.)
- **The nullable-token precedent already exists**: `sessions` table tokens are `BIGINT NULL`, set via a `hasTokens` gate in `sessions.go:476-502` (NULL = "no session reported", distinct from 0). Cost mirrors this exactly. In contrast `checkpoints`/`my_activity` tokens are `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` — cost must **break** that pattern and be `NULL`-able there, because absence ≠ $0.
- **Root `token_usage` is currently ignored** — `buildCheckpointRow` (checkpoint.go:372-378) sums per-session only; the `checkpointSummary.TokenUsage` field is parsed but unused. Cost follows the same per-session sum, with a root fallback as cheap insurance.

---

## Design decisions (recommend + justify)

### (a) Column types + semantics
- **`cost_usd NUMERIC(14,6) NULL`** on `checkpoints`, `sessions`, `my_activity`. NUMERIC (not float8) because it's money: exact `SUM()` accumulation with no drift, and the hint confirms NUMERIC is available. NULL-able everywhere (absence ≠ 0), overriding the `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` token convention on `checkpoints`/`my_activity`.
- **Reads always cast `cost_usd::float8`** and scan into `*float64`. This means the Go read path is identical to the existing `attribution_agent_percentage *float64` (DOUBLE PRECISION) pattern — **no `pgtype.Numeric` anywhere**. Exact accumulation stays in Postgres; only the final scalar is float8 for transport (a display cent value needs nothing more).
- **Writes bind `*float64`** (nil → NULL); pgx's NumericCodec encodes float64→numeric. (Zero-float alternative: decode `cost_usd` as `json.Number` and bind the string — note it, but `*float64` matches the rest of the ingest struct and is lower-friction.)
- **`cost_source TEXT NULL`** with `CHECK (cost_source IS NULL OR cost_source IN ('reported','estimated','mixed'))`. TEXT+CHECK, not a Postgres ENUM — the codebase uses TEXT for every small-vocab column (`payload_hydration_state`, `state`, `strategy`), and `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE` can't run inside Goose's transactional migration.
- **Per-model breakdown: store in the existing `sessions` JSONB, no new table, for v1.** Extend `SessionInfo` with `ModelUsage []ModelUsage` (`omitempty`). Justification: the per-session `model_usage` rides in the same frozen `sessions` JSONB that already carries `tokenUsage`/`attribution` (portable, materialiser reads it back unchanged, surfaces on checkpoint+session detail for free). **No v1 aggregation surface groups by model** (the note confirms `model` is used in zero aggregations today), so a dedicated `checkpoint_model_usage` table earns nothing until a "cost by model" panel exists — defer to v2.

### (b) Which surfaces get cost in v1 — with one consistent rule

**The consistent cost rule (applies to every aggregated cost surface):**
1. Storage: `cost_usd` is NULL when unknown, never 0-for-unknown; a real $0 is `0.000000`.
2. `SUM(cost_usd)` ignores NULLs → sum over **costed** checkpoints only; all-NULL → SUM is NULL → emit `null`, not 0.
3. Every cost sum is emitted with its **coverage**: `costed_checkpoints = COUNT(cost_usd)` alongside the existing `checkpoints = COUNT(*)`. UI renders "$X across N of M" and marks partial when N<M.
4. `cost_source` per scope = distinct non-null sources across costed checkpoints: uniform→that value, >1→`"mixed"`, N=0→`null`.
5. Averages divide by **N (costed)**, not M — mirroring `avg_tokens_per_checkpoint`, which already excludes zero-token checkpoints (`repo_aggregates.go:982`).

**v1 surfaces (all in entire-api, all flow through the proxy automatically):**
- `checkpoint-metrics`: `avg_cost_per_checkpoint` + `costed_checkpoint_count` + `cost_source`.
- `agent-activity` daily: per-(day,agent) `costUsd` + `costedCount` (camelCase — this panel returns JS objects directly).
- `contributor-tokens`: per-contributor `cost_usd` (even-split, **same divisor as tokens** = distinct groups; null when none of the contributor's checkpoints are costed). No per-contributor `cost_source` (low value; source lives on the summary/detail).
- Team `summary` + `agents`: `cost_usd` + `cost_source` + `costed_checkpoints`.
- checkpoint detail + session detail: root `costUsd`/`costSource`, per-session `tokenUsage.costUsd`/`costSource`, per-session `modelUsage[]`.
- **me/recap**: `summary.cost` + per-agent `cost` — included, but sequenced last (highest blast radius: residency event + user DB + partitioned table).

### (c) entire.io path: do NOT add cost to the PlanetScale fallback in v1
The `entire-api` flag targets the Entire staff cohort — exactly the callers who get proxied (real cost). The PlanetScale path is the legacy fallback for the non-flagged cohort; populating it would require cache.ts's checkpoint sync (`cache.ts:427-431,:576-579`) to re-parse the CLI's cost from metadata + a MySQL migration — **duplicating the Go ingest**. Since absence = "no cost data" is a state the UI must already handle for old checkpoints, the fallback simply **omits** cost and the UI shows the no-data state. Type the FE cost fields **optional** so the wire shape is a clean superset. Revisit only when cost graduates to GA (at which point the PlanetScale path is being retired anyway).

### (d) Frontend
- **Where:** (1) a new **"Spend"** `SmallStatCard` on `RepoAnalyticsPage` next to Throughput (total window cost + "N of M" coverage sublabel); (2) a total-cost line in `TokenUsageCard`; (3) per-contributor cost as a trailing text value in `ContributorTokensCard` (**not** a new bar — mixing $/tokens on one bar-list misleads); (4) a cost **pill** in `DetailHeader` next to the token pill.
- **Formatting** — new `formatCostUSD(v)` util: `null`→"—" (no-data); `0`→"$0.00"; `0<v<0.01`→"<$0.01" (exact in tooltip); `<1000`→2dp; `≥1000`→"$1.2k"/"$3.4M".
- **estimated-vs-reported:** subtle badge only when `cost_source !== "reported"` — "est" superscript with tooltip ("Estimated from token usage + model pricing"); `"mixed"`→"est*" tooltip ("Some sessions estimated"); `"reported"`→no badge.
- **Feature flag:** add `"checkpoint-cost"` to `feature-flags.json`; gate all cost UI via the existing PostHog runtime pattern so it ships dark and enables for the same staff cohort as the entire-api rollout.

### (e) Backfill + server-side estimation
- **No new backfill code, no mass backfill in v1.** The live ingest fills cost as new checkpoints land; the existing repo-activity backfill re-reads `metadata.json` and `UpsertCheckpoint` is idempotent, so cost flows through the existing machinery for free once the parse lands. Trigger a throttled (`BACKFILL_REPO_API_RPS`) re-hydrate only when CLI adoption warrants — not now.
- **Server-side estimation: never.** Computing cost from stored tokens+model server-side means a **second pricing table** that will drift from the CLI's as prices/models change — two sources of truth for one number, guaranteed to disagree per checkpoint. **The CLI is the single source of truth** (it owns model, per-model token split, and pricing). Old checkpoints stay unknown until the CLI re-writes their metadata; `cost_source` stays honest because every value originates at the CLI.

---

## Wire-shape diffs (JSON field names)

```
checkpoint-metrics  (+snake_case)
  + "avg_cost_per_checkpoint": number|null
  + "costed_checkpoint_count": number
  + "cost_source": "reported"|"estimated"|"mixed"|null

agent-activity .daily[]  (+camelCase — matches inputTokens/outputTokens)
  + "costUsd": number|null
  + "costedCount": number

contributor-tokens .contributors[]  (+snake_case — matches input_tokens)
  + "cost_usd": number|null

summary  &  agents[]  (team API, snake_case)

  + "cost_source": string|null
  + "costed_checkpoints": number        (summary only)

checkpoint detail (CheckpointInfo, camelCase)

me/recap  (camelCase)

  .agents[] + "cost": number|null
```

---

## Ordered, PR-sized plan (entire-api → entire.io)

Mirrors `runnerdefaults` embed pattern (`runnerdefaults/embed.go:14`): `//go:embed models/*.json`, leaf package (imports only `agent/types`).

- Cache rates optional → default Anthropic multipliers: read 0.1×, write 1.25× of input rate (package constants).

| codex | **new `turn_context` payload struct** (currently ignored, transcript.go:30); interleave in scan: track currentModel, per-snapshot delta attribution; clamp negative delta (counter reset) and re-baseline |
| opencode | add `ModelID json:"modelID"` to `MessageInfo`; sum `Cost` → `CostSource=reported` |
| copilotcli | `session.shutdown ModelMetrics` already keyed by model (transcript.go:216-236) — stop collapsing |
| cursor | hook path: tokens+model arrive together per turn |
| factoryaidroid | session-level sidecar model only → single bucket (acceptable, labeled estimated) |

5. **Per-model persistence (fast-follow)** — StepContext.ModelUsage → SessionState.ModelUsage map (checkpoint-scoped reset) → WriteOptions → `Metadata.ModelUsage` + summary merge; vogon e2e.

- **`CostUSD *float64` + `CostSource string` INSIDE `types.TokenUsage`** (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/types/token_usage.go`). Rides the existing recursion in all three sum functions (`accumulateTokenUsage` strategy/manual_commit_git.go:313, `aggregateTokenUsage` checkpoint/persistent.go:960, `addCheckpointTokenUsage` checkpoint_tokens.go:359) and `SubagentTokens` nesting automatically.
- Pointer = nil-vs-zero discrimination (unknown model → absent, never $0) — same pattern as `Metadata.GetCompactTranscriptStart`. `omitempty` gives back-compat free.
- float64 USD (precedent: `Attribution.AgentPercentage`); ~cent precision documented; backend re-quantizes.
- `CostSource` constants: `reported | estimated | mixed`.
- **Per-model breakdown** `types.ModelUsage {Model string; TokenUsage TokenUsage}` — sibling `Metadata.ModelUsage []ModelUsage` (omitempty). Required: flat scalar can't reconstruct which model cost what.

### Pricing package (new `cmd/entire/cli/pricing/`)

Mirrors `runnerdefaults` embed pattern (`runnerdefaults/embed.go:14`): `//go:embed models/*.json`, leaf package (imports only `agent/types`).

- JSON per provider: `{schema_version, models: [{id, provider, aliases (globs), input_per_mtok, output_per_mtok, cache_read_per_mtok?, cache_write_per_mtok?, effective_date}]}`
- Cache rates optional → default Anthropic multipliers: read 0.1×, write 1.25× of input rate (package constants).
- Lookup: exact id → normalized alias/glob → **miss = no estimate** (no implicit family fallback — mispricing risk).
- Seed: `models/anthropic.json` (Opus 4.8 $5/$25, Fable 5 $10/$50, Sonnet 5 $3/$15, Haiku 4.5 $1/$5 per MTok), best-effort `openai.json`, `google.json`.
- Settings override: `EntireSettings.Pricing *PricingSettings {Models []pricing.ModelRate; DisableEstimation *bool}` (settings/settings.go:63 area, nested-pointer-block convention); user entries replace embedded by id else append; `DisableEstimation` suppresses estimation only, reported cost survives.

### Estimation point: centralized dispatcher, per-model buckets from parsers

New optional capability interface in `agent/agent.go`:

```go
type ModelUsageCalculator interface {
    DeclaredCaps
    CalculateModelUsage(transcriptData []byte, fromOffset int) ([]types.ModelUsage, error)
}
```

Parsers emit per-model token buckets (tokens only; OpenCode also fills reported cost). New `agent.CalculateUsageWithCost(...)` in `agent/token_usage.go` prices each unpriced bucket via `pricing.Estimate`, labels source, folds buckets into the flat `*TokenUsage`. Fallback for non-implementers: single bucket keyed by session `state.ModelName`. Wire at both estimation sites: `lifecycle.go:920-923` (incl. Cursor hook path — price from `event.TokenUsage` + `event.Model`) and `strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:646,930,972`; `config.LoadPricingTable(ctx)` bridges settings→table.

Per-agent model threading (recon-verified):
| Agent | Change |
|---|---|
| pi | model already per-message (`entry.Message.Model`) — bucket in existing loop |
| geminicli | add `Model json:"model"` to `geminiMessageWithTokens` (types.go:108) |
| claudecode | add `Model` to `messageWithUsage` (types.go:96); model rides the max-output dedup struct |
| codex | **new `turn_context` payload struct** (currently ignored, transcript.go:30); interleave in scan: track currentModel, per-snapshot delta attribution; clamp negative delta (counter reset) and re-baseline |
| opencode | add `ModelID json:"modelID"` to `MessageInfo`; sum `Cost` → `CostSource=reported` |
| copilotcli | `session.shutdown ModelMetrics` already keyed by model (transcript.go:216-236) — stop collapsing |
| cursor | hook path: tokens+model arrive together per turn |
| factoryaidroid | session-level sidecar model only → single bucket (acceptable, labeled estimated) |

### PR-sized chunks (CLI)

1. **`pricing` package standalone** — embed, table, lookup, Estimate (+multiplier tests), seed JSONs. Zero wiring.
2. **Cost fields + sum plumbing** — token_usage.go, 3 merge sites (`addCostUSD`/`mergeCostSource` helpers), e2e mirror `e2e/testutil/metadata.go:5-11`. JSON round-trip + back-compat tests (old JSON → nil).
3. **Estimation + parser threading** — 3a dispatcher/wiring + pi/gemini/cursor; 3b claudecode/codex (hardest: turn_context); 3c opencode(reported)/copilot/factorydroid. Mixed-model fixture (opus+fable) asserts split + buckets-sum-to-flat.
4. **Display** — session_tokens.go / checkpoint_tokens.go (`--compare` cost delta) / tokens_profile.go; show only when present, suffix `(estimated)`/`(reported)`/`(mixed)`.
5. **Per-model persistence (fast-follow)** — StepContext.ModelUsage → SessionState.ModelUsage map (checkpoint-scoped reset) → WriteOptions → `Metadata.ModelUsage` + summary merge; vogon e2e.

### Edge cases (CLI)
Unknown model → unpriced bucket, flat = priced sum, source mixed/estimated; multi-session checkpoint mixing reported+estimated → `mixed`; override precedence by id; Codex counter reset clamp; Cursor input already fresh (no double count); `disable_estimation` keeps reported.

## Data contract (CLI → backend, pinned)

Checkpoint `metadata.json` (root `CheckpointSummary.token_usage` AND per-session `Metadata.token_usage`) gains optional fields; absent on old checkpoints, absence = unknown ≠ $0:

```json
"token_usage": { ..., "cost_usd": 0.4231, "cost_source": "estimated" }
"model_usage": [ { "model": "claude-opus-4-8", "token_usage": { "input_tokens": ..., "cost_usd": ..., "cost_source": "..." } } ]
```

`model_usage` uses the CLI's nested-`token_usage` shape (canonical — entire-api ingest structs match it, not a flattened variant). `cost_source` vocab everywhere: `reported | estimated | mixed`.

## Part B — Backend + Web pipeline (entire-api, entire.io)

### Decisions

- **Columns**: `cost_usd NUMERIC(14,6) NULL` + `cost_source TEXT NULL CHECK (... IN ('reported','estimated','mixed'))` on `checkpoints`, `sessions`, `my_activity`. NUMERIC = exact SUM; NULL-able deliberately breaks the `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` token convention (absence ≠ $0). Reads cast `::float8` → `*float64` (same pattern as `attribution_agent_percentage`); no pgtype.Numeric.
- **Per-model breakdown**: rides the existing per-session JSONB (`SessionInfo.ModelUsage`, omitempty) — no new table in v1 (zero aggregations group by model today).
- **Consistent cost rule** for every aggregate surface: SUM ignores NULLs; all-NULL → emit `null` never 0; every sum ships coverage `costed_checkpoints = COUNT(cost_usd)` vs total ("$X across N of M"); scope `cost_source` = single distinct value else `mixed`; averages divide by costed count.
- **BFF**: proxy is byte-shape passthrough (`proxyEntireApiForSession`) → cost fields flow with zero BFF route code. **No PlanetScale fallback cost in v1** — non-flagged cohort sees no-data state; avoids duplicating Go ingest in cache.ts + MySQL migration.

"est" badge when source ≠ reported. All gated behind new `checkpoint-cost` feature flag (PostHog runtime pattern), enabled for the same staff cohort as the entire-api proxy flag.

1. **entire-api PR1 — schema + ingest + write path**: repo migration `027_checkpoint_cost.sql` (checkpoints + sessions cols); `internal/ingest/checkpoint.go` parse cost (tokenUsage struct :62-69) + `model_usage` (nested shape) + `buildCheckpointRow` sum with `hasCost` gate, distinct-source→mixed, root-summary fallback; `store.go` structs + `UpsertCheckpoint`.
2. **entire-api PR2 — read aggregates + panels**: `repo_aggregates.go` Summary/Agents/CheckpointMetrics/AgentActivity/ContributorTokenRows gain `SUM(cost_usd)::float8`, `COUNT(cost_usd)`, source-agg; wire shapes in `teamtypes.go` + handlers in `repos.go` (checkpoint-metrics `avg_cost_per_checkpoint`/`costed_checkpoint_count`/`cost_source`; agent-activity daily `costUsd`/`costedCount`; contributor-tokens `cost_usd` even-split, same divisor as tokens, null-gated).
3. **entire-api PR3 — detail surfaces**: `sessions.go` materialise cost (mirror `hasTokens` gate :476-502); `checkpointapi.go` CheckpointInfo/session token usage/`modelUsage[]`.
4. **entire-api PR4 — me/recap + residency forward** (highest blast radius, last): user migration `007_my_activity_cost.sql` (partitioned parent — verify children inherit); `forwarder/publisher.go` UserActivityEvent +cost (content-free, residency-safe) + **SchemaVersion bump** for mixed-version rollout; consumer → MyActivityRow; recap aggregation null-safe.
5. **entire.io PR5 — FE types + util + flag**: optional cost fields in hand-written `repo-overview/api.ts` types (no SDK regen for panels); `formatCostUSD` + `CostSourceBadge`; `checkpoint-cost` in feature-flags.json.

7. **entire.io PR7 — detail UI**: DetailHeader cost pill; first verify whether detail pages use generated SDK (then widen BFF OpenAPI schema + `openapi:generate` + `api:sdk` regen) or hand-written types.

### Edge cases (pipeline)
All-NULL scope → `null` not 0; real $0 (N>0, sum 0) vs no-data (N=0) distinguished by coverage count; contributor with only uncosted checkpoints → null; root-only cost fallback prevents silent all-null; old checkpoints → omitted fields; two-phase forward: commit-first `my_activity` row null cost, post-hydration re-forward fills (idempotent).

## Codex CLI auth explained

**How it works**: `codex login` runs a browser OAuth flow against OpenAI → writes `~/.codex/auth.json` containing an access token (short-lived), a refresh token (long-lived), and account id. Every CLI/app-server call uses the access token; when it expires, Codex silently exchanges the refresh token for a new one. Usage bills against your ChatGPT plan quota (that's the `rate_limits.plan_type` + weekly `used_percent` we saw in your rollouts). Alternative mode: API-key auth (`OPENAI_API_KEY` / `codex login --api-key`) — bills the API org per token instead, no ChatGPT quota.

**What broke for you**: the task run returned "refresh token was revoked" — OpenAI's server invalidated the refresh token itself, so no new access tokens can be minted. Common causes: password/security change, logout on another device, server-side session rotation, plan change, or the account being re-authed elsewhere. The earlier `/codex:setup` showed "verified" because it read the cached `auth.json` state; the revocation only surfaces when a real API call tries to refresh.

**Fix** (interactive, needs your browser):
```
! codex logout
! codex login
```
(`!` prefix runs it in this session so output lands here.) After that, Codex rescue tasks work again — the shared runtime picks up the new token automatically.

# Make a clean PR

The commit history and PR should read like a careful engineer wrote them for the permanent record. Nothing personal, conversational, or AI-meta belongs in them.

## Never include
- **No Claude / AI session links or footers.** No `Claude-Session:` line, no `https://claude.ai/code/...`, no "Generated with Claude Code", no robot emoji footer, no "Co-Authored-By: Claude".
- **No references to people or conversations.** Never write "Thomas said this", "as X asked", "reply to him", "addressing Y's comment", "per Slack/Discord", "as discussed". The change is justified by what it does, not who mentioned it.
- **No weird meta.** No "I", "let me", "as an AI", no apologies, no narrating the process, no hedging.

## Commits
- Conventional and scoped: `type(scope): imperative summary` (e.g. `fix(auth): reject expired tokens`).
- One logical change per commit. Keep the diff tight, no unrelated formatting churn.
- Body only when it adds value: explain WHAT changed and WHY in plain technical terms.
- **The only way a person's name appears** is a real `Co-authored-by: Name <email>` trailer, used when you actually incorporated their code. That is factual attribution, never "X said in chat". Get a valid email (e.g. GitHub `id+login@users.noreply.github.com`) or skip the trailer.

## Before pushing
- Branch off the latest base. Never commit straight to a protected main.
- Run the repo's format + lint + tests. Confirm green on the committed tree before pushing.

## PR description: use this structure

Title is conventional style, same as the commit (`type(scope): summary`). For the body, fill the sections that apply and drop the ones that don't. Bullets over paragraphs throughout. A small change gets a few bullets, not a wall.

- **Trail** — always FIRST line of the body: the Entire trail link for the branch (`https://entire.io/gh/<owner>/<repo>/trails/<n>`). Get it with `entire trail show` on the branch (or `entire trail list`); if no trail exists, create one with `entire trail create`. Format: `**Trail:** <url>`.
- **What** — one or two lines on what changed. Plain and concrete.
- **Why / how it helps** — the problem it solves and the impact (fixes a bug, unblocks X, cuts Y). The reviewer should get the motivation without asking. Tie it to the outcome, never to who requested it.
- **How** (non-trivial changes) — the approach plus any key decision or tradeoff, and what a reviewer should look at closely.
- **Testing / verification** — exactly what you ran and the result. Be specific:
  - the commands (build, lint, the test suite) and that they passed
  - which cases you covered, including edge cases and the bug's repro
  - any manual checks (what you ran/clicked and what you saw)
  - confirm green on the COMMITTED tree, not an unsaved buffer (`git show HEAD` if unsure)
- **Risk / rollback** (risky changes only) — blast radius and how to revert.
- **Anything else that helps the reviewer:**
  - related issues/PRs, linked by number
  - breaking changes or migration steps, called out clearly
  - screenshots or before/after for UI changes
  - follow-ups intentionally left out of scope

Still no people, no chat references, no AI footer, no filler.

## Example body

> **Trail:** https://entire.io/gh/acme/app/trails/42
>
> **What:** Reject expired tokens in the auth middleware.
>
> **Why / how it helps:** Expired tokens were accepted until the next refresh, so a revoked session kept working for a window. This closes that gap.
>
> **How:** Check `exp` against request time before trusting the claims; return 401 on expiry instead of passing through.
>
> **Testing:**
> - `mise run test` green (added `TestAuth_RejectsExpired`: exp in the past, exactly-now, far future)
> - `mise run lint` 0 issues
> - verified on the committed tree (`git show HEAD`)

## Replying to review comments
- Reply with the technical resolution only ("Fixed in <sha> by ..."). Brief and factual.
- Do not editorialize ("great catch", "you're totally right") or reference the reviewer by what they said in chat. Resolve the thread once addressed.

# Building LLM-Powered Applications with Claude

This skill helps you build LLM-powered applications with Claude. Choose the right surface based on your needs, detect the project language, then read the relevant language-specific documentation.

## Before You Start

Scan the target file (or, if no target file, the prompt and project) for non-Anthropic provider markers — `import openai`, `from openai`, `langchain_openai`, `OpenAI(`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-5`, file names like `agent-openai.py` or `*-generic.py`, or any explicit instruction to keep the code provider-neutral. If you find any, stop and tell the user that this skill produces Claude/Anthropic SDK code; ask whether they want to switch the file to Claude or want a non-Claude implementation. Do not edit a non-Anthropic file with Anthropic SDK calls.

## Output Requirement

When the user asks you to add, modify, or implement a Claude feature, your code must call Claude through one of:

1. **The official Anthropic SDK** for the project's language (`anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `com.anthropic.*`, etc.). This is the default whenever a supported SDK exists for the project.
2. **Raw HTTP** (`curl`, `requests`, `fetch`, `httpx`, etc.) — only when the user explicitly asks for cURL/REST/raw HTTP, the project is a shell/cURL project, or the language has no official SDK.

Never mix the two — don't reach for `requests`/`fetch` in a Python or TypeScript project just because it feels lighter. Never fall back to OpenAI-compatible shims.

**Never guess SDK usage.** Function names, class names, namespaces, method signatures, and import paths must come from explicit documentation — either the `{lang}/` files in this skill or the official SDK repositories or documentation links listed in `shared/live-sources.md`. If the binding you need is not explicitly documented in the skill files, WebFetch the relevant SDK repo from `shared/live-sources.md` before writing code. Do not infer Ruby/Java/Go/PHP/C# APIs from cURL shapes or from another language's SDK.

**If WebFetch or repository access fails** (network restricted, timeouts, clone blocked): do not keep retrying — write code from the patterns and namespace/package tables in the `{lang}/` file, run the compiler or interpreter on it, and iterate on the error output. For statically-typed SDKs (C#, Java, Go) a compile-fix loop against local errors reaches working code faster than blocked network research.

## Defaults

Unless the user requests otherwise:

For the Claude model version, please use Claude Opus 4.8, which you can access via the exact model string `claude-opus-4-8`. Please default to using adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) for anything remotely complicated. And finally, please default to streaming for any request that may involve long input, long output, or high `max_tokens` — it prevents hitting request timeouts. Use the SDK's `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()` helper to get the complete response if you don't need to handle individual stream events

## ⚠️ API Drift — Your Training Prior May Be Stale

Several common Claude API shapes changed in 2025–2026. If you recall a pattern from training, verify it against the `{lang}/` files in this skill before writing — the rows below are the most frequent drift points:

| Area | Stale prior | Current API |
|---|---|---|
| Extended thinking | `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | On Claude 4.6+ models: `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`. `budget_tokens` is deprecated on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and **rejected with a 400** on Fable 5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 4.8 / 4.7. Pre-4.6 models still use `budget_tokens`. |
| Web search / web fetch tool type | `web_search_20250305`, `web_fetch_20250910` | `web_search_20260209`, `web_fetch_20260209` (dynamic filtering) on Opus 4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6. Older models keep the basic variants; on Vertex AI only basic `web_search_20250305` is available (web fetch is not on Vertex) — see the Server Tools QR below. |
| PHP parameter names | snake_case wire names as named args (`max_tokens`) | Top-level named args are camelCase (`maxTokens`). Nested array keys vary by feature (e.g. `'taskBudget'`, `'skillID'`, `'mcp_server_name'`) — copy the exact key from the documented example; do not bulk-convert. |
| Managed Agents credentials | Keep secrets host-side via custom tools (the only option before vaults shipped) | Vault `environment_variable` credentials — stored by Anthropic, substituted at egress, never visible in the sandbox (`shared/managed-agents-tools.md` → Vaults). Host-side custom tools remain the fallback for self-hosted sandboxes. |

The `{lang}/` files in this skill are authoritative over recalled patterns.

---

## Subcommands

If the User Request at the bottom of this prompt is a bare subcommand string (no prose), search every **Subcommands** table in this document — including any in sections appended below — and follow the matching Action column directly. This lets users invoke specific flows via `/claude-api <subcommand>`. If no table in the document matches, treat the request as normal prose.

Do not summarize the guide — execute it. If the user did not name a target model, ask which model to migrate to in the same turn as the scope question. |

## Language Detection

Before reading code examples, determine which language the user is working in:

1. **Look at project files** to infer the language:

   - `*.py`, `requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `Pipfile` → **Python** — read from `python/`
   - `*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` → **TypeScript** — read from `typescript/`
   - `*.js`, `*.jsx` (no `.ts` files present) → **TypeScript** — JS uses the same SDK, read from `typescript/`
   - `*.java`, `pom.xml`, `build.gradle` → **Java** — read from `java/`
   - `*.kt`, `*.kts`, `build.gradle.kts` → **Java** — Kotlin uses the Java SDK, read from `java/`
   - `*.scala`, `build.sbt` → **Java** — Scala uses the Java SDK, read from `java/`
   - `*.go`, `go.mod` → **Go** — read from `go/`

2. **If multiple languages detected** (e.g., both Python and TypeScript files):

   - Check which language the user's current file or question relates to

3. **If language can't be inferred** (empty project, no source files, or unsupported language):

   - If AskUserQuestion is unavailable, default to Python examples and note: "Showing Python examples. Let me know if you need a different language."

4. **If unsupported language detected** (Rust, Swift, C++, Elixir, etc.):

   - Suggest cURL/raw HTTP examples from `curl/` and note that community SDKs may exist
   - Offer to show Python or TypeScript examples as reference implementations

5. **If user needs cURL/raw HTTP examples**, read from `curl/`.

### Language-Specific Feature Support

Every SDK language above supports both the beta Tool Runner and Managed Agents (beta) — Python (`@beta_tool` decorator), TypeScript (`betaZodTool` + Zod), Java (annotated classes), Go (`BetaToolRunner` in the `toolrunner` pkg), Ruby (`BaseTool` + `tool_runner`), C# (`BetaToolRunner` + raw JSON schema), PHP (`BetaRunnableTool` + `toolRunner()`); code entry points are in the Tool Use Patterns quick reference below. cURL is raw HTTP (no SDK features) and supports Managed Agents.

> **Managed Agents code examples**: see the reading guide in the `## Managed Agents (Beta)` section below.

---

## Which Surface Should I Use?

> **Start simple.** Default to the simplest tier that meets your needs. Single API calls and workflows handle most use cases — only reach for agents when the task genuinely requires open-ended, model-driven exploration. "Simplest" means the least code you own: for a hosted, scheduled, or memory-backed agent, Managed Agents is usually the simplest option (no loop code, no state files, no scheduler), even though it's a bigger platform.

| Use Case                                        | Tier            | Recommended Surface       | Why                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Classification, summarization, extraction, Q&A  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | One request, one response                                    |
| Batch processing or embeddings                  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | Specialized endpoints                                        |
| Multi-step pipelines with code-controlled logic | Workflow        | **Claude API + tool use** | You orchestrate the loop                                     |
| Custom agent with your own tools                | Agent           | **Claude API + tool use** | Maximum flexibility                                          |
| Server-managed stateful agent with workspace    | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Anthropic runs the loop and hosts the tool-execution sandbox |
| Persisted, versioned agent configs              | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Agents are stored objects; sessions pin to a version         |
| Long-running multi-turn agent with file mounts  | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Per-session containers, SSE event stream, Skills + MCP       |
| Agent that runs on a schedule (cron, "every night") | Agent       | **Managed Agents** — scheduled deployments | Deployments fire sessions autonomously; no client-side scheduler |

> **Note:** Managed Agents is the right choice when you want Anthropic to run the agent loop *and* host the container where tools execute — file ops, bash, code execution all run in the per-session workspace. If you want to host the compute yourself or run your own custom tool runtime, Claude API + tool use is the right choice — use the tool runner for the agentic loop — its per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, logging, error interception, and conditional execution (see `shared/tool-use-concepts.md`) — or the manual loop when you want to own the entire loop yourself.

> **Cloud-provider access.** **Claude Platform on AWS** is Anthropic-operated with same-day API parity — see `shared/claude-platform-on-aws.md` for client setup. For per-feature availability on **Claude Platform on AWS**, **Amazon Bedrock**, **Google Vertex AI**, and **Microsoft Foundry**, see `shared/platform-availability.md` — that table is the single source of truth in this skill; do not infer availability from anywhere else.

### Building an Agent: Four Approaches

Once you've decided you actually need an agent (open-ended, model-driven tool use), there are four distinct ways to build one. Two independent questions separate them: **who supplies the harness** (the agent loop + context management) and **who supplies the deployment** (the infra the agent runs on). The Tool Runner and the Claude Agent SDK both supply a *harness only* — you still host and deploy them yourself — which is why they're easy to conflate. Managed Agents (CMA) is the only option that supplies **both** the harness *and* managed deployment; the manual loop supplies neither.

| # | Approach | You write | Harness & deployment | Tools available | Use when |
|---|----------|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|----------|
| 1 | **Claude API — manual loop** | The `while stop_reason == "tool_use"` loop yourself | You build the harness; you host | Only tools you define | You want to own the *entire* loop — no beta dependency, or a control flow the Tool Runner's per-turn hooks don't fit |
| 2 | **Claude API — Tool Runner** (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner` + `@beta_tool` / `betaZodTool`) | Just the tool functions | SDK supplies the loop (**harness only**); you host | Only tools you define | A custom-tool agent without hand-writing the loop (most cases). Per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, error interception, result modification (e.g. `cache_control`), retries, streaming, and compaction |
| 3 | **Managed Agents** (REST, beta) | Agent config + your tool results | Anthropic supplies the harness **and** hosts a per-session sandbox (**harness + deployment**) | Anthropic-hosted sandbox (bash, files, code exec) + Skills/MCP + your tools | You want Anthropic to run the loop *and* host the per-session workspace; persisted/versioned configs; long-running sessions |
| 4 | **Claude Agent SDK** — *separate product* (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) | A prompt + options | SDK supplies the Claude Code harness + built-in tools (**harness only**); you host | Built-in Read/Write/Edit/Bash/Glob/Grep/WebSearch/WebFetch + MCP + subagents | You want a batteries-included coding/filesystem agent running on your own infra |

The harness/deployment split is the key mental model: options 1, 2, and 4 all **leave deployment to you**; only option 3 (CMA) adds managed deployment. Options 1–3 are what this skill generates; option 4 is a different library with its own docs — see the disambiguation below.

> **Tool Runner ≠ Claude Agent SDK.** These sound alike but are different packages:
> - **Tool Runner** is part of the regular Anthropic API SDK (`anthropic` / `@anthropic-ai/sdk`), reached via `client.beta.messages.tool_runner`. It automates the request → execute → loop cycle *for tools you define*. No built-in tools, no filesystem access, no sandbox — you supply every tool and host the compute. It is option 2 above, a thin helper over `POST /v1/messages`.
> - **Claude Agent SDK** (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) is Claude Code packaged as a library. It ships built-in tools (file read/write/edit, bash, grep, web search), the full agent loop, context management, hooks, subagents, permissions, and sessions. You call `query(prompt, options)` and it drives everything.
>
> Both are **harness-only — you host and deploy them.** The difference is scope of harness: the Tool Runner loops over tools *you* define (with per-turn hooks for approval, interception, result modification, and retries — but no built-in tools); the Agent SDK is the full Claude Code harness with built-in tools. Neither provides managed deployment — that's what **Managed Agents (CMA)** adds (Anthropic hosts the loop and a per-session sandbox).
>
> **This skill covers the Claude API and Managed Agents (options 1–3); it does not generate Claude Agent SDK code.** If the user actually wants the Claude Agent SDK, point them to its docs (`code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk`) — don't substitute the API Tool Runner for it, or vice-versa.

### Should I Build an Agent?

Before choosing the agent tier, check all four criteria:

- **Complexity** — Is the task multi-step and hard to fully specify in advance? (e.g., "turn this design doc into a PR" vs. "extract the title from this PDF")
- **Value** — Does the outcome justify higher cost and latency?
- **Viability** — Is Claude capable at this task type?
- **Cost of error** — Can errors be caught and recovered from? (tests, review, rollback)

If the answer is "no" to any of these, stay at a simpler tier (single call or workflow).

## Architecture

Everything goes through `POST /v1/messages`. Tools and output constraints are features of this single endpoint — not separate APIs.

**User-defined tools** — You define tools (via decorators, Zod schemas, or raw JSON), and the SDK's tool runner handles calling the API, executing your functions, and looping until Claude is done. For full control, you can write the loop manually.

**Server-side tools** — Anthropic-hosted tools that run on Anthropic's infrastructure. Code execution is fully server-side (declare it in `tools`, Claude runs code automatically). Computer use can be server-hosted or self-hosted.

**Structured outputs** — Constrains the Messages API response format (`output_config.format`) and/or tool parameter validation (`strict: true`). The recommended approach is `client.messages.parse()` which validates responses against your schema automatically. Note: the old `output_format` parameter is deprecated; use `output_config: {format: {...}}` on `messages.create()`.

**Supporting endpoints** — Batches (`POST /v1/messages/batches`), Files (`POST /v1/files`), Token Counting (`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` — see `shared/token-counting.md`), and Models (`GET /v1/models`, `GET /v1/models/{id}` — live capability/context-window discovery) feed into or support Messages API requests.
