content.text:
Foundry changes my assessment materially — and it's the *right* call for the reason I flagged. Verified against Microsoft's own catalog:

## The privacy blocker is solved (why Foundry is correct)

DeepSeek V4 Flash [is on Foundry](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/azure-ai-foundry-blog/introducing-deepseek-v4-flash-and-v4-pro-in-microsoft-foundry/4515174) (added May 2026). "Models sold by Azure" **process prompts/responses in your customer-specified geography** — EU data zones are Sweden Central / Germany West Central, US zones are listed. So transcript content stays on **Azure infra in-region, never DeepSeek's China API**. That's exactly the residency concern I raised, resolved — provided you deploy **regional or DataZone, not Global** (Global can process anywhere the model's deployed). Two caveats to check: match the deployment geos to Entire's jurisdiction cells (EU/US are covered; **verify AU/SG have a DeepSeek data zone** — they may not), and the catalog shows a **deprecation date of 8/20/2026** on the current listing, so confirm you're pinning a supported version.

## But the code change is now *bigger*, not smaller

The direct-DeepSeek shortcut I mentioned (point `anthropic-sdk-go` at `/anthropic`) **does not apply on Foundry.** Foundry serves DeepSeek as **OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions** (`v1/chat/completions`, vLLM-backed) — no Anthropic Messages endpoint. So both call sites (`checkpointanalysis/model.go`, `sessionname/sessionname.go`) that use `anthropic.MessageNewParams` must be **rewritten onto an OpenAI-compatible Go client** (or the Azure AI Inference SDK). That client swap is the actual "huge change" — not a base-URL flip.

## Tool calling: genuinely a non-issue

Two independent reasons it doesn't matter:
1. **Your workload doesn't use it** — checkpoint analysis is text→JSON→`Unmarshal`, zero tools.
2. Even if you wanted it: [Microsoft Learn lists DeepSeek-V4-Flash on Azure as **not supporting tool calling**](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-sold-directly-by-azure) (conflicts with the base model's own capability — the vLLM serving likely doesn't expose it). So don't build on Foundry tool calls. For structured output use **OpenAI JSON mode** (`response_format: json_object`, or json_schema) instead — that's supported and is the right replacement for your JSON-blob prompt.

## The two concrete migration gotchas

- **Session-naming's prefill breaks.** It relies on Anthropic assistant prefill (`"{"`, `sessionname.go:34`) to force JSON. OpenAI-format has no prefill — replace it with `response_format: {type: "json_object"}` (or json_schema for the `{name}` shape). This is a behavior change, must live-test.
- **Error classification breaks.** The cap-park logic string-matches `"usage limit"` in Anthropic's 400 body (`model.go:111-131`). Azure/Foundry returns different error shapes (429s, Azure error envelopes) — re-map these or jobs nak-loop instead of parking/backing off.

## Net

Foundry is the right vehicle (solves residency), but budget it as a **provider-client migration**: OpenAI-compat client, JSON-mode replacing prefill, Azure error re-mapping, and a quality A/B (does V4-Flash hold the 18-label vocab + section JSON as well as sonnet — your defensive parsing cushions failures but not quality). Tool calling is off the table and doesn't need to be on it.

The safe first step is still the same regardless: **make model + endpoint + provider configurable** (hardcoded consts today) and **split the two consumers' keys/config** so you migrate analysis and session-naming independently and A/B via env, not a redeploy. Want me to scope that refactor as a branch — an OpenAI-compat client seam behind the existing interface, both call sites configurable, no provider decision baked in? I'll leave the actual Foundry cutover to you.

Victor's mostly right, and it's worth conceding the big points cleanly rather than defending #1725 as-is.

**Where he's dead right:**
- **`confirmed := false` is the real fix** — all three PRs agree. Everything else is packaging.
- **The flag redesign is genuinely better.** The current set has double-negatives and murky interactions (`--init-repo`/`--no-init-repo`/`--no-github`/`--skip-initial-commit`). His `--bootstrap=prompt|local|github|off` enum + `--commit-existing-files` models the actual decision tree in one axis. That's cleaner UX and cleaner code.
- **His safety primitive beats ours.** Our #1725 walks the folder, tallies files/MB, and shows the user a size summary to confirm against. Victor's model — **default to an empty initial commit, never stage/push existing files unless `--commit-existing-files`** — makes that whole apparatus unnecessary. If you commit nothing by default, you don't need to tell the user what you're about to commit. That's a stronger, simpler guarantee: safe-by-default instead of informed-consent-against-a-computed-summary.

**Worth being candid about:** the fix-until-zero audit rounds *amplified* exactly the complexity he's reacting to — each pass hardened the folder walker (fail-safe truncation, dir-vs-entry budget, unreadable-dir handling). That hardening was real and correct *given* the walk-and-confirm design — but Victor's point is that the design itself is the wrong primitive, so all that hardening is solving a problem we created. He's right.

**What to keep from #1725 regardless of the flag shape** — small, orthogonal to his redesign, fold them in:

| Keep | Why |
|---|---|
| Default-NO confirm | the agreed core |
| No-network-before-consent ordering | don't run `gh auth status` before the user consents to init (audit-caught) |
| Visibility-truthful plan text | don't print "PRIVATE" when `--repo-visibility public` was passed |
| `--yes` scope-bounding | `local+--yes` must never touch GitHub — his table already has this, good |

**Concede to Victor:** the workspace-root / nested-repo hard-stop and the whole `inspectBootstrapDir` walker can go. Under his default-empty-commit model the leak vector largely closes on its own (you're not committing or pushing user content, nested repos included, unless they opt in). If anyone still wants a nested-`.git` guard, it's a cheap separate check — not the 50k-entry budgeted walker — and arguably its own issue.

**The actual action is consolidation, not more code.** Three PRs on one issue is the real problem. Pick Victor's design as the base, fold in the four keepers above, one owner, close the other two. Given he's done the design thinking and it's better, I'd hand him the lead and offer #1725's audited bits as a diff to graft in.

Want me to draft the thread reply (concede the walker, back the `--bootstrap` enum, list the four keepers as graftable commits from #1725), or scope the consolidated implementation so whoever owns it has the plan? I'd not just silently keep #1725 open in parallel — that's the duplication he's flagging.

Here's the exact blast radius.

**The issue:** [#1717](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/1717) — enable in a non-repo dir creates+pushes a GitHub repo without confirmation.

**The two duplicate PRs (the actual consolidation target):**
| PR | Author | Title | Closes #1717? |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#1720](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1720) | @computermode | fix(enable): confirm before init/create/push in a non-repo directory | ❌ no closing link |
| [#1725](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1725) | app/entire (ours) | fix(enable): require explicit confirmation before creating a repository | ✅ closes #1717 |

Both touch the same `entire enable` bootstrap path, both flip `confirmed := false`, both add push-prevention on top. That's the duplication Victor's calling out.

**Victor himself has no competing PR open.** His open PRs (#1703, #1681, #1063, #1007) are unrelated — the "another one I created" he mentions isn't in the open list, so he's acting as reviewer/designer here, not a third code owner. Good — it means the fork is just **#1720 vs #1725**, with Victor proposing the redesign to reconcile them.

**Adjacent PRs on the same `entire enable` surface — NOT dupes, but a `--bootstrap` flag redesign will collide with them, so coordinate (don't close):**
- [#1172](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1172) @evisdren — checkpoint sync destination picker + public-repo warning on enable (closest in spirit — also a confirmation-UX change)
- [#1618](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1618) @peyton-alt — guided setup ladder (enable onboarding)
- our own [#1713](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1713) / [#1714](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1714) / [#1719](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1719) — touch `setup.go`/enable paths for other fixes; a flag overhaul rebases over them

**So the decision is narrow:** pick one of #1720 / #1725 as the base (Victor's redesign favors the simpler primitive, which leans toward reworking rather than either as-is), fold the four keepers from #1725 (default-NO, no-network-before-consent, visibility-truthful plan, `--yes` scoping) into it, close the other, and land the `--bootstrap` enum coordinating with #1172 since it's the neighbor most likely to conflict.

Issue #1717: `entire enable` in a non-repository directory creates and pushes a GitHub repository without confirmation.

## The redesign to implement (replaces the current #1725 approach)

Current #1725 flips `confirmed := false` (keep) but also added a heavy folder walker (`inspectBootstrapDir`: file/dir counting, MB via humanBytes, workspace-root nested-repo hard-stop, fail-safe truncation) to show the user a size summary before confirming. Reviewer feedback: that primitive is wrong — replace "walk-and-show-size-then-confirm" with a **safe-by-default** model where nothing user-content is committed/pushed unless explicitly opted in, which makes the walker unnecessary.

**New flag model (single decision axis + content opt-in):**
- `--bootstrap` (string enum, default `prompt`): behavior in a non-git directory.
  - `prompt` — ask interactively (default-NO on every confirmation).
  - `local` — git init only, no GitHub.
  - `github` — git init + create GitHub repo + add origin (+ push per --commit-existing-files).
  - `off` — exit with a clear error, do nothing.
- `--commit-existing-files` (bool, default **false**): stage, commit, and (with bootstrap=github) push the files already in the directory. **Default = empty initial commit, existing files left unstaged/uncommitted/unpushed.** This is the core safety primitive.
- `--initial-commit-message` (string): message for the initial commit. **Requires --commit-existing-files** — hard error if set without it ("--initial-commit-message requires --commit-existing-files").
- `--repo-name` / `--repo-owner` / `--repo-visibility` (strings): valid only with bootstrap=github; **hard error** if set with local/off. Defaults: repo-name→dir basename, repo-owner→gh login, repo-visibility→private.
- `--yes`/`-y` (bool, default false): skip prompts, accept the selected mode's defaults. **Scope-bounded**: local+--yes NEVER touches GitHub; github+--yes accepts private/name/owner defaults; committing content STILL requires --commit-existing-files (--yes alone never commits/pushes existing files).

## KEEP these four hardening bits from current #1725 (fold into the new model, they're orthogonal):
1. Default-NO on every interactive confirmation (the confirmed:=false core).
2. No-network-before-consent: do NOT run the gh availability/auth probe (`gh auth status`) until AFTER the user consents to bootstrap=github AND init — a declined/local/off path makes ZERO gh/network calls.
3. Visibility-truthful plan text: any confirmation/plan text states the ACTUAL resolved visibility (public/private/internal), never a hardcoded "PRIVATE" when --repo-visibility overrides it.
4. --yes scope-bounding (in the model above).

## DROP from current #1725:
- The entire `inspectBootstrapDir` folder walker and everything it fed: file/dir counting, humanBytes/MB display, the workspace-root nested-repo hard-stop, scanTruncated/fail-safe-truncation, dir-vs-entry budget, unreadable-dir handling, plannedAdjustableFields size logic. Under safe-by-default (empty commit, no existing files pushed) the leak vector closes without it. Remove the code AND its tests (TestInspectBootstrapDir*, workspace-root tests, file-cap tests, etc.). If there's a CHEAP pre-existing guard worth keeping (e.g. refuse to git init if cwd already contains a .git — check if that's existing behavior), keep only that; do NOT reintroduce a walker.

## Back-compat — CRITICAL, determine from the actual code:
The CLI is a released product (v0.8.1). BEFORE changing flags, determine which flags ALREADY SHIP on origin/main (pre-#1725) vs which #1725/#1720 added. `git log origin/main -- cmd/entire/cli/setup*.go` and inspect origin/main's `entire enable` flag set. Mapping: --no-init-repo→--bootstrap=off; --init-repo (non-interactive local init)→--bootstrap=local (or github if it currently proceeds to GitHub — VERIFY the current semantics before mapping); --no-github→--bootstrap=local; --skip-initial-commit (default) ↔ --commit-existing-files=false (the new default, so --skip-initial-commit becomes a no-op alias / deprecated). Preserve behavior for existing scripts.
- For flags that #1725 itself ADDED (never released): free to replace, no deprecation needed.
- If CLAUDE.md / repo posture says pre-production rename-freely for this surface, you may hard-replace with a clear migration note — but default to deprecation-aliases since enable is user-facing and released. State which you chose and why.

## Security invariant (must hold, mutation-verify):
No code path creates or pushes a GitHub repo, and no existing user file is committed/pushed, without EITHER an explicit non-defaulted human yes OR an explicit opt-in (--bootstrap=github for creation, --commit-existing-files for content). Enumerate every create/push/commit-existing call site and prove each is gated.

## Live verification matrix (built binary + a `gh` shim that logs/fails loudly on `repo create` — do NOT create real GitHub repos; use non-interactive refuse paths + shim for the create paths):
- default (bootstrap=prompt) interactive, EOF/decline → no init, no repo, no push, 0 gh calls.
- bootstrap=off → exits, nothing done, 0 gh calls.
- bootstrap=local (or --yes) → git init, EMPTY initial commit, existing files NOT staged/committed, no GitHub, 0 gh calls.

Local HEAD = remote = `aff7f6e623d8076f329a7a10afa40b4d74f59d82`, a single clean commit on top of current `origin/main` (`b29d739c0`).

### Final flag model (as implemented)
- `--bootstrap` (enum, default `prompt`): `prompt` (ask; every confirm defaults NO), `local` (git init only), `github` (init + create repo + push), `off` (exit).
- `--commit-existing-files` (bool, default **false**): the core safety primitive. Default → **empty initial commit**, existing files left untracked/uncommitted/unpushed.
- `--initial-commit-message` (string): **requires** `--commit-existing-files` (hard error otherwise).
- `--repo-name` / `--repo-owner` / `--repo-visibility`: valid only with `--bootstrap=github` (hard error with `local`/`off`).
- `--yes`: scope-bounded — alone resolves to a **local** init (never GitHub); GitHub still needs `--bootstrap=github` or a `--repo-*` flag; content still needs `--commit-existing-files`.

### Back-compat mapping + deprecation decision
All 8 bootstrap flags **ship in released v0.8.1 and v0.8.42** (verified via `git show <tag>`), so I kept them as **deprecated aliases** (not hard-replaced), via cobra `MarkDeprecated` (hidden from help, prints a one-line hint):

| Deprecated (released) | Maps to | Verified released semantics |
|---|---|---|
| `--init-repo` | `--bootstrap=local` | help text promised only local init; GitHub-on-`--init-repo` was itself part of the surprise. Mapped to `local` (safety + documented meaning). |
| `--no-init-repo` | `--bootstrap=off` | exact (exit/decline). |
| `--no-github` | local (GitHub suppressed) | preserves prompt-then-local / non-interactive-decline. |
| `--skip-initial-commit` | no-op | matches the new empty-commit default. |

Intentional, security-motivated behavior changes (documented in PR/commit): the initial commit no longer includes existing files by default; `--yes` alone no longer creates a GitHub repo.

### Security-invariant proof (every create/push/commit-existing site gated)
Single funnel `runGitHubBootstrapInit → resolveBootstrapDecision → git init → post-consent gh probe → useGitHub gate → finalize`:
- `gitInit`: gated by `proceed` (explicit mode, `--yes`, or a default-NO confirm the user actively accepted).
- `ghRepoCreate` + `git push`: gated by `useGitHub`, true only via `--bootstrap=github`, a `--repo-*` flag, or an interactive default-NO "yes" — never on prompt-non-interactive/local/off.
- `git add -A` (staging existing files): only when `commitFiles == opts.CommitExistingFiles`; nothing else can set it. The default commit is `git commit --allow-empty` with no `git add`.
- gh probe (`gh --version`/`gh auth status`) runs only after init consent and only when GitHub is intended; local identity sourcing passes `allowGH=false` so `local` makes zero gh calls.

### Live verification matrix (built binary + `gh` shim; no real GitHub repos)
All rows confirmed with terminal evidence:
- default non-interactive → declines, no init, **0 gh calls**.

- `--bootstrap=github --commit-existing-files --yes` → files staged, committed, **pushed** (tree includes files).
- `--repo-name X --yes` (no `--bootstrap`) → repo created (gh-flag intent honored under `--yes`).

- existing git repo → normal enable, bootstrap section absent.

import json, glob, datetime as dt, collections
root="/Users/suhaan/.claude/projects/-Users-suhaan-devenv"
now=dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc)
cutoff=now-dt.timedelta(hours=3)

R={"claude-fable-5":(10,50,1.0,12.5),"claude-mythos-5":(10,50,1.0,12.5),
   "claude-opus-4":(5,25,0.5,6.25),"claude-sonnet-5":(3,15,0.3,3.75),
   "claude-sonnet-4":(3,15,0.3,3.75),"claude-haiku-4":(1,5,0.1,1.25),"claude-haiku-3":(0.8,4,0.08,1.0)}
def rate(m):
    if not m: return None
    for k,v in R.items():
        if m.startswith(k): return v
    return None
agg=collections.defaultdict(lambda:[0,0,0,0,0]) # in,out,cc,cr,calls
seen=lines=bad=0
files=glob.glob(root+"/**/*.jsonl",recursive=True)
for f in files:

    for ln in fh:
        ln=ln.strip()
        if not ln or ln[0]!="{": continue
        lines+=1
        try: d=json.loads(ln)
        except Exception: bad+=1; continue
        ts=d.get("timestamp")
        if not ts: continue
        try: t=dt.datetime.fromisoformat(ts.replace("Z","+00:00"))
        except Exception: continue
        if t<cutoff: continue
        msg=d.get("message")
        if not isinstance(msg,dict): continue
        u=msg.get("usage")

        m=msg.get("model") or d.get("model") or "unknown"
        i=u.get("input_tokens",0) or 0
        o=u.get("output_tokens",0) or 0
        cc=u.get("cache_creation_input_tokens",0) or 0
        cr=u.get("cache_read_input_tokens",0) or 0
        if i+o+cc+cr==0: continue
        a=agg[m]; a[0]+=i;a[1]+=o;a[2]+=cc;a[3]+=cr;a[4]+=1; seen+=1
    fh.close()
print(f"window: {cutoff:%Y-%m-%d %H:%M}Z -> {now:%H:%M}Z (3h) | files={len(files)} lines={lines} bad={bad} usage_rows={seen}\n")
tot_in=tot_out=tot_cc=tot_cr=tot_cost=tot_calls=0

print(hdr); print("-"*len(hdr))
for m in sorted(agg, key=lambda k:-sum(agg[k][:4])):
    i,o,cc,cr,c=agg[m]; r=rate(m)
    cost=(i*r[0]+o*r[1]+cr*r[2]+cc*r[3])/1e6 if r else None
    cs=f"{cost:9.2f}" if cost is not None else "     n/a "
    print(f"{m:28} {c:>6} {i:>12,} {o:>11,} {cc:>12,} {cr:>13,} {cs}")
    tot_in+=i;tot_out+=o;tot_cc+=cc;tot_cr+=cr;tot_calls+=c

print("-"*len(hdr))

{"baseRefName":"main","body":"**Trail:** https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/832

## What

Make the `entire enable` bootstrap flow (running in a directory that is not yet a Git repository) safe-by-default: nothing is created on GitHub and no file already in the directory is committed or pushed unless the user explicitly opts in. Model the behavior as a single `--bootstrap` mode plus a content opt-in, replacing the ad-hoc flag set and the confirmation-by-directory-walk primitive.

## Why

`entire enable` run from a non-git directory would `git init` → `git add -A` → commit → create a **private** GitHub repo named after the directory → push, with the interactive confirmations defaulting to **YES**. A bare Enter (or EOF on stdin while a controlling TTY was present) auto-accepted every step, so a single mistyped directory could publish its contents to a brand-new remote before the mistake was noticed. Reported in #1717.

## The new flag model

| Flag | Type / default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--bootstrap` | enum, default `prompt` | Behavior in a non-git dir: `prompt` (ask; every confirmation defaults to NO), `local` (git init only), `github` (git init + create GitHub repo + push), `off` (exit, do nothing). |
| `--commit-existing-files` | bool, default `false` | Stage, commit, and (with `github`) push the files already in the directory. **Default = empty initial commit; existing files left untracked / uncommitted / unpushed.** The core safety primitive. |
| `--initial-commit-message` | string | Message for the initial commit. **Requires `--commit-existing-files`** (hard error otherwise). |
| `--repo-name` / `--repo-owner` / `--repo-visibility` | string | Configure the new GitHub repo; **valid only with `--bootstrap=github`** (hard error with `local`/`off`). Defaults: dir basename / gh login / private. |
| `--yes` / `-y` | bool, default `false` | Skip prompts, accept the mode's defaults. **Scope-bounded:** on its own it resolves to a local init (never GitHub); GitHub creation still requires `--bootstrap=github` or a `--repo-*` flag, and committing existing files still requires `--commit-existing-files`. |

## Safe-by-default rationale

The content-leak vector is closed **by construction**: the initial commit is empty unless `--commit-existing-files` is given, so no user-authored file can be staged/committed/pushed without an explicit opt-in, and no GitHub repo is created without `--bootstrap=github` (or a `--repo-*` flag, or an interactive default-NO "yes"). That makes the earlier "walk the directory, tally file count + size, detect nested repos, then confirm" primitive unnecessary — there is nothing to tally when nothing is committed by default — so that whole subsystem (folder walker, byte-size display, workspace-root hard-stop, fail-safe truncation, and their tests) is removed.

## Kept from the earlier fix (folded into the new model)

1. **Default-NO** on every interactive confirmation.
2. **No network before consent:** the `gh` availability/auth probe runs only after the user consents to `git init`, and only when a GitHub repo is intended — a declined/local/off run makes zero `gh`/network calls.
3. **Truthful visibility:** confirmation/plan text states the actual resolved visibility (public/private/internal), never a hardcoded "PRIVATE".
4. **`--yes` scope-bounding** as described in the table above.

## Security invariant

No path creates or pushes a GitHub repo, and no existing file is committed/pushed, without either an explicit non-defaulted human "yes" or an explicit opt-in (`--bootstrap=github` for creation, `--commit-existing-files` for content). Single funnel: `runGitHubBootstrapInit` → `resolveBootstrapDecision` (decides proceed + GitHub intent; no side effect, no network) → `git init` → post-consent `gh` probe → `useGitHub` gate → finalize → `doInitialCommit` (stages only when `commitFiles`) + `ghRepoCreate`. Every create/push/stage site is gated on those two booleans, each reachable only via an explicit opt-in.

## Back-compat

The bootstrap flags shipped in released versions (v0.8.1 / v0.8.42), so the pre-existing flags are retained as **deprecated aliases** mapped onto the new model, each printing cobra's one-line deprecation hint and hidden from `--help`:

| Deprecated flag | Maps to |
|---|---|
| `--init-repo` | `--bootstrap=local` |
| `--no-init-repo` | `--bootstrap=off` |
| `--no-github` | local (GitHub suppressed) |
| `--skip-initial-commit` | no-op (matches the new empty-commit default) |

`--repo-*` and `--initial-commit-message` keep their names (now scoped as above). Existing scripts keep working; the intentional, security-motivated behavior changes are that the initial commit no longer includes existing files by default (add `--commit-existing-files` to restore that) and `--yes` alone no longer creates a GitHub repo (use `--bootstrap=github` or a `--repo-*` flag).

## Testing

Unit + integration (all green, incl. `-race`); `golangci-lint` 0 issues; `gofmt` clean. The three security-critical guards are mutation-verified (revert guard → test fails → restore): default-NO confirm, no-create-without-opt-in, no-existing-files-without-`--commit-existing-files`.

### Live verification (built binary, `gh` shim logging every call and simulating creation against a local bare remote — no real GitHub side effects)

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| default (`prompt`) non-interactive | refuses; no init, 0 gh calls |
| `--bootstrap=off` | exits; nothing done, 0 gh calls |
| interactive, decline init (EOF) | refuses with 0 gh calls, no git init |
| `--bootstrap=local` / bare `--yes` | git init, **empty** initial commit, existing files untracked, 0 gh calls |
| `--bootstrap=local --commit-existing-files` | existing files committed locally, 0 gh calls |
| `--bootstrap=github --yes --repo-name X` (shim) | repo created, **empty** commit pushed — existing files NOT pushed |
| `--bootstrap=github --commit-existing-files --yes` (shim) | existing files staged, committed, pushed |
| `--repo-name X --yes` (no `--bootstrap`) | repo created (gh-flag intent honored under `--yes`) |
| `--initial-commit-message` without `--commit-existing-files` | hard error, nothing done |
| `--repo-name` with `--bootstrap=local` | hard error |
| `--repo-visibility public` (interactive) | plan reads "Create a new **PUBLIC** repository …" |
| deprecated `--init-repo` / `--no-init-repo` / `--no-github` | still work, map correctly, print a deprecation hint |
| existing git repo | normal enable; bootstrap not triggered |

`gh repo create` was never invoked in any refusal scenario, and no `gh`/network call was made before init consent on any path.

| Flag | Type / default | Meaning |

**Trail:** https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/847

## What

Model `entire enable`'s non-git-directory bootstrap as a single `--bootstrap` mode plus a content opt-in, replacing the ad-hoc flag set (`--init-repo` / `--no-init-repo` / `--no-github` / `--push`). The initial commit is now **empty by default** — files already in the directory are staged, committed, or pushed only when the user explicitly opts in with `--commit-existing-files`.

## Why / how it helps

The confirmation gap from #1717 (a non-repo `entire enable` could `git init` → create a **private** GitHub repo → push, with prompts defaulting to YES) was already closed on `main` by #1720 (default-NO prompts, explicit GitHub create, explicit push). This PR builds on that in two ways:

- **One mental model instead of four flags.** `--bootstrap=prompt|local|github|off` says exactly what happens in a non-git directory; the four legacy booleans become hidden deprecated aliases.
- **Existing files are never staged without consent — by construction.** `main` still runs `git add -A` for the initial commit by default, so a stray `entire enable` in the wrong directory still commits that directory's contents locally (and pushes them if a remote was created). The new default records an empty `--allow-empty` commit and leaves every pre-existing file untracked; `--commit-existing-files` is the single, explicit switch that opts into committing/pushing them.

This is a refactor + hardening, not a bug fix — #1717 is already resolved on `main`.

## The new flag model

| Flag | Type / default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--bootstrap` | enum, default `prompt` | Behavior in a non-git dir: `prompt` (ask; every confirmation defaults to **NO**; non-interactive declines unless `--yes`), `local` (git init only), `github` (git init + create GitHub repo + push), `off` (exit, do nothing). |
| `--commit-existing-files` | bool, default `false` | Stage, commit, and (with `github`) push the files already in the directory. **Default = empty initial commit; existing files left untracked / uncommitted / unpushed.** The core safety primitive. |
| `--initial-commit-message` | string | Message for the initial commit. **Requires `--commit-existing-files`** (hard error otherwise). |
| `--repo-name` / `--repo-owner` / `--repo-visibility` | string | Configure the new GitHub repo; **valid only with `--bootstrap=github`** (hard error with `local`/`off`/`--no-github`). Defaults: dir basename / gh login / private. |
| `--yes` / `-y` | bool, default `false` | Skip prompts, accept the mode's defaults. **Scope-bounded:** on its own it resolves to a local init (never GitHub, never commits existing files); GitHub creation still requires `--bootstrap=github` or a `--repo-*` flag, and committing existing files still requires `--commit-existing-files`. |

## Safe-by-default rationale

The content-leak vector is closed **by construction**: the initial commit is empty unless `--commit-existing-files` is given, so no user-authored file can be staged/committed/pushed without an explicit opt-in, and no GitHub repo is created without `--bootstrap=github` (or a `--repo-*` flag, or an interactive default-NO "yes"). That also makes the earlier "walk the directory, tally file count + size, detect nested repos, then confirm" primitive unnecessary — there is nothing to tally when nothing is committed by default.

### Security invariant

No path creates or pushes a GitHub repo, and no existing file is committed/pushed, without either an explicit non-defaulted human "yes" or an explicit opt-in (`--bootstrap=github` for creation, `--commit-existing-files` for content). Single funnel, side-effect- and network-free until `git init`:

`runGitHubBootstrapInit` → `normalizeBootstrapOptions` (validate + fold aliases) → `resolveBootstrapDecision` (proceed + GitHub intent; no side effect, no network) → `git init` → **post-consent** `gh` probe → `useGitHub` gate → finalize → `doInitialCommit` (stages only when `--commit-existing-files`) + `ghRepoCreate`.

A declined / `local` / `off` run makes **zero** `gh`/network calls, and no `gh` probe ever runs before init consent.

## Back-compat

The pre-existing bootstrap flags are retained as **deprecated aliases**, hidden from `--help`, each printing cobra's one-line deprecation hint:

| Deprecated flag | Maps to |
|---|---|
| `--init-repo` | `--bootstrap=local` |
| `--no-init-repo` | `--bootstrap=off` |
| `--no-github` | local (GitHub suppressed) |
| `--skip-initial-commit` | no-op (matches the new empty-commit default) |

`--repo-*` and `--initial-commit-message` keep their names (now scoped as above).

**Intentional behavior changes:**
- The initial commit no longer includes existing files by default — add `--commit-existing-files` to restore that.
- `--yes` alone no longer creates a GitHub repo — use `--bootstrap=github` or a `--repo-*` flag.
- **`--push` is removed.** It shipped only on `main` (via #1720) and in nightlies — never in a stable release — so this is not a released-surface break. In the new model `--bootstrap=github` always creates **and** pushes; pushing is safe by construction because the commit is empty unless `--commit-existing-files`.

## Testing / verification

- `go build ./...` clean; `gofmt -l` clean; `mise run lint` (golangci-lint) **0 issues**; `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/...` green (~7,000 package tests).
- The three security-critical guards are **mutation-verified** (revert the guard → a test fails → restore): default-NO init confirm; no-GitHub-create-without-opt-in; no-existing-files-without-`--commit-existing-files`. The last is caught by a real-git test (`…EmptyCommitLeavesFilesUntracked`) that fails with a decoy `secret.env` becoming tracked when the guard is removed.
- **Live matrix on the built binary** — a `gh` shim logging every call and simulating creation against a **local bare remote** (no real GitHub side effects), a decoy `secret.env` in every scratch dir, 34 scenarios across `{prompt,local,github,off} × {--yes} × {--commit-existing-files} × {--repo-*} × {interactive/non-interactive/EOF}`. Confirmed: no scenario made a `gh` call before `git init`; `gh repo create` fired only in the explicitly-authorized `github`/`--repo-*`+`--yes`/interactive-double-yes scenarios; `secret.env` reached a remote in exactly one scenario — the one passing `--commit-existing-files`. Empty-commit GitHub pushes ship a zero-file tree, so the `.entire/`/`.claude/` files written by setup and any pre-existing files are all excluded.

## Relationship to other work

- Supersedes #1725 (the same redesign, branched before #1720 landed and no longer reconcilable); #1725 will be closed in favor of this.
- Builds on #1720, which resolved #1717 on `main`.

Branch `feat/claudecode-cost`.

## Findings

### 1 — `cmd/entire/cli/agent/token_usage.go:297` remainderBucket emptiness includes APICallCount
`remainderBucket`'s non-empty test includes `APICallCount`, so a shortfall that is only an API-call-count delta (zero across all four token fields) still emits a spurious zero-token remainder bucket into `ModelUsage`. Exclude `APICallCount` from that emptiness check (base it on the four token fields only: Input/Output/CacheCreation/CacheRead). Read the function for the exact condition. Add/adjust a unit test proving an APICallCount-only shortfall produces no remainder bucket, while a real token shortfall still does.

### 2 — `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:848` Copilot session-state diagnostic cost never repriced
`sessionStateBackfillTokenUsage` prices the full-session `state.TokenUsage` with an empty fallback model; model recovery happens afterward in `backfillModelAndReprice`, whose identity check `state.TokenUsage == sessionData.TokenUsage` is false (different pointer), so the session-state diagnostic total is never repriced once the model is recovered. Persisted checkpoint (sessionData) is priced correctly — only the diagnostic total is affected. Read both functions; reprice the session-state total too once the model is recovered, GUARDED so a zero-data recovery window can never clobber a good value (mirror the existing guard on the sessionData reprice). If a safe fix genuinely needs a larger refactor, instead add a precise code comment documenting the limitation and say so in your report (orchestrator will dismiss-with-rationale). Prefer the fix. Add a test if feasible.

### 3 — `cmd/entire/cli/agent/token_usage.go:386` latent provenance mislabel in foldBucketCost/PriceUsage
A bucket with non-nil `CostUSD` but empty `CostSource` folds into a non-nil total with source "" (renders with no reported/estimated/mixed suffix). Currently unreachable. Add defensive normalization: when a bucket/usage has a non-nil CostUSD but empty CostSource at that boundary, treat it as `CostSourceEstimated`. Read foldBucketCost/PriceUsage/MergeCostSource to place it consistently. Add a unit test.

### 4 — `cmd/entire/cli/pricing/doc.go:6` stale package doc
Doc states "there is no runtime fetch" and describes pricing as embedded + settings overrides only. Round 2 added an opt-in background remote-pricing refresh (`pricing/remote.go`, `RefreshRemoteCache`, gated by `pricing.remote`). Update doc.go to describe the opt-in remote layer AND clarify there is no *inline* fetch on the hook path (refresh is detached/background). Concise + accurate.

- `mise run lint` (0 issues).
- `mise exec -- go test ./cmd/entire/cli/...` (or `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/...`) — all green, no FAIL. Re-run once if a transient FAIL appears under load.

## Commit + push
One or a few conventional commits (NO AI/Co-Authored-By footer). Push: `git push origin feat/claudecode-cost`. If push reports a remote issue, still commit and report the shas.

## Report
Per finding: fix + test name; commit sha(s); gate output tails; and for #2, whether you fixed it or recommend dismiss-with-rationale (with reason).

## Summary

All three PR #261 trail-review findings are fixed on `feat/checkpoint-cost` (pushed: `1a8e49b..99a117a`). Every test was mutation-verified (reverting the fix makes the test fail), so each is genuinely fix-sensitive.

### Finding 1 (Medium) — `ValidCostUSD` magnitude bound
- **Fix**: `internal/store/store.go` — added `const maxCostUSD = 1e8` and a `&& v < maxCostUSD` clause to `ValidCostUSD`, plus updated the doc comment to state the NUMERIC(14,6) range and the poison-loop rationale.
- **Sanitize path verified**: `SanitizeCost` (store.go:502) calls `ValidCostUSD`, so it inherits the range check with no further edit — an over-range value now drops to `nil` there too.
- **Test**: extended `TestNormalizeCostSourceAndValidCostUSD` (`internal/store/store_test.go`) — accepts `99999999.999999` and `0`; rejects `1e8`, `1e9` (plus existing NaN/Inf/-1). **Unit-level, ran and passed.** Mutation: removing the bound → `ValidCostUSD(1e8)=true` → FAIL.
- **Commit**: `4b9d6ec`.

### Finding 2 (Medium) — sanitize cost before JSONB store
- **Fix**: `internal/ingest/checkpoint.go` — `mapTokenUsage` now calls `store.SanitizeCost(tu.CostUSD, tu.CostSource)`. This is the single choke point all three carriers (root, per-session, per-model) flow through into the `SessionInfo` JSONB that `checkpointapi.go:277` echoes verbatim. Confirmed there is no other raw-metadata→JSONB cost site: the only other cost writes are the aggregate path (`buildCheckpointRow`, already `ValidCostUSD`-guarded) and the egress path (`flow.go`, already `SanitizeCost`d). No regression to the aggregate — a rogue source now arrives pre-normalized to `""` and is skipped identically.
- **Test**: added `TestParseSessionSanitizesInvalidCost` (`internal/ingest/checkpoint_test.go`) — drives `parseSession` with `cost_usd:-1`, over-range `1e9`, and unknown `cost_source` across root/session and per-model blocks; asserts null cost + empty source, and that a valid cost with a rogue source keeps the value but empties the source. **Unit-level, ran and passed.** Mutation: removing sanitize → cost `1e9`/source `provider-x` persist → FAIL.
- **Commit**: `0a99dec`.

### Finding 3 (Low) — inclusive/exclusive `until` mismatch
- **Decision**: I chose the localized "translate the bound" option over changing the shared `checkpointLinkWhere` predicate. That predicate feeds `Summary` for 4+ other endpoints (repoSummary, projectSummary, me team-scope, activity buckets) that intentionally agree as half-open; flipping it globally is a large, out-of-scope blast radius for a Low finding. Instead, in `projectSpend` (`internal/httpapi/repos.go`) I set `hi = until.Add(time.Microsecond)` when `until != nil`. Since `commit_date` is microsecond-quantized `TIMESTAMPTZ`, `< until+1µs` is provably identical to the `<= until` that `checkpoint_count` uses, and admits nothing beyond the boundary. Also softened the function's doc comment to note the at-most-one-boundary-checkpoint divergence from `/projects/{id}/summary` (the scope/visibility leak-prevention rationale is untouched).
- **Test**: added `TestIntegrationPipelineCheckpointMetricsProjectSpendUntilBoundary` (`internal/httpapi/pipeline_integration_test.go`) — seeds one costed checkpoint at exactly `until`, queries with `?until=<that instant>`, asserts `checkpoint_count == project_spend.total_checkpoints == 1` and cost included. **Integration-level (needs Postgres+NATS); ran via `mise run test:pipeline` and passed.** Mutation: reverting to `hi = *until` → `project_spend.total_checkpoints=0`, cost nil → FAIL.
- **Commit**: `99a117a`.

## Gate output tails
- `go build ./...` — exit 0, clean.
- `go vet ./internal/store/... ./internal/ingest/... ./internal/httpapi/...` — clean.
- `gofmt -l` on all 6 changed files — no output (clean).
- `mise run lint` (golangci-lint 2.11.2) — `0 issues.`
- `mise run test` (unit) — all packages `ok`, green.
- `mise run test:integration` (throwaway Postgres, Docker) — ran; store suite `ok` in 24.3s, all `PASS` (includes the Finding-1 store tests and `repo_aggregates` tests).
- `mise run test:pipeline` (throwaway Postgres+NATS, Docker) — ran; `httpapi` `ok` in 4.0s, all project_spend tests incl. the new boundary test `PASS`.

Docker was available, so **no finding-test was left unverified** — the Finding-3 test is integration-level but ran successfully.

## Decisions worth flagging
- **Finding 1 bound is `v < 1e8` exactly per spec.** One microscopic residual: a value in `[99999999.9999995, 1e8)` passes this check but rounds up to `100000000.000000` on NUMERIC(14,6) and would still overflow. I implemented exactly the task's spec (`reject v >= 1e8`, accept `99999999.999999`) rather than tightening to `< 99999999.9999995`, since the realistic poison trigger is a broken serializer emitting large magnitudes, not a cost inside a sub-rounding window — and tightening would risk the exact accept-case the task's test requires. Flagging in case you want the stricter bound.
- **Finding 3** intentionally trades a documented invariant slightly: `project_spend` can now differ from `/projects/{id}/summary` by at most the single boundary checkpoint for an identical `until`. In practice they never share an instant (different parsers: `parseOverviewDate` vs `parseTimeframe` with a live `now`), and the security parity is unchanged. Documented in-code.</result>

server="${ENTIRE_NATS_URL:-tls://localhost:4222}"
: "${ENTIRE_INTERNAL_TLS_CERT_FILE:?set it to the entire-api workload client cert (dev: entiredb internal cert)}"
: "${ENTIRE_INTERNAL_TLS_KEY_FILE:?set it to the matching client key}"
: "${ENTIRE_INTERNAL_TLS_CA_FILE:?set it to the internal CA bundle}"

content.text:
## What "the platform" is + where fresh pricing comes from

**The platform = Entire's server tiers** (`entire-api` cells + `entire.io`) — internal, not a product name. The CLI is the client; the platform is server-side. Dipree's "pull new cost faster" = the server can refresh pricing without a CLI release. Already partly real: **entire-api #261 stores cost server-side today.**

**Where the platform would pull live pricing (web search):**
- **LiteLLM `model_prices_and_context_window.json`** — the de-facto community pricing+context registry, 2600+ models / 140+ providers, plain JSON on GitHub, pullable directly. Most widely used source.
- **models.dev** — model catalog + pricing registry (what LiteLLM's site surfaces).
- **OpenRouter `/api/v1/models`** — JSON pricing for 315+ models, **updated daily**.

## The real architectural point (and I think Dipree's right)

Cost = **tokens × pricing**. Those two have opposite ownership:
- **Tokens + model** are facts only the agent/CLI can see (parsed from transcripts) → must be captured client-side, immutable.
- **Pricing** drifts over time and per-model → best pulled fresh by the platform.

So the clean split: **CLI stores tokens+model; the platform applies pricing at read-time** (pulled from a live source above). Benefits: re-price history when rates change/correct, zero CLI-release gating, one source of truth. #261 already stores tokens+model server-side — the server could compute `cost_usd` itself instead of trusting the CLI's stored figure.

That directly challenges **#1702's design** (CLI computes + persists `cost_usd` into checkpoint metadata). Round-2 softened it (CLI pulls a remote pricing table) but Dipree wants it fully server-side. This is a **direction call, not a bug** — I won't rip cost storage out of #1702 without your decision. Options when you want: (a) keep CLI cost as an estimate + platform re-prices authoritatively, or (b) CLI stops storing cost entirely, platform owns it.

The live E2E loop still running validates the *current* design; the numbers it returns are still the right proof regardless of which way you steer.

Sources: [LiteLLM (GitHub)](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm) · [LiteLLM models registry](https://models.litellm.ai/) · [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/)

content.text:
#1752 is real and substantial — pure-Go `gopher-lua` runtime, `plugins/` package with hooks/commands/KV/capabilities/manifest, 5k lines. Here's my take:

## Cost is a *bad* test case for the plugin system now — precisely because of the pivot

Split cost into its two halves and both leave the "third-party CLI plugin" slot empty:

- **Capture** (tokens / fast-detection / api-usage) → that's **core Entire**, not a plugin. Session capture is the product. You wouldn't ship it as an optional third-party plugin.
- **Pricing** (tokens → $) → we just **moved it to the platform** on purpose (Dipree: fresh rates without a client release). Re-implementing pricing as a *CLI* plugin walks that straight back — a plugin's `models.json` is exactly the stale-client-pricing problem the pivot removed.

So "since we changed, can we not" → **correct, mostly don't.** Before the pivot, cost was Georg's natural "add things like this via plugins" example; after it, cost has no piece that wants to be a client-side third-party plugin.

## But the pivot *clarifies* #1752 rather than killing it

The hook surface is still exactly right — just demo it with something that genuinely belongs client-side and third-party:
- **spend/budget alert** — hook on checkpoint, warn when a session's tokens cross a threshold (reads the same `model_usage`, no pricing needed).
- **notifier** — Slack/Datadog/webhook on checkpoint or push.
- **custom per-session summary** or **usage export** to a local file/format.
- a **custom command** contributed by a plugin.

Any of those exercises hooks + commands + KV without touching the cost architecture. That's the real test.

## Two things from the thread I'd act on
- **jdx's git-repo pricing** is the right Phase-3 mechanism for the *platform* pricing source — a pricing git repo + `git pull` beats standing up a JSON API, is versioned, and dovetails with "edit `models.json`". Lighter than a service.
- **gopher-lua was the right call** — matches jdx exactly (avoid `pkg/plugin` + `hashicorp/go-plugin`: both need a build step / Go compiler, non-starter for outside authors; Extism/wasm he flagged as abandoned + slight overhead). No-build-step Lua is correct.

Want me to (a) do a real review of #1752, or (b) prototype one of those non-cost demo plugins (e.g. the spend-alert hook) to exercise the system end-to-end?

input.content:
**Trail:** https://entire.io/gh/entirehq/entire-api/trails/298

> **Draft — direction change pending team sign-off.** This reverses the round-2 decision that "the CLI is the single source of truth and the server never estimates." Opening as a draft so the new design can be reviewed side-by-side with #261 before we commit to the reversal.

## What

entire-api computes checkpoint/session/per-model cost **itself**, at ingest, from the `model_usage` token breakdown it already ingests — and ignores any cost the CLI supplies. Pairs with the CLI change in entireio/cli (CLI stops storing cost).

## Why

Per team discussion (Dipree): cost shouldn't be stored in the CLI; the platform can pull fresh pricing far faster (no CLI release to correct a rate or add a model). Splitting the feature by ownership: the CLI captures the facts only it can see (tokens + model + fast/api-usage); the platform owns pricing and the authoritative cost.

## How

- New `internal/pricing/` — the CLI's audited pricing engine ported verbatim (byte-identical rate tables for anthropic/openai/google/cursor, id-spelling resolution incl. Bedrock/Vertex/tier variants, Anthropic cache multipliers 0.1×/1.25×). Own `Usage` type; no cross-repo dep. Ported unit tests included.
- `internal/ingest/cost.go` `estimateCost` + `parseSession`/`buildCheckpointRow`: each `model_usage` bucket is priced from its four token fields (input/cache-creation/cache-read/output), summed to the checkpoint/session cost, `cost_source = estimated`. Unknown model → nil (never a guess). The CLI-supplied `cost_usd` is **ignored entirely**; the unpriceable-root fallback was removed (nil, never a stale number).
- Reuses the existing cost columns + aggregation panels unchanged. Raw token buckets stay stored, so a Phase-3 re-price job can recompute when rates change without re-ingesting.

## Supersedes

Supersedes #261 (which ingested and stored the CLI's cost). This branch is #261's ingestion/panels/migrations **plus** the two server-compute commits on top.

## Testing

- `go build`/`vet`/`gofmt`/`mise run lint` clean; unit (pricing 64, ingest tests) + `test:integration` (16 cost tests) + `test:pipeline` green (throwaway PG+NATS).
- Math verified: a claude-opus-4-8 bucket (200k in / 50k out / 1M cache-read / 100k cache-write) → **$3.375000**, exact vs hand math and vs `pricing.Estimate`.
- **Live E2E (R2):** the real ingest code, driven on a real new-CLI checkpoint (no stored cost) against live Postgres, computed **$0.0800115** (= rate math); a planted CLI cost of `999.99` was ignored; surfaced in Postgres (`0.080012`) and the HTTP detail DTO. Full-transport (R1: git push → NATS → worker → authed HTTP) verification in progress.

## Known findings (for review)

- **Dual precision in one response:** checkpoint `cost_usd` is `NUMERIC(14,6)` (`0.080012`) while per-model JSONB keeps full float (`0.0800115`) — summing sessions ≠ top-level (sub-cent). Decide whether to align.
- **Cost is load-bearing on `model_usage[].model`:** an ingested path with aggregate tokens but no resolvable `model_usage` model yields nil cost (the old CLI-computes design was more forgiving). Confirm every cost-bearing agent emits `model_usage`.

## Follow-ups

Phase 3: server-side live pricing pull (a pricing git repo + `git pull`, per jdx, is lighter than a JSON API) + a re-price job over the stored token buckets. No pricing-source live-refresh in this PR (embedded table only).

**Trail:** https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/865

> **Draft — direction change pending team sign-off.** Reverses the round-2 decision that "the CLI is the single source of truth" for cost. Opening as a draft so it can be reviewed alongside #1702 before committing to the reversal. Pairs with entirehq/entire-api (platform computes cost).

## What

The CLI stops **persisting** cost into checkpoint metadata. It keeps persisting the token facts the platform prices from (`model_usage` with all four token fields per model + model id, flat token counts, model, api-call counts). Cost is now shown only as a clearly-labeled **local estimate** in the token commands.

## Why

Per team discussion (Dipree): don't store cost in the CLI — the platform can pull fresh pricing far faster (no CLI release to fix a rate or add a model). The CLI's job narrows to capturing the facts only it can see; the platform (entire-api) owns pricing and the authoritative cost.

## How

- A single choke point — `Metadata.WithoutCost()` / `CheckpointSummary.WithoutCost()` — applied at all six checkpoint-metadata marshal sites (branch + refs backends). It clears `cost_usd`/`cost_source` at every level (flat, subagent subtree, each per-model bucket) while preserving the four token fields, model ids, and counts.
- The in-memory compute path is intentionally **kept** — condensation's model-recovery rebucketing keys on `CostUSD == nil`, so removing it would change when `model_usage` is rebucketed. Only what's written to disk drops cost.
- Token commands (`entire session tokens`, `entire checkpoint tokens [--compare]`, `entire tokens profile`) recompute a local estimate on the fly via `agent.EstimateCost` from the persisted tokens + `model_usage`, labeled `$X (estimated locally)` with a note that the authoritative cost lives on the platform. Unknown model → no cost line (never `$0`). The `pricing/` package is retained for this local display.

## Supersedes

Supersedes #1702 (which computed and stored cost in the CLI). This branch is #1702 **plus** the two reduction commits on top.

## Testing

- `gofmt`/`mise run lint` clean; `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/... ./api/checkpoint/...` green.
- `TestWriteCommitted_DoesNotPersistCost`: a checkpoint with cost + subagents + per-model buckets round-trips with token counts / model ids / subagent counts intact and cost nil/empty at every level.
- Updated condensation test proves persisted `model_usage` is bucketed under the recovered model with token counts, but no cost.
- Display tests: token commands still render a cost line, computed live, labeled as a local estimate.

## Note for review

Backfill/summary rewrites now also strip cost from any **legacy** checkpoint they rewrite (cost written by an older CLI is cleared on the next attribution/summary backfill). Consistent with "the CLI does not persist cost" — flagging to confirm it's intended.

## Follow-up

If the team decides the CLI should drop cost **display** entirely too, the `pricing/` package + the cost fields/machinery could be removed (larger blast radius — condensation's model-recovery currently rides on the cost path; would need re-expressing as a pure model-signal). Not done here.

The entire chain runs on the live local stack: real `git push` → entiredb ref → NATS `repo_refs_v1` → entire-api `run:repo` ingester (computes cost server-side) → Postgres → **authed** `GET` returns the platform-computed `cost_usd` / `cost_source=estimated`. The auth wall the prior run hit is solved (not bypassed).

## End-to-end trace (single checkpoint, live)

## Cost vs rate math (exact)

Raw pushed checkpoint metadata carries `model_usage` (opus: in 4, out 204, cache-read 39483, cache-write 8824) and **no cost field at all** → the platform computed it:
`4·$5 + 204·$25 + 39483·$0.50 + 8824·$6.25` per MTok = `0.00002 + 0.0051 + 0.0197415 + 0.055150 = $0.0800115` → stored `0.080012` (NUMERIC(14,6) half-up). Matches the surfaced `cost_usd` exactly. `cost_source=estimated` confirms server-side estimation (a CLI-reported cost would read `reported`).

## What it took to get past the auth wall (exact seams solved)

1. **Register + grant a repo on local core**: break-glass → `POST /api/auth/system/login` → login JWT; `POST /api/v1/projects` (account-owned by admin → admin gets push); `POST /api/v1/repos` (this **provisions** entiredb DHT placement — the adopt/`admin repos import` path does NOT, so pushes to an imported-only ULID 503 with `no providers reachable for repo`). Had to `POST /api/admin/users/{admin}/approve` first (token exchange refuses waitlisted accounts).
2. **Mint a repo push token**: the documented `dev:mint-repo-token` is **stale** (`/api/authz/repo-token` is gone → 404). Real path is `POST /oauth/token` RFC-8693 token-exchange: `subject_token=<login JWT>`, `audience=https://localhost:8080/git/repo/<ULID>`, `scope=repo:push`, Basic `entire-cli:`.
3. **Push**: plain `git push https://localhost:8080/git/repo/<ULID>` with `-c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Bearer <push token>"` + `GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY=1` (no `git-remote-entire` needed).
4. **Workers**: `run:repo` reaches entiredb's Repo API over the **svctok mTLS listener** `https://localhost:8380/api/v1` using the entire-api workload cert (`internal-cert-entire-api.pem`, SPIFFE `spiffe://partial.to/local/entire-api`, granted repo-read); NATS auth uses the same cert. Created the 3 entire-api streams (`repo_index_jobs{,_backfill}`, `user_activity_v1`) via `nats` CLI.
5. **Authed read**: entire-api's `Authenticator` requires an identity token with `scope=openid` + `aud==ENTIRE_JURISDICTION_AUDIENCE`. Local core (standalone) had **no** `ENTIRE_JURISDICTION_AUDIENCE`, so it could not mint `openid` for any audience — **restarted the core dev process** with `ENTIRE_JURISDICTION_AUDIENCE=https://us.partial.to` (same signing keys/DB, transparent to nodes). Then minted the identity token via `/oauth/token` (`audience=https://us.partial.to`, `scope=openid`).

## Real bugs / friction the live transport exposed

- **`entiredb mise-tasks/dev/mint-repo-token` is broken** — targets the removed `/api/authz/repo-token` (returns Go's `404 page not found`). Should use the `/oauth/token` token-exchange.
- **entire-api authz Reader is TLS-only with no plaintext dev escape** (`internal/authz/reader.go: DialReader` → `credentials.NewTLS`), but the dev SpiceDB serves plaintext gRPC (`:50051`). Result: every `cmd/api` authz check `503`s against a stock dev SpiceDB. Worked around with a stdlib TLS→plaintext proxy (`:50052`, mkcert cert, ALPN h2) + `ENTIRE_SPICEDB_ENDPOINT=localhost:50052` / `ENTIRE_SPICEDB_CA_FILE=internal-ca.pem`. There is no `ENTIRE_SPICEDB_INSECURE`/plaintext option — a genuine local-dev gap.
- **`cmd/api` treats `ENTIRE_SNAPSHOT_CIPHER` as fatal**; the `repo-activity` worker only warns on the identical condition. Inconsistent — the api needs snapshot config unrelated to serving cost.
- **Content read-through endpoints 502 locally**: `GET …/checkpoints` and `…/commits/{sha}` forward the caller's identity token to entiredb's Repo API, and the entiredb nodes' `ENTIRE_TRUSTED_AUDIENCES` doesn't include the jurisdiction host `https://us.partial.to`, so entiredb `401`s the read-through. The cost DTO (`overview/checkpoint-metrics`, Postgres-only) is unaffected. Local-config gap on the node side, not a product defect.
- **Cost only surfaces through commit-anchored aggregates**: `checkpoint-metrics`/detail count via `checkpoint_commits` (default-branch `shipped` links). Pushing only the `entire/checkpoints/v1` metadata branch (and letting it become HEAD/default) yields `checkpoint_count:0`. Needs the user commit carrying `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` pushed on the default branch — i.e., push `main` **first** so entiredb HEAD (→ `default_branch`) is `main`.

{"author":"peyton-alt","body":"### Problem

`checkpoint rewind` (and the hidden top-level `rewind`) are deprecated and announced for removal, but `rewind --list` is currently the **only machine-readable checkpoint listing** the CLI offers. Both test harnesses and docs depend on it, so the removal is blocked until an equivalent exists on a non-deprecated command.

### Wrinkle: the two commands show different data

- `checkpoint rewind --list` returns `strategy.GetRewindPoints()` — the **live session's rewind points from the shadow branch** (includes task checkpoints, logs-only points, condensation IDs; capped at 20). JSON output.
- `checkpoint list` runs the explain-branch view — **condensed checkpoints from `entire/checkpoints/v1`** for the current branch, human-formatted through a pager.

So a naive `--json` on `checkpoint list` would serialize a different dataset than the one consumers of `rewind --list` need.

### Proposal

Add `--json` to `entire checkpoint list`, exposing the rewind-point fields (`id`, `message`, `metadata_dir`, `date`, `is_task_checkpoint`, `tool_use_id`, `is_logs_only`, `condensation_id`, `session_id`, `session_prompt` — see `runRewindList` in `cmd/entire/cli/rewind.go`).

Design decision needed on how to reconcile the datasets, e.g.:
- a scope flag (`--pending` / `--all`) selecting shadow-branch vs condensed view, or
- `--json` covers both datasets with a `source` discriminator field.

### Migrate consumers (grep says it's more than one helper)

- `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/testenv.go` — `TestEnv.GetRewindPoints()` shells out to `checkpoint rewind --list`; repointing this one helper migrates ~48 call sites across 11 integration test files.
- `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/setup_cmd_test.go` — direct invocation.
- `cmd/entire/cli/testutil/testutil.go` — another direct consumer.
- `e2e/entire/entire.go` — the e2e harness has its own copy.
- `e2e/tests/rewind_test.go` — exercises the deprecated command itself; parts of it should be retired with the command.
- Docs: `WINDOWS.md`, the `test-repo` skill (`.claude/skills/test-repo/SKILL.md` + `.agents/skills/test-repo/SKILL.md`).

### Then

Complete the announced removal of `checkpoint rewind` / top-level `rewind` (whether the interactive rewind flow survives elsewhere is part of that removal decision, not this issue).

### Optional rider (or split into a second small issue)

The test harness also rides on the deprecated no-op `TestEnv.Cleanup()`: delete the method and sweep its ~44 `defer env.Cleanup()` call sites in the integration suite. Same shape of debt, cheap to do in the same pass. - `checkpoint list` (default) → condensed checkpoints, human view (unchanged).

Heal misses vercel.json-only orphans: the re-enable recovery path checks isEmptyMetadataBranch, which requires a literal empty tree. But orphan creation runs vercelconfig.MaybeMergeMetadataBranchConfig (common.go ~536 on main), so on vercel-enabled repos the pre-fix orphan tip contains vercel.json — isEmpty is false, the heal never fires, and those devices keep the divergent orphan forever even after upgrading and re-running enable. Stale origin tracking ref still shadows the configured checkpoint_remote. DefaultV1Refs always has Primary in Push, so PrimaryFetchableFromOrigin() is true and EnsurePrimaryRef consults origin/entire/checkpoints/v1 first. On a repo that migrated from origin-hosted checkpoints to a dedicated checkpoint_remote, a clone carries the stale origin tracking ref, so: (a) local-ref-missing → 'Created local ref from origin' fires at line ~558 and bootstrapPrimaryFromCheckpointRemote (line 570) is never reached; (b) local-empty-orphan + differing origin ref → the divergence path points local at origin's stale data. Either way stale checkpoints get seeded and can later be replayed into the checkpoint remote.

Fix: adopt PR #1384's authority rule — when remote.Configured(ctx), never seed from origin: consult the checkpoint remote first (bootstrap/heal), and if it yields nothing usable, keep local or create an orphan rather than falling back to origin. Ported #1384's `metadataBranchInitFiles` allowlist + `metadataBranchHasData`, replacing `isEmptyMetadataBranch` at every call site in `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go`. A tip tree containing only `vercelconfig.FileName` is now treated as data-free, so the heal fires on vercel-enabled repos.

### Finding 2 (Medium) — stale origin ref shadows checkpoint_remote
Ported #1384's authority rule: restructured `EnsurePrimaryRef` so `remote.Configured(ctx)` short-circuits at the top and never consults origin — heal (local exists) or bootstrap→orphan (local missing), never falling back to origin's tracking ref. ```markdown
# Task: work the Entire CLI bug backlog — one live-verified fix PR per issue

Repo: `entireio/cli` (Go). For each assigned issue, take it end-to-end: reproduce it
LIVE, fix at the root, PROVE the fix by re-reproducing (the bug must no longer occur),
audit it, and open a clean PR under my GitHub account. Never claim a fix you haven't
demonstrated live.

## Issue selection
- Target: open `bug`-labeled issues with NO PR that would close them:
  `gh issue list --repo entireio/cli --label bug --state open --limit 200 --json number,title`
  then drop any number that appears in an open PR's closing refs (a PR body with
  `Fixes/Closes #N`).
- SKIP what you can't reproduce locally on this machine, and say why you skipped it:
  web/dashboard-only (entire.io UI), cloud/platform-only (Factory Droid, Copilot Cloud),
  or Windows/PowerShell-only if you're not on Windows. Work the CLI-reproducible ones.

## Per-issue loop — do NOT skip a step
1. REPRODUCE LIVE FIRST. Build from a fresh worktree off `main`, set up a real scratch
   repo + agent/hook flow, and trigger the EXACT failure in the issue. Capture the actual
   bad output. If you cannot reproduce it, STOP and report that — do not fix blind.
2. FIX at the root. Minimal, targeted, matches surrounding style.
3. LIVE-VERIFY. Re-run the exact repro from step 1 → confirm the bug no longer happens.
   Then run the edge cases around it. The proof is "re-reproducing no longer triggers it,"
   not merely a green unit test.
4. MUTATION-VERIFIED regression test. Revert the fix → the new test must FAIL → restore →
   it passes. If reverting doesn't fail it, the test is worthless; rewrite it.
5. /audit the change (or run the loop yourself): review as a careful reviewer AND
   adversarially (edge/nil/concurrency/security); fix everything; re-verify; loop until
   two consecutive clean passes AND build+lint+tests are green.
6. /makepr — open the PR per the conventions below.

## Environment
- One isolated worktree per issue: `git worktree add -b fix/<issue>-<slug> <path> origin/main`.
  NEVER commit to the main checkout.
- Toolchain is mise: `mise trust` the new worktree, then `mise exec -- go ...`.
- Build: `go build -o /tmp/entire-<issue> ./cmd/entire`.
- Gates (green on the COMMITTED tree): `gofmt -l` clean, `mise run lint` 0 issues,
  `mise exec -- go test ./cmd/entire/cli/...`; integration: `go test -tags integration ...`.
- Repro harness: temp git repo → `entire enable --agent <agent>` → drive the real hook flow;
  inspect state with `entire checkpoint list --pending --json`, `entire status`, etc.

## PR conventions (/makepr) — author under MY account
- Open the PR with `gh pr create` FIRST (as me), THEN create the trail. `entire trail create`
  auto-opens the PR via the Entire GitHub App, which sets the PR author to `app/entire`.
  Creating via `gh` first claims the author slot as my user; trail-create then just links to
  the existing PR. Sequence:
    git push -u origin <branch>
    gh pr create --base main --head <branch> --title "fix(<scope>): <summary>" --body-file body.md
    entire trail create --branch <branch> --title "fix(<scope>): <summary>"
    gh pr edit <n>  # prepend "**Trail:** <url>" to the body
- Conventional title `fix(<scope>): <imperative summary>`.
- NO AI/bot footers — no "Generated with", no "Co-Authored-By: <AI>", no session links.
- Body: Trail link first, then What / Why / How / Testing. Use `Fixes #<issue>`. In Testing,
  state the exact live repro, that re-running it no longer triggers the bug, the edge cases,
  and that gates are green on the committed tree.
- Reply to review threads with the technical resolution only, then resolve them.

## Honesty
One PR per issue. Per issue report: reproduced Y/N (+how), root cause, the fix, the live
re-verify result, audit outcome, PR link. Separate "verified fixed" from "couldn't verify."
If a bug isn't real, isn't reproducible, or needs a design decision, say so — don't force a fix.

Windows-only (skip unless on Windows): #1072, #1096, #1675.
Web/platform (skip — not CLI-reproducible): #421?, #1039, #1040, #859, #1006; #376 is a question.

**[#756 — Betterleaks instead of Gitleaks](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/756)**
Requested swapping the secret scanner from Gitleaks to Betterleaks. Shipped: `go.mod` pins `betterleaks v1.5.0`, `redact/redact.go` uses its detector, and the CHANGELOG (#1043/#1045/#1068) confirms it with a regression test guarding the git-env bug. Implemented.

Diagnosed — it's a **rename that outran the tag**. The binary was renamed `entire-sem` → `entire-graph` on `main`, *after* v0.1.0 was cut:

- `@latest` resolves to the only tag, **v0.1.0**, whose `cmd/` still has `entire-sem` / `sem-bench` (the old names) — no `cmd/entire-graph`.
- The new `cmd/entire-graph` (+ `cmd/graph-bench`) exists **only on `main`**, which is untagged.

So `go install .../cmd/entire-graph@latest` can't find the package at v0.1.0.

**Works right now** (install from `main`):
```
go install github.com/entireio/entire-graph/cmd/entire-graph@main
```
(The tagged binary still exists under its old name: `go install github.com/entireio/entire-graph/cmd/entire-sem@v0.1.0` — but that's the pre-rename build.)

**Proper fix (maintainer):** cut a new tag off `main` — e.g. `v0.2.0` — that contains `cmd/entire-graph`. Then `@latest` resolves to it and the original command works. Also worth updating the install docs from `entire-sem` → `entire-graph`.

Want me to **cut the `v0.2.0` tag/release** off current `main` (pushed today) so `@latest` works? I'd verify `cmd/entire-graph` builds first. Won't tag without your go-ahead.
Fix this for other ppl too ; in the docs, and tell us how to update other ppl already testing

- **🪶 Lean on memory where it counts.** Memory is released after the build. On repositories it fully indexes, peak stays in tens of MB where the competitor uses hundreds: **80 MB vs 599 MB** (nlohmann/json), **64 vs 285** (koin), **43 vs 225** (Dapper).

- **🕸️ A 30-relation code graph with stable identity.** `compound-v1` symbol IDs survive ordinary edits. Relations span structure, calls, inheritance, fields, service boundaries, and config dependencies, each tagged with resolution and confidence.
- **💸 Fewer tokens for coding agents.** For a core symbol like `redisCommand` in redis, the five structural questions cost about **2,300 tokens** from the graph versus about **654,000 tokens** to read the 23 files that reference it: a **283x reduction** (measured with tiktoken). Savings scale with how widely a symbol is used.
- **🧩 Part of Entire.** The same graph powers entity-level checkpoint context, so a checkpoint can be judged (keep, revert, continue) without reading the full diff.

**Requirements:** Entire CLI · Git · Go toolchain with CGO enabled (tree-sitter uses native parser bindings).

```sh
# 1. Install the plugin binary and register it with Entire's managed plugin dir
go install github.com/entireio/entire-graph/cmd/entire-graph@main
entire plugin install "$(go env GOPATH)/bin/entire-graph" --force

# 2. Verify the install and the local-only environment
entire graph version
entire graph doctor --json        # includes "no_egress": true

# 3. Run your first semantic diff, from any git repository
entire graph commit HEAD
```

If `$(go env GOPATH)/bin` is already on your `PATH`, Entire can discover the binary directly after `go install`. Entire plugins are local executables, not a hosted marketplace: `entire graph` works because Entire finds an `entire-graph` binary in its managed plugin directory or on `$PATH`.

### 🛠️ Install From Source

```sh
git clone https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph.git
cd entire-graph
mise run build
entire plugin install ./entire-graph --force
```

For a one-command local source install run `scripts/install-local.sh`; it builds `./entire-graph`, installs it, prints `entire graph version`, and fails before writing anything if the parent `entire` CLI is not on `PATH`. For release archives with `SHA256SUMS`, run `scripts/release.sh`. See [docs/operations.md](docs/operations.md) for target and cgo details.

-- models-updater: an example command plugin that downloads a models.json

Good news: `Model` is an interface — clean seam. Not just an env flip though; Fireworks = different API shape (OpenAI chat-completions, not Anthropic messages), so it's a code change, but contained.

**Where it lives** (`internal/checkpointanalysis/model.go`):

- `anthropicModel` (:54) wraps `anthropic.Client`; `NewAnthropicModel(apiKey, baseURL, gatewayToken)` (:63) → CF AI Gateway → `m.client.Messages.New(... Model: analysisModel ...)` (:76).

**How to switch to Fireworks:**
1. New impl `fireworksModel` (same `Model` interface) — OpenAI-compat client → `https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1/chat/completions`, Fireworks model id (e.g. `accounts/fireworks/models/llama-v3p3-70b-instruct` or `deepseek-v3`). Force JSON out (`response_format` json/json_schema or prompt).

**Gotchas:**
- Anthropic-messages → OpenAI-chat: map system/user prompt to `messages[]`, parse `choices[0].message.content` as the JSON blob the pipeline expects.
- **Dead path for Fireworks:** the Anthropic-workspace-cap deferral (`generator.go:105`, HTTP 400 cap → `labels_state=deferred`) is Anthropic-only. Fireworks errors = 429/5xx; adjust retry classification, skip the cap-defer branch.
- **CF AI Gateway:** current path routes through it (`internal/aigateway`, `provider="anthropic"`, cost attribution/caching). Fireworks: either add a fireworks provider path on the gateway, or bypass + call direct (lose gateway caching/attribution).
- Pick a fast/cheap Fireworks model good at structured JSON — Haiku's role is small+cheap+reliable-JSON.

Two parts: make it pluggable, then A/B it on a frozen corpus with a judge + cost/latency meters. No gold labels exist, so "accuracy" = strong-model judge + deterministic validity, not a single truth.

**1. Make it swappable** (the seam already exists)
- Add `fireworksModel` impl + `CHECKPOINT_ANALYSIS_PROVIDER` config → pick anthropic|fireworks at build. Both satisfy `Model`, so eval can hold both at once.

**2. Eval harness** (offline, standalone — no NATS/prod pipeline)
- **Corpus:** freeze N real checkpoints' transcripts (pull from the store's analyzed checkpoints, or captured fixtures). Same input to both models. Freeze = repeatable.
- **Run both:** Haiku (incumbent baseline) + Fireworks (candidate) over the same N. Capture output labels/facets + raw usage + wall-clock per call.
- **Accuracy** (no ground truth → 3 signals):
  - *Deterministic:* label-vocab validity (invalid/dropped-label rate — `labels.go` constrains the set), JSON-schema validity, facet coverage.
  - *Judged:* blind A/B — strong model (Fable/Opus) sees transcript + both label sets (order-shuffled), picks better fit → **win-rate**. Also absolute 1–5 relevance score each.
  - *Agreement:* Jaccard label overlap Haiku↔Fireworks (drift signal, not truth).
- **Efficiency:** per-checkpoint latency (p50/p95), tokens in/out, **$/checkpoint** (Fireworks rate × tokens vs Haiku rate). Fireworks open models ~10× cheaper/token — the tradeoff you're testing.
- **Output:** one table `model | valid% | judge-win% | mean relevance | p50 latency | tokens | $/ckpt`.

**Guardrails:** frozen corpus + multiple runs (LLM output varies); LLM-judge is itself noisy → strong judge, shuffle order, maybe 3-vote majority. Report both judged + deterministic so it's not judge-only.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build blind A/B judge inputs. Randomized order per item, hidden key kept separately."""
import json, os, random, glob

CAE = "/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suhaan-devenv/ec68e677-f6b8-4c44-bbd2-7fe9e938e78a/scratchpad/cae"
random.seed(20260717)  # deterministic A/B assignment

# MiniMax outputs (all 34; we only use the 14 with a fair baseline)
cand = {r["id"]: r for r in json.load(open(f"{CAE}/candidate_minimax.json"))}

# Fair per-item Haiku outputs
base = {}
for f in glob.glob(f"{CAE}/baseline_fair/*.json"):
    r = json.load(open(f))
    base[r["id"]] = r

ids = sorted(base.keys())
os.makedirs(f"{CAE}/judge_inputs", exist_ok=True)
key = {}
for i in ids:
    if i not in cand:
        print(f"WARN: {i} missing from candidate; skip"); continue
    mm = cand[i]["output"]      # string (raw json text) or dict
    hk = base[i]["output"]      # dict
    # normalize both to parsed dict
    mm_obj = mm if isinstance(mm, dict) else json.loads(mm)
    hk_obj = hk if isinstance(hk, dict) else json.loads(hk)
    if random.random() < 0.5:
        A, B, a_is = mm_obj, hk_obj, "minimax"
    else:
        A, B, a_is = hk_obj, mm_obj, "haiku"
    key[i] = a_is
    json.dump(
        {"id": i, "extraction_A": A, "extraction_B": B},
        open(f"{CAE}/judge_inputs/{i}.json", "w"), indent=2,
    )
json.dump(key, open(f"{CAE}/judge_key.json", "w"), indent=2)
print(f"prepped {len(key)} judge inputs")
print("A_is distribution:", {v: list(key.values()).count(v) for v in ("minimax","haiku")})

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Unblind judge_out via judge_key, tally per-model quality; join MiniMax efficiency."""
import json, glob, statistics as st

CAE = "/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suhaan-devenv/ec68e677-f6b8-4c44-bbd2-7fe9e938e78a/scratchpad/cae"
key = json.load(open(f"{CAE}/judge_key.json"))          # id -> "minimax"|"haiku" (which one is A)
DIMS = ["label_accuracy", "summary_faithful", "structure", "overall"]

rows = []
for f in sorted(glob.glob(f"{CAE}/judge_out/*.json")):
    j = json.load(open(f))
    i = j["id"]
    a_is = key[i]
    b_is = "haiku" if a_is == "minimax" else "minimax"
    mm = j["A"] if a_is == "minimax" else j["B"]
    hk = j["A"] if a_is == "haiku" else j["B"]
    w = j.get("winner", "tie")
    win = a_is if w == "A" else (b_is if w == "B" else "tie")
    rows.append({"id": i, "minimax": mm, "haiku": hk, "winner": win,
                 "conf": j.get("confidence", 0), "reason": j.get("reason", "")})

print(f"judged items: {len(rows)}\n")

def col(model, dim): return [r[model][dim] for r in rows]

print("=== per-dimension mean (1-5) ===")
print(f"{'dim':18} {'minimax':>8} {'haiku':>8}  delta")
for d in DIMS:
    m = st.mean(col("minimax", d)); h = st.mean(col("haiku", d))
    print(f"{d:18} {m:8.2f} {h:8.2f}  {m-h:+.2f}")

wins = {"minimax": 0, "haiku": 0, "tie": 0}
for r in rows: wins[r["winner"]] += 1
n = len(rows)
print("\n=== head-to-head (blind winner) ===")
print(f"minimax wins: {wins['minimax']}/{n}   haiku wins: {wins['haiku']}/{n}   ties: {wins['tie']}/{n}")

# overall-score head-to-head (per item, who scored higher on 'overall')
mm_hi = sum(1 for r in rows if r["minimax"]["overall"] > r["haiku"]["overall"])
hk_hi = sum(1 for r in rows if r["haiku"]["overall"] > r["minimax"]["overall"])
eq = n - mm_hi - hk_hi
print(f"by overall-score: minimax higher {mm_hi}, haiku higher {hk_hi}, equal {eq}")

print("\n=== per-item (unblinded) ===")
print(f"{'id':26} {'mm_ovr':>6} {'hk_ovr':>6}  {'winner':>8} conf")
for r in sorted(rows, key=lambda x: x["id"]):
    print(f"{r['id']:26} {r['minimax']['overall']:6} {r['haiku']['overall']:6}  {r['winner']:>8} {r['conf']}")

# efficiency join (MiniMax measured; Haiku priced on same token profile)
cs = json.load(open(f"{CAE}/candidate_summary.json"))
print("\n=== efficiency ===")
print(json.dumps(cs, indent=2))
# cost at published rates on the measured token profile (input ~identical: shared prompt+transcript)
ti = cs.get("mean_tokens_in"); to = cs.get("mean_tokens_out")
if ti and to:
    mm_cost = ti/1e6*0.30 + to/1e6*1.20
    hk_cost = ti/1e6*1.00 + to/1e6*5.00   # claude-haiku-4-5 $1/$5 per MTok
    print(f"\ncost/checkpoint on measured token profile ({ti:.0f} in / {to:.0f} out):")
    print(f"  minimax-m3   ${mm_cost:.6f}")
    print(f"  haiku-4-5    ${hk_cost:.6f}   ({hk_cost/mm_cost:.2f}x minimax)")

json.dump(rows, open(f"{CAE}/tally_rows.json", "w"), indent=2)
