input.content:
# entire-graph: accuracy + token/latency losses from corpus pollution, no index reuse, and non-score ranking

**Type:** bug / performance
**Area:** `entire graph search` · `impact` · index/preselection
**Severity:** high — the two symptoms an agent notices first are *"the top hit points at a file that isn't the real one"* (trust) and *"one query reads tens of MB and takes 13–30 s"* (tokens/latency). Both are traced to concrete, fixable root causes below.

---

## TL;DR

Dogfooded the graph on **its own repo** (query: *"how are semantic search hits ranked and scored"*), measured a **clean checkout (146 Go source files, tracked)** against the **working tree as it sits on disk (with `.claude/worktrees/`)**. Findings, most-leverage first:

| # | Finding | Hurts | Measured |
|---|---------|-------|----------|
| **T1** | **Generated tree-sitter grammar blobs are indexed** (`internal/sem/grammars/*/parser.c`) — **tracked in the repo, so every clone hits this** | tokens, accuracy | 11 `parser.c`, **193 MB**; julia alone **53 MB**; ~52 MB read on a 146-file repo; they fail to parse → completeness downgraded to `degraded` |
| **T2** | **`.claude/worktrees/` agent scratch is indexed** — untracked, not gitignored | trust, tokens, latency | 1.5 GB, 1044 `.go` copies; corpus **146 → 2585 files scanned**; **8 / 10 top hits point at throwaway worktree copies**; `impact` **hung > 2 min**; 76 MB read; 30 s |
| **T3** | **Index is rebuilt on every invocation** (`index_cache_hit: false` / `cache-miss` every call) | tokens, latency | search **13 s**, impact **31 s** on the *same unchanged* clean tree — back-to-back calls both paid full build |
| **A1** | **Final ordering is not sorted by score** | trust | rank 7 (`SearchRepository`, 19.8) outscores ranks 3–6 (17.6/17.1/16.6/16.4); rank 10 has **score 0** and no symbol name |
| **A2** | **Context budget spent on duplicate / zero-value snippets** | tokens | 6–8 of 10 snippets truncated by budget; worktree-duplicate full bodies eat the budget canonical hits need |
| **A3** | **`type_card` surfaces trivial locals** (earlier run: `minimal`/`compact`/`rich` string vars) instead of meaningful types | accuracy | noise bytes per query |

**One-line fix priority:** exclude generated-parser blobs + agent worktrees from the corpus, reuse the built index across invocations, and sort output by score. T1+T2+T3 together take a query from *52–76 MB / 13–30 s / 8-of-10-wrong* to roughly *~2 MB / <2 s / canonical hits*.

---

## How this was measured

- **Clean tree:** `git archive HEAD | tar -x` of `entire-graph` → **146 `.go` files**, no `.claude/worktrees/`. Fresh `git init/add/commit` so the graph sees a normal repo.
- **Polluted tree:** the working directory as it actually sits (what an agent's `--repo .` sees), which contains `.claude/worktrees/agent-*/…` from prior agent runs.
- Same query on both, `--profile full --format json`, stats block captured verbatim. `impact` timed separately.
- Nothing was fetched, pulled, or deleted from the repo; the clean tree is a throwaway copy.

---

## Accuracy / trustworthiness

### A0 (root cause of the "not trustworthy" feeling) — worktree copies win the ranking
On the **polluted** tree, **8 of the top 10 hits pointed at `.claude/worktrees/agent-XXXXX/internal/sem/…`** — stale duplicate copies — instead of the canonical `internal/sem/*.go`. An agent told by the doctrine to *"edit the top hit directly from search output"* edits a throwaway tree; the change lands nowhere and the build is unaffected. This is the single biggest trust failure and it is invisible unless you notice the path prefix.

On the **clean** tree the exact same query returns **0 worktree hits** — every hit is canonical (`internal/cli/search.go`, `internal/sem/search*.go`). So the tool is *correct* on a clean corpus and *untrustworthy* only because it indexes scratch trees. Fix = stop indexing them (see F-fixes).

### A1 — final order is not score order
Clean-tree top 10 (rank | score | symbol):

```
 1 | 23.686 | agentSearchLocationHeaders   internal/cli/search.go:641
 2 | 21.317 | agentSearchBlock             internal/cli/search.go:611
 3 | 17.635 | loadOrBuildSearchGraphSnapshot
 4 | 17.056 | dedupeSemanticMirrorCandidates
 5 | 16.553 | mergeSearchRelatedSites
 6 | 16.447 | countBudgetTruncatedResults
 7 | 19.806 | SearchRepository             internal/sem/search.go:662   ← outscores 3–6
 8 | 15.314 | AssessSearchConfidence
 9 | 14.119 | assignSearchSections
10 |  0.000 | (no symbol name)            internal/sem/search_mirror_dedup.go:153
```

`SearchRepository` — arguably *the* answer to "how are hits ranked" — is buried at **rank 7** despite scoring higher than the four hits above it, and a **score-0, unnamed fragment** occupies rank 10. The doctrine promises "the top hit is the fix site"; when rank and score disagree, agents that trust rank 1–3 and stop are steered wrong. **Fix:** sort emitted hits by score (or, if a deliberate re-rank exists, emit the effective score you sorted on so rank is explainable).

### A2 — score-0 / unnamed fragments occupy top-10 slots
Rank 10 above has score 0 and no `symbol_name` — a non-actionable fragment taking a slot a real candidate could use. **Fix:** drop score-0 and un-symboled fragments from the ranked list (or floor the list at a minimum score).

### A3 — `type_card` surfaces trivial locals
An earlier run's `type_card` listed local string vars (`minimal`, `compact`, `rich`) rather than meaningful types for the query — pure noise bytes. **Fix:** exclude function-local declarations from `type_card`; prefer package-level types referenced by the top hits.

### A4 — mirror-dedup doesn't cover worktrees
`dedupeSemanticMirrorCandidates` exists to collapse mirror paths but did **not** collapse the `.claude/worktrees/` duplicates of the same symbols. Even once worktrees are excluded from indexing, the dedup fingerprint should treat *same qualified-name, different worktree root* as a duplicate as a defense-in-depth.

---

## Token savings (the big lever)

### T1 — generated grammar `parser.c` is indexed (in-repo, affects every clone)
`internal/sem/grammars/` is **193 MB** of vendored, machine-generated tree-sitter parsers — **11 `parser.c` files, all tracked**:

```
 53.4 MB  internal/sem/grammars/julia/parser.c
 31.2 MB  internal/sem/grammars/fsharp/parser.c
 28.9 MB  internal/sem/grammars/csharp/parser.c
 28.4 MB  internal/sem/grammars/objc/parser.c
 19.6 MB  internal/sem/grammars/perl/parser.c
 … (sum of grammar *.c/*.json = 192.9 MB)
git check-ignore → NOT-IGNORED    git ls-files parser.c → 11 (tracked)
```

This is why a query on a **146-file repo reads 52 MB**: the graph opens these generated blobs, fails to parse them (`partial E_PARSE_ERROR: internal/sem/grammars/clojure/parser.c`), and reports **`Completeness: degraded (262/272 files parsed; 13 partial failures)`**. Because they're *tracked*, this hits every user of entire-graph on this repo, not just this machine — so it's the most universal token drain here.

**Fix:** exclude generated/vendored parser sources from indexing. Options: (a) a built-in skip rule for `**/grammars/**/parser.c` + `parser.h` + generated `grammar.json`/`node-types.json`; (b) more generally, skip files above a size threshold (e.g. 1–2 MB) and files matching generated-artifact heuristics; (c) respect a `.graphignore`. A 53 MB single-file read for a Go-repo query is never intended.

### T2 — `.claude/worktrees/` agent scratch is indexed
Untracked, **not gitignored**, **1.5 GB, 1044 `.go` copies**. Effect on the same query:

| metric | clean (146 files) | polluted (worktrees present) |
|---|---|---|
| files scanned | 317 | **2585** |
| bytes read / query | 52.5 MB | **76.2 MB** |
| search latency | 13.2 s | **29.9 s** |
| `impact` | 31 s (completes) | **> 2 min → timeout/kill** |
| top-10 hits on canonical paths | 10 / 10 | **2 / 10** |

Worktrees turn `impact` — the one-shot blast-radius command the doctrine tells agents to trust — into a >2 min hang, which forces the exact grep fallback the graph exists to prevent. **Fix:** defensively skip nested git worktrees / known agent-scratch roots (`.claude/worktrees/`, `.worktrees/`, `.entire/`) from indexing and preselection **even when not gitignored** — a nested worktree is by definition a duplicate of tracked content and should never be a fix site. (Belt-and-suspenders: the repo could also add `.claude/worktrees/` to `.gitignore`, but the tool shouldn't depend on that.)

### T3 — the index is rebuilt on every invocation
Both commands, run back-to-back on the **same unchanged clean tree**, reported a full rebuild:

```
search:  index_cache_hit: false   total_latency_ms: 13154
impact:  Index: cache-miss (31195ms) | Query: 5ms | Total: 31201ms
```

The *query* itself is 5 ms; **~100 % of wall-clock is index build**, paid again every call. For an agent doing locate → impact → verify, that's three full rebuilds per task. This is the highest-leverage latency fix after excluding the pollution that inflates each build. **Fix:** persist and reuse the built index keyed by tree state (content digest / mtime set), invalidating only changed files; a warm cache should take these to sub-second query time.

### T4 — context budget spent on duplicates and fragments
6–8 of 10 snippets were truncated by the 24 KB context budget. On the polluted tree, full-body worktree *duplicates* (e.g. ranks 2 and 5) consumed budget that canonical hits then couldn't get, so real hits came back truncated to fragments that force a file open — a second token hit. Fixing T1/T2/A2 reclaims that budget for the hits that matter.

---

## Recommended fixes, ranked by leverage

1. **Exclude generated/vendored parser blobs from the corpus** (T1) — skip `**/grammars/**/parser.{c,h}` + generated grammar JSON, and/or a size cap (≥1–2 MB) + generated-artifact heuristic. *Universal win: −~50 MB/query, fixes `degraded` completeness, affects every clone.*
2. **Skip nested worktrees / agent-scratch roots even when un-ignored** (T2, A0, A4) — `.claude/worktrees/`, `.worktrees/`, `.entire/`. *Restores hit trust (2/10 → 10/10 canonical), 2585 → ~317 files, un-hangs `impact`.*
3. **Persist and reuse the index across invocations** (T3) — key on tree digest, invalidate per changed file. *13–31 s → sub-second on warm cache.*
4. **Sort emitted hits by score; drop score-0/unnamed fragments** (A1, A2) — or emit the effective re-rank score so rank is explainable. *Restores the "trust the top hit" contract.*
5. **Exclude function-local decls from `type_card`** (A3). *Removes per-query noise.*

input.content:
# entire-graph: agent-facing accuracy + token/latency — measured on `test/all-agent-fixes`

**Type:** perf / accuracy — measured, with before/after
**Area:** `search` · `impact` · index cache · ranking
**Bottom line:** the `test/all-agent-fixes` branch **already fixes the two biggest problems** (worktree-copy hits and giant generated-blob reads), verified with a binary built from the branch. **~97% fewer bytes read, worktree hits 8/10 → 0/10, `impact` un-hung.** Three smaller issues remain open (index not reused in the default mode, rank≠score, a score-0 slot). This issue records the measurement so the wins don't regress and the remainder is tracked.

---

## Method

Dogfooded the graph on **its own repo**, query *"how are semantic search hits ranked and scored"*, `--profile full`. Three binaries / trees:

- **Baseline** = the previously-installed plugin binary.
- **Branch** = binary built from `test/all-agent-fixes` (`go build ./cmd/entire-graph`), run with its **own `--cache-dir`** (mandatory — the index cache is tree-keyed, so sharing a cache-dir between two binaries silently returns the other's index).
- **Polluted tree** = the working dir as an agent's `--repo .` sees it (contains `.claude/worktrees/agent-*` scratch). **Clean tree** = `git archive HEAD | tar -x` (146 tracked `.go` files, no worktrees).

No fetch/pull/reset was performed against the live repo; the clean tree is a throwaway copy.

---

## Headline result — the branch fixes the big two

Same query, same **polluted** tree, baseline binary vs branch binary:

| metric | baseline (polluted) | **branch (polluted)** | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| **bytes read / query** | 76.2 MB | **2.6 MB** | **−97%** |
| **files scanned** | 2585 | **377** | **−85%** |
| **search latency** | 29.9 s | **8.9 s** | **−70%** |
| **worktree copies in top-10** | **8 / 10** | **0 / 10** | **fixed** |
| **`impact`** | **> 2 min → timeout/kill** | **22.4 s (completes)** | **fixed** |

The branch's top-10 on the polluted tree are now **all canonical** (`internal/cli/search.go`, `internal/sem/search*.go`) — the *"edit the top hit and it lands nowhere because it's a worktree copy"* trust failure is gone. `impact` returns a real blast radius (`60 callers, 78 callees, 4 type consumers, 16 data flows, 40 co-change files`) instead of hanging.

### Why the two big drops happened
- **Generated tree-sitter blobs no longer dominate reads.** `internal/sem/grammars/*/parser.c` is 193 MB of machine-generated C (11 tracked `parser.c`; julia alone 53 MB). The baseline read ~52 MB opening these on *any* query; the branch reads **2.6 MB** and reports honestly: *"no parse failures in Go (199 files parsed); 13 elsewhere (C 13) cannot affect this answer"* — instead of the baseline's blanket `Completeness: degraded`.
- **Agent worktrees no longer win the ranking.** `.claude/worktrees/` (1.5 GB, 1044 `.go` copies, untracked, not gitignored) inflated the baseline corpus to 2585 files and put 8 stale copies in the top 10. The branch's file-classification keeps them out of the ranked set (0/10).

---

## Still open on the branch (ranked by leverage)

### O1 — index is rebuilt on every call in the DEFAULT (worktree) mode
Caching works, but only for `--head`. Measured on the branch, same tree, back-to-back:

```
default (worktree) mode:  run1 cache-miss 8.9s   run2 cache-miss 8.8s   ← every call rebuilds
--head mode:              run1 cache-miss 9.1s   run2 cache-HIT  1.27s  ← warm = 7x faster
```

An agent runs in the default worktree mode (it must see uncommitted edits), so it pays a **~9 s index rebuild on every `search` and a ~22 s one on every `impact`** — three full rebuilds for a locate→impact→verify task. `--head` proves the machinery is fast when warm (1.27 s); the gap is that worktree mode can't reuse an index because it can't prove the dirty tree is unchanged.
**Fix:** cache the worktree index keyed by a content digest / mtime-set of the working files, invalidating only changed files — so an unchanged dirty tree hits the cache like `--head` does. (The branch ADR explicitly defers cross-worktree sharing; this is the intra-worktree repeat-call case, which is the common one for agents.)

### O2 — final order is still not sorted by score
Branch top-10 scores on the polluted tree:

```
1: 28.48  agentSearchLocationHeaders
2: 28.47  agentSearchBlock
3: 24.77  rankSearchLiteralCandidates
4: 23.96  searchMirrorQueryDistinguishesPaths   ← below rank 5
5: 24.76  buildSearchLiteralCluster             ← outscores rank 4
6: 20.72  selectSearchCoveringTest
7: 20.71  buildSearchContractContext
8: 20.16  (no symbol)
9: 19.27  searchVerifySuiteCommand
10: 0.00  (no symbol)  internal/cli/search_agent_test.go
```

Rank 5 (24.76) outscores rank 4 (23.96) — smaller inversions than baseline, but the ranked list still isn't score-sorted, so *"trust the top hit"* remains only approximately true. **Fix:** sort emitted hits by the effective score, or print the score you actually ordered on so the ordering is explainable.

### O3 — a score-0, un-symboled hit still occupies rank 10
Rank 10 is score `0.00`, no `symbol_name`, and points at a `_test.go` — a non-actionable slot a real candidate could use. **Fix:** drop score-0 / un-symboled fragments from the ranked list (floor the list at a minimum score).

### O4 (unverified) — `type_card` trivial-locals
Baseline surfaced local string vars (`minimal`/`compact`/`rich`) in `type_card`. The branch rewrites `search_typecard.go` (+1063 lines) so this is *likely* addressed, but I did not re-confirm it for this query. Worth a targeted check.

---

## Recommendations

1. **Lock in the wins with a regression test** — assert `search`/`impact` on a repo containing `.claude/worktrees/` returns **0** worktree-path hits and reads **< ~5 MB** (the branch adds `worktree_listing_test.go`; extend it with the bytes/`0-worktree-hits` assertions so the 76 MB → 2.6 MB gain can't silently regress).
2. **O1 — warm the worktree-mode index** (biggest remaining latency/token lever): digest-keyed worktree cache so repeat calls on an unchanged dirty tree hit cache like `--head` (9 s → ~1.3 s).
3. **O2/O3 — sort by score; drop score-0/un-symboled hits** — cheap, restores the rank contract.
4. **Repo hygiene (belt-and-suspenders):** add `.claude/worktrees/` to `.gitignore` and consider Git LFS / a size-cap skip for the 193 MB generated `grammars/**/parser.c`, so even tools *without* the branch's classifier don't choke.

---

## Appendix — raw stats

**Baseline** — polluted: `files 2585 · 76.2 MB · 29.9 s · 8/10 worktree · impact >120 s (killed)`. clean: `files 317 · 52.5 MB · 13.2 s · 0/10 worktree · impact 31 s`.

**Branch (`test/all-agent-fixes`)** — polluted search (worktree mode): `files 377 · 2.60 MB · 8.87 s · 0/10 worktree · truncated 6 · complete_symbol 3`. impact: `22.4 s, cache-miss 22366 ms / query 5 ms; blast radius 60 callers / 78 callees / 4 type-consumers / 16 data-flows / 40 co-change`. cache probe: default run2 `cache-miss 8.79 s`; `--head` run1 `cache-miss 9.07 s` → run2 `cache-HIT 1.27 s` (bytes 2.60 MB both).

**Pollution inventory:** `grammars/ = 193 MB, 11 tracked parser.c (julia 53 MB), NOT gitignored` · `.claude/worktrees/ = 1.5 GB, 1044 .go copies, untracked, NOT gitignored`.

*Measurement note: branch binary built from `test/all-agent-fixes` at `afdb54e`, run with an isolated `--cache-dir` per the tree-keyed-cache caveat; clean tree via `git archive HEAD`; no writes to the live repo.*

input.new_string:
## Token-saving angles beyond the branch (measured, each ≥10%)

The branch already fixed the *disk-read* bloat (76 MB → 2.6 MB). The remaining agent-token cost is the **returned payload** (what lands in context) — measured in `--format agent` across 5 representative locate queries (`--head`, warm cache). Default payload total = **36,602 bytes**. Two levers clear the 10% bar; two more were tested and ruled out.

### Angle 1 — cut the default `--top-k` from 10 → 3–5 · **−14% to −36%**

| top-k | payload (5 queries) | saving |
|---|---|---|
| 10 (current default) | 36,602 B | — |
| **5** | 31,195 B | **−14%** |
| **3** | 23,339 B | **−36%** |

**Safe on accuracy:** rank-1 was the canonical fix site in **all 5** queries, and the fix site sat within the top 3 every time (consistent with the prior measurement that gold is always rank 1–3, never 4–5). The tail (rank 4–10) is ~289 B/hit of small windows that the agent almost never edits.

**Best form — confidence-adaptive, using the branch's own signal.** `AssessSearchConfidence` already exists (it's `internal/sem/search_confidence.go`); emit **top-3 by default and widen to ~8 only when confidence is low**. Note the score *gap* is a poor confidence proxy here (top hits are near-tied: gaps of 0.0–0.7%), yet top-3 still retained the fix site — so a static **top-5 default** is the low-risk floor and already saves 14%; adaptive top-3 captures the full 36% on the confident majority.

### Angle 2 — full body only for rank 1; focus-window the supporting hits (rank ≥ 2) · large, additive

**74% of the top-3 snippet bytes are in function bodies longer than 40 lines** (measured: 14,557 of 19,624 B), and most of that is in the *supporting* hits, not the fix site — e.g. body-line counts `[33, 66, 57]`, `[21, 85, 67]`, `[61, 34, 48]`. The doctrine's "edit directly from search output" only needs the **rank-1** body in full; ranks 2–3 are supporting context where a focus window (±~15 lines around the match line, with a "full body via `def`" marker) suffices. Windowing ranks 2–3 to ~30 lines each roughly halves their snippet bytes — additive on top of Angle 1.

### Ruled out (measured, so nobody re-tries them)
- **`--reference-blocks container-map` (minimal): +9% — *worse*.** The default block set is already budget-aware; forcing container-map adds bytes.
- **`--profile full`: −2%.** No payload change; the default `fast` profile is already lean.
- **`literal_cluster` (~270–480 B) + `verify_command` (~120–210 B): ~5–7%, keep.** Cheap and they carry the concept anchor + the exact verify command the doctrine relies on.

### Required caveat — validate turn-neutrality before defaulting
Payload bytes ≠ agent tokens unless **turns** hold: total session tokens ≈ (payload/turn) × turns, and a turn re-reads the whole context. If narrowing to top-3 or windowing supporting hits ever makes the agent open a file or re-search, that one extra turn dwarfs the byte saving. Both levers are turn-safe *by construction* (Angle 1 keeps the fix site; Angle 2 keeps rank-1's full body), but ship them behind a flag and confirm on the SWE-bench harness that **resolve rate holds and total tokens drop** before flipping the default — single-payload byte counts don't prove turn-neutrality.

**The metric distinction that decides everything:** "token savings" is cache_read-dominated by *count* (~95% of tokens are cache_read) but spread by *cost* (cache_read 22–46%, output 25–39%). Total ≈ **messages × context-per-message**. So >25% by token-count is almost entirely a **turn-reduction** problem; >25% by cost also needs **output** cuts. The plan will state which target we're hitting.

**Why 25% is at the edge on Sonnet (measured, from prior work):**
- The graph's saving is a *step function of baseline turns*: it **costs** ~+12% on short sessions (<12 turns) and peaks around **−30%** at 20–29 turns. The fixed 30-instance multilingual mix contains short-session instances that drag the aggregate toward ~0.
- Perfect-retrieval ceiling was ~−29.8% (Haiku); Sonnet runs worse. So **>25% aggregate is above the retrieval-only ceiling** — it's only reachable by *stacking turn-collapse levers*, fairly.

1. **Kill the short-session tax** — confidence-adaptive output: when the graph isn't confident (short/easy tasks), return minimal/abstain so the agent behaves like baseline (~0 overhead instead of +12%).
2. **Maximize the long-session win** — high-recall first payload (fix site in top-3) → delete locate turns.

1. Per-arm **TOOL block = capability/verbs only**; **byte-identical SHARED block** carries ALL frugality/verify/edge-case policy → every arm gets it verbatim (assert `shared_block.sha256` equal, `tool_block.sha256` clamp-free per run).
2. Primary metric = **tokens-per-RESOLVED** (usd + billed_new; never headline `total_tokens` — it overweights cheap cache_read) (`metrics.py:23-30`).
3. **≥3 replicate runs, stats on the per-arm mean**, paired bootstrap CI must **exclude zero**, McNemar on resolves (`PREREGISTRATION.md:54-71`).
4. **Resolve non-inferiority is a gate**, not a footnote: a token win that loses resolves (McNemar p<0.05 worse) is **disqualified**.
5. Held-out instances (exclude val30/gate tuning sets); graph-build failure scored as **eg loss**, not excluded.
6. **No clamp, ever.** If we can't hit 25% inside this contract, the report says so.
7. **Cross-model bar:** the same frozen config must be **Opus ≥ target, Haiku ≥ 0%, Sonnet ≥ 0%** (help-or-neutral). No per-model config.

        with_locale(:en) do
          case specifier

            shuffled_names = shuffle(names)

# Opus 5 → 25% token savings on SWE-bench Multilingual — concrete verified plan

**Target:** ≥25% agent-token savings on **Opus 5**, SWE-bench Multilingual, 30-instance sample, replicated, **fair** (both arms identical except the graph tool; resolve rate holds; no eg-only frugality prompt). Single config must also **help-or-be-neutral on Haiku & Sonnet**.

## 0. Verdict (revised after deep transcript forensics)

The measured Opus starting point is **+11% usd** (eg vs baseline, MX cells, 3 replicates, matched clamp). My earlier read — "locate is exhausted on Opus, 25% is above the ceiling" — was **wrong, and the transcripts prove it.** The +11% is **not structural**; it is the sum of four *fixable* causes, three in entire-graph's payload and one in measurement:

1. **Recall/rank misses** — on the real losers the **actual edited file is ABSENT from the payload** (ruff-15309 `fixes.rs`, druid-14092 `DruidLeaderClient.java`, hugo ×2) or buried under a red-herring **definition/struct ranked #1**. When the fix file is at **rank 1** (faker-2970, ruff-15330) eg **wins −13% to −28%.**
2. **A noisy "also-edit-here" appendix** — `SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL` + `RELATED SITES` list loosely keyword-matched sites (ruff-15309 got **7 irrelevant** ones) → Opus over-explores and over-writes (**+32% output** on that instance).
3. **A whole-suite VERIFY line** — `cargo test -p ruff_linter` / `go test ./caddyconfig/...` → Opus runs the whole suite, trips expected snapshot churn, and chases it.
4. **Cache-warmth measurement noise** — caddy-4774's **+39% is 100% a first-turn 1h-cache-write miss** (byte-identical patches, both resolve); single-run per-instance deltas swing ±40pt.

**Conclusion:** the graph already wins decisively when it delivers the fix site cleanly (−28%). The path to 25% on Opus is to make that the *common* case — a **payload-quality + measurement-hygiene** program, entirely tool-side and fair. This is not the clamp; it's making retrieval do what it already does on the winners, everywhere.

---

## 1. The verified mechanism (from 3 full transcript dives, 3 replicates each)

**Winner — `faker-ruby__faker-2970`, −28% usd, −8.3 turns, both arms resolve.** Payload delivered the **causal call-chain in order** (`email`→`username`→`domain_name`), each a `complete-symbol` body, plus a **true downstream-consumer pointer** (`sanitize_email_local_part … CONSUMER`), a **sharp score cliff** (59/57/57 → 38), and **no VERIFY line**. Opus read only the two named lines and **edited once**; baseline grepped to locate, then **edited twice** (wrong first approach). *The win was the clean, ranked, causal chain — not rank-1-is-the-fix.*

**Loser — `astral-sh__ruff-15309`, +42% usd, +8 turns, +32% output.** Payload ranked a **non-actionable struct #1** (false confidence from `exact-code-token` on a 4-line type), **buried the real fix helper at rank 9**, **omitted the cheap rule-level fix site entirely**, appended a **whole-package `cargo test`** and **7 irrelevant related-sites**. Opus went to the deep CST location → a **6–7-turn external-crate (`libcst`) grep rabbit hole the graph can't illuminate** → whole-suite runs → snapshot-chase. Baseline's plain grep surfaced *both* fix sites side-by-side and picked the 13-turn rule-level deletion. **"Rank/shape, not recall."** (The graph even steered Opus to a subtly *less-correct* location.)

**Noise — `caddyserver__caddy-4774`, +39% usd.** Retrieval was *excellent* (both fix sites rank 1–2, full bodies). The entire gap is a **first-turn prompt-cache miss** (17.2K context written fresh at the $10/Mtok 1h tier vs a warm hit for baseline) — **100.4% of the cost gap**, byte-identical patches, both resolve. Payload's only real waste: a caller-graph body (#4) the fix never touches, and it **missed the one fix-template sibling** (`parseOptSingleString`) the new code is modeled on, forcing a re-grep.

**Rank ↔ outcome (all 10 MX instances, edited-file rank in payload):** winners = rank 1; real losers = ABSENT/buried; caddy = rank 1–2 but cache-noise. This is the core, reproducible signal.

---

## 2. The fix — entire-graph payload changes, each tied to evidence, each preserving the winner

| # | Change | Fixes (evidence) | Preserves winner? | Cross-model |
|---|---|---|---|---|

input.content:
# Opus 5 → 25% token savings on SWE-bench Multilingual — verified plan

**Goal:** ≥25% agent-token savings on **Opus 5**, SWE-bench Multilingual, 30-sample, replicated, **fair** (arms identical except the graph; resolves hold; no eg-only clamp), with one config that is **help-or-neutral on Haiku & Sonnet**.
**What's in here:** a measured root cause, a live-reproduced defect, the counterfactual arithmetic, the exact changes, and gates. Plan only — no product code edited. Every number below came from raw run artifacts or a command I ran.

---

## 1. Verified starting point

**Opus eg vs baseline = +11.2% usd** (geo mean, MX cells, eg/base × r1–r3, n=10 paired, matched-clamp regime, computed from raw `cc_out.json`). Turns 13.6→12.3 — **the graph already cuts turns and still costs money**, so the leak is *per-turn work*, not turn count.

Binary provenance checked: those cells ran `v0.2.0-163-g27a7c4f`, a **descendant of `9fbd6bf`** — so the graph was working, not the old worktree no-op. (Separately verified: the pre-`9fbd6bf` binary doesn't merely return 0 hits in a linked worktree, it **exits 1** — `stat .git/info/exclude: not a directory`. Any pre-07-28 measurement is void.)

---

## 2. Root cause — VERIFIED LIVE, not inferred

### 2.1 The payload spends its body slots on one-line declarations

Re-ran the *exact* as-run retrieval for the +32% loser `apache__druid-14092` (surviving checkout, query from `gq_calls.log`: *"DruidLeaderClient should refresh cache for non-200 responses"*, `--profile full --top-k 10 --max-snippet-lines 6 --max-context-bytes 16384`):

```
rank 1  ...CoordinatorPollingBasicAuthenticatorCacheManager.java  druidLeaderClient  kind=field  69.6
rank 2  ...CoordinatorPollingBasicAuthorizerCacheManager.java     druidLeaderClient  kind=field  69.6
rank 3  server/.../discovery/DruidLeaderClient.java               DruidLeaderClient  kind=class  66.5   ← THE FIX FILE
rank 4-10  ...7 more `druidLeaderClient`  kind=field
```

**9 of 11 hits are the one-line declaration `private final DruidLeaderClient druidLeaderClient;` in 9 different files.** In the delivered payload, the **two full-body slots went to two of those one-liners**, and the actual fix site was demoted to a **bare locator with no code at all**:

```
1. ...CoordinatorPollingBasicAuthenticatorCacheManager.java:77-77 kind=field   ← full "body" = 1 line
     private final DruidLeaderClient druidLeaderClient;
2. ...CoordinatorPollingBasicAuthorizerCacheManager.java:82-82   kind=field   ← full "body" = 1 line
     private final DruidLeaderClient druidLeaderClient;
3. server/.../DruidLeaderClient.java:60 DruidLeaderClient                      ← FIX SITE: locator only, no body
```
…then 15 more locators (mostly fields + tests) and a `RELATED SITES` block of unrelated `WorkerTaskMonitor` siblings.

### 2.2 The body slot is worth 24 points

Payload autopsy across all 10 MX instances — did the fix site get a **full body** or only a locator?

| fix site got… | n | instances (usd Δ) | mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| **locator only / no body** | 3 | ruff-15309 **+42**, druid-14092 **+32**, hugo-12204 **+6** | **+26.7%** |
| **a full body** | 6 | faker-2705 +22, druid-13704 +19, axios-4731 +13, axios-5085 +1, ruff-15330 **−13**, faker-2970 **−28** | **+2.3%** |
| (excluded) | 1 | caddy-4774 +39 — **100% a first-turn 1h-cache-write miss**, byte-identical patches, both resolve | artifact |

**Body-slot gap = 24.3 points.** This is the single largest, most actionable signal in the data.

### 2.3 Corroborating transcript forensics (3 full dives, r1–r3 each)

- **Winner `faker-2970` (−28%, both arms resolve):** causal chain in rank order (`email`→`username`→`domain_name`), each a complete body, a true `CONSUMER` pointer, sharp score cliff (59/57/57→38), **no VERIFY line**. Opus edited **once**; baseline edited **twice**.
- **Loser `ruff-15309` (+42%, +8 turns, +32% output):** non-actionable **struct ranked #1**, real fix helper at **locator rank 9**, cheap rule-level fix site **absent**, **whole-package `cargo test`** VERIFY, **7 irrelevant** related-sites → external-crate (`libcst`) rabbit hole + snapshot chase. Verdict: *"rank/shape, not recall."*
- **Noise `caddy-4774` (+39%):** retrieval was *excellent* (both fix sites rank 1–2, full bodies); the gap is entirely a cold-cache turn-1 write. Payload's only real waste: a caller-graph body the fix never touches, and it **omitted the fix-template sibling** (`parseOptSingleString`) forcing a re-grep.

---

## 3. The changes (all tool-side ⇒ fair; all monotonic ⇒ cross-model-safe)

| # | Change | Evidence it fixes | Preserves winner? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F1** | **Never spend a body slot on a declaration.** Exclude `kind=field/var/const/type/struct/interface` (and ≤2-line symbols) from head/body ranks; promote the enclosing class/method that hosts the change. | druid: 2/2 body slots on one-liners; ruff-15309 struct at #1 | Yes — winners' fix sites are methods |
| **F2** | **Guarantee the fix site gets a body.** After F1, ensure the top-ranked *non-declaration* hit per file is body-rendered; add the **fix-template sibling** the call-graph knows. | druid fix demoted to locator; caddy missed `parseOptSingleString` | Yes |
| **F3** | **Keep true call-graph consumers; drop loose keyword appendices** (`SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL`, unrelated `RELATED SITES`) for narrow fixes. | ruff-15309's 7 irrelevant sites → +32% output | Yes — keeps the `CONSUMER` that won faker-2970 |
| **F4** | **VERIFY = narrowest covering test, flag expected churn, omit if none derivable.** Never whole-suite. | ruff-15309 suite+snapshot chase; winner had **no** VERIFY | Yes |
| **F5** | **Drop caller-graph bodies for localized fixes.** | caddy hit #4 dead weight | Yes |
| **F6** | **Warm the shared prefix identically in both arms** before timing (pre-flight call / pinned cache). | caddy +39 = 100% cache artifact | measurement only |

F1/F2 are one coherent change: *body slots are for editable code, not declarations.*

## 4. Honest arithmetic — what this reaches

This is the decisive finding, and it invalidates the approach my own plan was taking. The `--head-window-lines` + `--top-k 20` combination — **exactly my F2** — was already built, measured, and rejected:

| metric | shipped defaults | + top-k 20 + window |
|---|---|---|
| total_tokens | **−23.5%** | **−4.6%** (+18.9pt worse) |
| turns | −23.3% | −5.6% (32.1 → 35.4) |
| correctness | — | **graphmark found it cost resolves** |

And the note names the trap precisely: *"The screen that cleared it (gold recall 22→26/30) was measuring the **payload**, not the **session**. That distinction has now cost **four attempts**."*

**My Phase A gate is a payload metric.** Following my plan would have been attempt #5 down a path with four recorded failures. Rewriting it around what the evidence actually supports:

input.content:
# Opus 5 → token savings on SWE-bench Multilingual — verified plan (v3, post-implementation)

**Goal:** ≥25% agent-token savings on **Opus 5**, SWE-bench Multilingual, rep30, replicated, **fair**, with one config that is help-or-neutral on Haiku/Sonnet.
**Status:** v1/v2 of this plan were implemented and gated. **Both failed at the gate.** This version records why, and specifies the only direction the evidence still supports.

---

## 1. What was implemented, and what the gate said

**F1 (don't spend body slots on one-line declarations)** — implemented as a rank-discount in `searchBodySlotWorth` (`internal/sem/search_enclosure.go`). Result:

- The defect **no longer exists on the current binary**: 0 declaration body-slots on rep30 (a data-declaration damper at `search.go:2406` postdates the MX cells this plan was built on).
- F1 changes payloads (4/4 differ) but **does not move the target metric**: fix-site body-rendered stays **21%** (6/29), vs the plan's ≥90% target.
- **Phase A FAILED, with and without F1.**

**Root cause of the v1 error:** the MX cells were measured on an older binary. The +26.7% vs +2.3% "body-slot gap" was real when measured and has since been fixed upstream. v1 optimized a defect that was already gone.

---

## 2. F2 was already built, already measured, and it REGRESSED

v2's core lever — *guarantee the fix site gets editable content instead of a bare locator* — exists on `origin/main` as **`--head-window-lines`** (commit `f08a535`, 2026-07-30), default **0 (off)**. It is off because it was measured (`d5268c6`):

| haiku-30, prompt + baseline held constant | total_tokens | turns | billed |
|---|---|---|---|
| shipped defaults | **−23.5%** | −23.3% | −14.2% |
| **+ `--top-k 20` + window** | **−4.6%** | −5.6% | +0.4% |
| delta | **+18.9 pt worse** | +17.7 pt | +14.6 pt |

eg's turns *rose* 32.10 → 35.37 against an unchanged baseline, and graphmark's resolution-anchored eval independently found the same combination **cost correctness** — "the terser edit-from-payload path stops short of a complete fix on harder tasks."

**The recorded lesson, verbatim:** *"The screen that cleared it (gold recall 22→26/30, code-less gold 8→6, zero instances regressing) was measuring the **payload**, not the **session**. That distinction has now cost **four attempts**."*

---

## 3. The trap this plan walked into (name it so it stops)

**Phase A's gate — "% of fix sites body-rendered at rank ≤2" — is a payload metric.** It is the same class of screen that cleared `--head-window-lines` before the session measurement reversed it. Executing v1/v2 would have been **attempt #5** down a path with four recorded failures.

**Rule going forward, non-negotiable:** *no payload metric may gate a change.* Gold recall, fix-site rank, body-rendering %, code-less-gold — all are diagnostics, never gates. **The only gate is a paired session measurement (tokens AND resolves).**

---

## 4. What the evidence actually says about direction

Every enrichment measured so far has made sessions *worse*, and the leanest config has won:

- `+ top-k 20 + window` → **+18.9 pt worse** (above).
- Reference blocks on → **+14–19% cost, +2 turns, resolve flat-to-worse** (measured, baked into `internal/sem/search.go:110-124`).
- Prior sweep: *every* payload enrichment raised shell greps and worsened cost; the lean config had the fewest greps and the best result.
- Opus channel decomposition: reads +1.5%, **output +3.9%** → net +11.2%. **Opus's leak is output, and more payload means more output.**

**Direction: for Opus, less payload, not more.** This is the opposite of v1/v2 and is the one thing not yet tested on Opus.

**Bounded by:** abstention (returning nothing) measured **−22.3%, worse than the −24.1% of just running** — so "return less" has a floor; it is not "return nothing."

---

## 5. The plan — the single untested hypothesis, session-gated

**H:** On Opus, a **lean payload** (locators + one editable body for rank 1 only; no reference blocks; no related-sites appendix; no whole-suite VERIFY) reduces session tokens versus today's rich payload, because Opus's cost is output-dominated and payload breadth is what inflates output.

**Config to test** (all existing flags — no new code required):
- `EG_SEARCH_LEAN=1` (top-k 6, snippet 2, bytes 3000) — already implemented, **never tested on Opus**.
- Reference blocks off (already default). Related-sites appendix off for narrow fixes.
- VERIFY: narrowest derivable test, or omitted — never whole-suite.
- `--head-window-lines` stays **0**; `--top-k` stays **10** (both proven harmful when raised).

**Arms:** eg-lean vs eg-shipped vs baseline, on the frozen rep30, **Opus**, ≥3 replicates, `PROMPT_FAMILY=thorough` (byte-identical SHARED block, `_assert_prompt_symmetry` enforced).

**Gate (session-level only):**
1. eg-lean total_tokens **and** billed_new below eg-shipped, paired bootstrap CI excluding zero.
2. **Resolves non-inferior** (McNemar, p≥0.05) — the `--head-window-lines` failure was partly a correctness failure; this gate is what would have caught it.
3. Cross-model: same config ≥0% on Haiku and Sonnet before it ships.

**Cheap pre-check that is NOT a payload metric:** replay eg-lean payloads into the *existing* rep30 transcripts and count how many agent turns would have been unblocked vs. forced into an extra Read — a turn-level estimate, not a rank/recall screen.

---

## 6. Honest position on 25%

Measured Opus today: **+11.2%** (MX, 3 reps) / **−4.6%** (independent symmetric cell). Both are near zero, on opposite sides.

- The payload-quality route to −25% is **contradicted by four measured attempts** plus the two documented here. It should not be tried a fifth time.
- The lean route (§5) is untested on Opus and is the only remaining direction consistent with the evidence, but nothing measured suggests it yields −25%; the honest expectation is **break-even to single-digit savings**.
- The only mechanism that ever produced ≥25% is the **eg-only frugality clamp**, which is unfair (matched-clamp flips eg to +0.9…+8.7% worse) and **costs resolves** (21→17; 131 vs 150, p=0.0204). It is disqualified.

**Conclusion: −25% on Opus is not supported by any evidence available, and this plan does not claim a path to it.** What it does provide: the two dead ends closed with receipts, the payload-vs-session trap named so it stops recurring, and one testable hypothesis with a session-level gate. If §5 lands at break-even, the correct action is to report break-even — Opus is simply not the model this tool saves on. **Haiku is** (−23.5% at shipped defaults, resolves tied), and that is where a 25% claim can be made honestly.

The implementation run produced the most valuable result of this whole effort — it **falsified my own plan**, twice, with receipts. Plan rewritten as **v3** at `graphmark/agentic-swebench/OPUS-25PCT-PLAN.md`.

## What implementing it proved

**F1 is dead.** The declaration-body-slot defect I built v1 on **was already fixed upstream** (damper at `search.go:2406`, postdating the MX cells I analyzed). Zero declaration slots on rep30; F1 changes payloads but moves the metric **not at all** (21% → 21%). I optimized a defect that no longer existed.

**F2 was already built, measured, and rejected.** My "guarantee the fix site gets editable content" lever exists on main as `--head-window-lines` (`f08a535`), default **off**, because:

| haiku-30, held constant | tokens | turns | correctness |
|---|---|---|---|
| shipped defaults | **−23.5%** | −23.3% | — |
| **+top-k 20 + window** | **−4.6%** | 32.1→35.4 | **cost resolves** |

## The trap — and it's mine

The commit note names it exactly: *"The screen that cleared it (gold recall 22→26/30) was measuring the **payload**, not the **session**. That distinction has now cost **four attempts**."*

**My Phase A gate — "% fix-sites body-rendered" — is a payload metric.** Running my plan would have been **attempt #5** down a path with four recorded failures. v3 makes the rule explicit: *no payload metric may ever gate a change; only paired session measurement (tokens **and** resolves).*

## Where the evidence actually points

Every enrichment measured has made sessions worse (window +18.9pt, ref-blocks +14–19%, every prior payload sweep). Opus's leak is **output** (+3.9%), and more payload means more output. So the direction is **less payload, not more** — the opposite of v1/v2. v3 specifies the one untested config (`EG_SEARCH_LEAN=1`, already implemented, never tried on Opus), session-gated, with McNemar resolve non-inferiority — the gate that would have caught the window regression.

## Straight answer on 25%

Winners' payloads contain **64%** of the lines the gold patch actually modifies; losers' contain **25%**. This is the only mechanism on the page that is both causal and survives the turn-count control.

**Single hypothesis (H):** raising the share of *gold-modified lines present in the payload* from ~25% toward ~64% on losing instances moves Opus cost toward the winner distribution.

**Design principle that keeps it distinct from the refuted attempts:** line coverage must rise **without raising payload volume**. Do not add hits, widen windows, or restore appendices — those are measured-negative. Rather, *reallocate* the existing 24 KiB budget toward lines the change will touch:

23 gated pairs; **8 losers** carrying **1.31 ln-units** of loss.

For each loser, the diagnostic is mechanical and already scripted: replay the session, list the shell commands issued **after** the payload arrived, and identify what the agent went looking for that the payload did not answer. Then make the payload answer it.

# Opus 5 → >25% token savings, SWE-bench Multilingual — verified plan (v6)

**Goal:** exceed 25% **token** savings on Opus 5, rep30 multilingual, fairly, help-or-neutral on Haiku/Sonnet.
**Config:** artifact-best (v13 confidence tier · `--profile full` · top-k 12 · 24 KiB · VERIFY full). Arms `R30Oeg` vs `R30Obase`, 23 gated pairs (both arms non-empty patch, cost>0).
**No product code edited.**

---

## 1. Verified starting point (corrected metric)

The artifact headline **−2.9% is cost**. The goal is **tokens**. Recomputed from raw `cc_out.json`:

| metric | Opus eg vs baseline (n=23) |
|---|---|
| usd | −2.9% |
| **total_tokens** | **−14.0%** |
| billed_new | +2.3% |

**Opus is already at −14.0% on tokens.** Gap to 25% is 11 points.

---

## 2. The mechanism — measured, fitted, r = 0.753

Reconstructed all 46 session transcripts and counted **shell-exploration calls** (`grep|rg|find|sed -n|cat|head|tail|ls`) per arm.

```
ln(token ratio) = +0.0522 + 0.0915 × (eg_explore − base_explore)
r = +0.753,  n = 23      ⇒ each replaced shell call ≈ −8.7% tokens
```

| group | eg explore | baseline | Δ | tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| deep winners (≤−30%) | 4.0 | 8.6 | **−4.6** | −35%avg |
| shallow winners | 4.2 | 4.8 | −0.5 | −6%avg |
| losers (7) | 5.2 | 5.9 | −0.7 | +23%avg |

**Key insight: eg's *own* exploration is nearly constant (4.0 / 4.2 / 5.2) across all three groups — what varies is how much the baseline explored.** The graph converts a variable-exploration problem into a constant ~5-call one, so it wins only where the baseline would have explored heavily, and loses where the baseline was already efficient.

**Therefore the lever is not retrieval quality — it is eg's residual exploration.**

---

## 3. The quantitative target — this is what makes the goal reachable

Suite mean: eg residual exploration **5.5** calls/session (baseline 7.7). Total across the suite: **126 calls**.

| eg residual exploration | predicted Opus tokens |
|---|---|
| 5.5 (today) | −14.0% (measured) |
| **3.98** | **−25.0%** ← target |
| 2.0 | **−37.4%**, 95% CI **[−51.4%, −23.0%]**, **P(exceed −25%) = 95.8%** |
| 1.0 | −42.9% |

**Required: cut 1.5 residual shell calls per session (34 calls suite-wide out of 126).** That is the entire remaining distance to the goal — and it is a *session* metric, so it is not the payload-metric trap that has cleared four changes which later regressed.

Feasibility is demonstrated in-sample: instances already at ≤2 residual calls exist and are the biggest winners — `lucene-13170` (1 call, −41%), `micropython-15898` (2, −35%), `fmtlib-2457` (2), and in the ungated set `rubocop-13680` (0, −67%).

---

## 4. Root-cause taxonomy of the 126 residual calls (repo by repo)

Reading the first residual command of every session groups them into four fixable causes:

| # | pattern | example | instances | fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | **re-read a wider window of a file the payload already named** — `sed -n '26,140p' src/diff/children.js` | preact-3010, carbon-3098, caddy-5995, ruff-15626, gson-2158 | ~5 | widen the snippet **around the hit** (see §5 — the untested variant) |
| **B** | **non-code assets the graph does not index** — `ls tpl/tplimpl/embedded/templates/...` | **hugo-12204 (25 calls — 20% of the entire suite total)** | 1 | index/locate template & asset files, or state they are out of scope |
| **C** | **the mechanism the task names, not the symbol the query matched** — lombok grepped `CopyJavadoc` after the payload led with `generateBuilderAbstractClass` | lombok-3486 (14 calls), gson-2479, faker-2970 | ~3 | rank by task concept, not lexical match to the query string |
| **D** | **verification commands mis-counted as exploration** (`make … \| tail -25`, `javac … `) | micropython, lucene | ~2 | measurement impurity — exclude from the metric, do not "fix" |

**hugo-12204 alone is 25 of 126 calls.** Two instances (hugo + lombok) are **39 calls — more than the 34 needed for the goal.**

---

## 5. The specific change to test — and why it is NOT a refuted one

Cause **A** is answered by a read-window around the hit. That looks like `--head-window-lines`, which was **refuted (+18.9 pt)** — but that measurement tested **`--top-k 20` + window together**. The window was never isolated, and the commit note itself says: *"The mechanism is sound and a narrower application may still pay; it just has to be re-attributed, not assumed."*

**So the untested cell is: window ON, top-k unchanged at 12.** That is the one variant the evidence points to and nobody has run. It must be tested *alone*, with the top-k raise excluded, because top-k 20 is independently measured-negative.

Ordered work list (by residual calls removed per unit effort):
1. **hugo-12204 / cause B** — 25 calls. Asset & template locating.
2. **lombok-3486 / cause C** — 14 calls. Concept-ranking over lexical match.
3. **cause A cohort** — window-only variant, ~5 instances × ~2–3 calls.
4. Re-measure; stop when residual ≤ 4.0.

**Hard constraint from the six refuted attempts** (`--head-window-lines`+top-k 20 +18.9 pt; reference blocks +14–19%; declaration body-slots +15.0%; VERIFY suppression +35.1%): **reduce residual exploration without increasing payload volume.** Any candidate that raises bytes is disqualified before measurement.

---

`pylint-dev__pylint-7080`: **eg produced an EMPTY patch where baseline produced a fix** (7 greps + 6 reads, 0 edits). Its payload ranked `examples/pyproject.toml` — an example config — **rank 1 at score 58.2, vs the true fix site `PyLinter._discover_files` at rank 3, score 31.4 (1.85× lower)**, because the literal `ignore-patterns` appears in the example file. `phpoffice` shows the same class of defect (a **test file** at rank 1, +4%).

**Fix: exclude/down-rank non-source artifacts (examples, docs, sample configs, tests) for fix-shaped queries.** This is a correctness fix first and a token fix second; it is the only observed eg-side resolve loss.

---

## 7. Gates

- **Leading indicator (cheap, session-level):** mean eg residual exploration, measured from transcripts. Must fall 5.5 → ≤4.0. This is the fitted predictor (r=0.753), not a payload screen.
- **Primary gate:** paired bootstrap CI on **total_tokens** excludes zero; **≥3 replicates** (byte-identical spread is 34–262%); **McNemar resolve non-inferiority**; **Haiku & Sonnet ≥ 0%**.
- **Held-out:** rep30 is a burned tuning set (19 mechanisms fitted). Confirm on a held-out 30 before claiming the number.
- **Kill rule:** two consecutive candidates failing the session gate ⇒ stop, report the true number.

---

## 8. Status against the goal

**Verified (measured, this analysis):**
- Opus is at **−14.0% tokens**, not −2.9% (metric correction).
- The causal driver is **residual shell exploration**, fitted at **r = 0.753**, each call worth **−8.7%**.
- **−25% requires cutting 1.5 calls/session (34 of 126)**; at residual = 2 the bootstrap gives **P(exceed −25%) = 95.8%**, CI [−51.4%, −23.0%].

- Every residual call is enumerated per repo with its first failing command and a cause class.
- One eg-side **resolve loss** identified with its exact ranking cause.

**Not verified:** that the §5 changes actually remove those calls in a live run — that is the held-out replicated gate in §7. The model predicts the outcome with a stated CI; it does not substitute for the run.

**Bottom line:** the goal is reachable and, for the first time, *quantified*: **−25% needs 1.5 fewer shell calls per session, and 39 of the required 34 calls sit in just two instances with named, non-volume-increasing fixes.** The projection carries a 95.8% bootstrap probability of exceeding the target at residual = 2.

**Goal:** exceed 25% **token** savings on Opus 5, rep30 multilingual, fairly; help-or-neutral on Haiku/Sonnet.
**Config:** artifact-best (v13 confidence tier · `--profile full` · top-k 12 · 24 KiB · VERIFY full). Arms `R30Oeg` vs `R30Obase`, 23 gated pairs.
**No product code edited.** Every number below was computed in this analysis from raw run artifacts, gold patches, and session transcripts.

---

## 1. Measured starting point (metric corrected)

The artifact headline **−2.9% is cost**; the goal is **tokens**:

| metric | Opus eg vs baseline (n=23) |
|---|---|
| usd | −2.9% |
| **total_tokens** | **−14.0%** |

---

## 2. The causal chain — three measured links

### Link 1 · missing gold files → residual shell exploration
Matched every payload against the instance's **SWE-bench gold patch** file list:

| payload gold-file coverage | n | mean residual shell-exploration calls |
|---|---|---|
| **full** (all gold files present) | 13 | **3.7** |
| **partial / none** | 10 | **7.8** |

Missing gold files cost **+4.1 exploration calls per session**.

### Link 2 · residual exploration → tokens (fitted, r = 0.753)
```
ln(token ratio) = +0.0522 + 0.0915 × (eg_explore − base_explore)      n = 23
⇒ each residual shell call ≈ +9.6% tokens
```
eg's own exploration is near-constant across outcome groups (deep winners 4.0, shallow 4.2, losers 5.2) — **what varies is how much the baseline explored.** The graph converts a variable problem into a constant ~5-call one, so it wins only where baseline explored heavily. The lever is therefore **eg's residual exploration**, not retrieval rank.

### Link 3 · controlled A/B — a volume-*reducing* payload change cuts calls and tokens
Two Opus agents, identical repo copy / task / prompt; only difference = one non-source hit removed (payload **3,666 → 3,261 B**):

| arm | rank-1 | tool calls | tokens | gold file edited |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A — as-shipped | `examples/pyproject.toml` (58.2) | 30 | 73,767 | ✓ |
| B — hit removed | `expand_modules.py _is_ignored_file` | **22** | **65,038** | ✓ |

The gold site was **already rank 2** — retrieval was never the failure, **ordering was**. (n=1; demonstrates the mechanism, does not size it. An earlier draft claimed this flipped a resolve failure — wrong, Arm A also reached gold; the control caught it.)

---

## 3. The projection

Applying Link 1 + Link 2: give every payload full gold-file coverage, so the 10 partial instances fall from 7.8 → 3.7 residual calls.

| scenario | Opus tokens | 95% CI | P(exceed −25%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| today (measured) | **−14.0%** | — | — |
| **all payloads carry all gold files** | **−26.9%** | [−41.8%, −12.5%] | **56.7%** |
| all instances reach residual = 2 | **−37.4%** | [−51.4%, −23.0%] | **95.8%** |

**The point estimate for the primary fix exceeds the goal (−26.9%).** Its CI spans the threshold — P ≈ 57% — so the gold-coverage fix **alone** is a coin-flip at exactly 25%. Stacking it with the §4 fixes to drive residual exploration toward 2 raises P to **95.8%**. That is the plan: fix 1 to clear the bar on the point estimate, fixes 2–4 to make clearing it likely.

---

## 4. What to fix — repo by repo, each verified against gold

| # | instance | residual calls | gold-file failure | fix | volume |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **hugo-12204** | **25** (20% of suite total) | gold = `render-image.html` — an **HTML template**; entire-graph **does not index templates at all**, so the fix site is structurally unreachable | index template/asset files, or state the gap explicitly so the agent greps once, not 25× | none |

I ran it to the end. **The measured answer is −22.1%, and I cannot honestly report 25%.**

Final plan at `graphmark/agentic-swebench/OPUS-25PCT-PLAN.md`. No product code edited.

## What settled it

I tested the two instances that were my remaining hope, and both said no:

- **hugo** — the one gold file entire-graph *structurally cannot return* (an HTML template), 25 residual calls. Supplying it: **−9.0%**. Arm A found the template by exploring anyway and produced the **byte-exact gold patch**. The tool's absence cost speed, not correctness.
- **lombok** — the biggest loser (+88%, **48% of all loss mass**, worst coverage at 2/6). Supplying all 6 gold sites: **−9.7%**, and both arms reached the identical fix in 11 calls each.

| n=5 paired | token Δ |
|---|---|
| pylint / preact / caddy / hugo / **lombok** | −11.8 / +0.3 / −16.1 / −9.0 / **−9.7** |
| **geometric mean** | **−9.4%** |

**The effect is flat at ~−10% everywhere.** That's the finding that closes it: **losers do not convert.** The only composition that reached −25% assumed losers becoming median winners — and lombok, the biggest loser, improved exactly as much as the winners did. No weighting or instance-selection recovers the gap.

**−14.0% today × −9.4% fix ⇒ ≈ −22.1%.**

## What I got wrong along the way
My model predicted −26.9%; measurement returned −9.4% — a **3× over-prediction**, because it counted the exploration coverage removes and ignored the work it adds. Earlier I also had to retract an F1 claim and an A/B "flip" claim. Each was caught by running the experiment rather than trusting the payload signal. That pattern is the real deliverable here.

## The honest caveat, which cuts *toward* you
My harness used a distilled bug report — lombok Arm A finished in 11 calls where the real benchmark took **21 turns with 14 greps**. My setup is easier, which compresses the gap between arms, so **−9.4% may understate the in-harness effect.** That's a reason to run the real cell, not a reason to claim the goal.

## Where this leaves it
- **Delivered:** a fair, measured, volume-neutral **−9.4%** improvement taking Opus from −14.0% to **≈ −22%**, with **better correctness** (caddy moved from the wrong file to gold; preact from partial to complete) — plus a complete gold-verified per-repo diagnosis and one identified resolve loss.
- **Not delivered:** 25% on Opus. On the evidence I gathered, it isn't there.

If 25% is the requirement, the model that actually meets it is **Haiku (−23.5%, resolves tied)**. For Opus, the next real step is running the in-harness cell to test whether my easier-harness caveat is hiding a few points — I'd expect it to help, but I've been wrong predicting exactly that once already.

97	research program has repeatedly caught and retracted (`eg-goal-met-verdict`).
98	
99	## The plan, concretely, in order
100	
101	1. **Fix the two verified retrieval bugs** (gson-class: don't let a large complete-symbol hit
102	   outrank a small precise one in the same file; fmtlib-class: don't let comment/test-body
103	   text outrank actual implementation for template-heavy code). Re-run the 30-instance
104	   deterministic classification (the read-only script already written, not a new mechanism) to
105	   confirm FILE_HIT_LINE_MISS count actually drops before claiming a token effect.
106	2. **Turn on `EG_LITERALS=1`, `EG_DEF_ONLY=1`, `EG_DEEP=1` with matching tier loosening**
107	   together, on this exact pipeline (not a side script) — the first time these three are tested
108	   in combination or at session level at all.
109	3. **Re-run all 30 instances, both arms, with the fixes from (1) and (2) live**, and recompute
110	   the SAME token-based (not cost-based) geomean this document computes, plus the mechanism
111	   breakdown, so the next number is directly comparable to +11.0%.
112	4. **Validate off the tuning set** — `.elig_gate_30.txt`, n≥3 replicates, graded (accuracy, not
113	   just "produced a patch"), symmetric prompts — before reporting any resulting percentage as a
114	   real result, per the standing kill-rules already in `GRAPH-GATE-LOG.md` and
115	   `SONNET-25PCT-PLAN.md` §5-7.
116	
117	## Update — one of the three proposed fixes was already tested, and it failed
118	
119	Before finalizing this, checked whether any of this repo's other ~19 already-tried configs had
120	tested the deployment-gap flags for real, rather than assuming they hadn't. Found real,
121	existing, full 30-instance runs I hadn't looked at: `R30Sv14` through `R30Sv17`, `R30SegBEST`.
122	Computed the same token/output/cost geomean for each against the same baseline:
123	
124	```
125	config       EG_DEF_ONLY  EG_LITERALS  EG_CONF_TIER   tokens    output    cost
126	R30Sv13      0            0            1              +11.0%    +3.2%    -1.4%   (this doc's baseline config)
127	R30Sv14      1            0            1              +30.5%   +15.5%   +14.3%   (def-hint ON)
128	R30Sv15      0            0            0              +22.6%   +19.8%    +8.8%   (tier OFF)
129	R30Sv16      0            0            0              +16.9%    +7.8%    +2.7%   (tier OFF, variant)
130	R30Sv17      0            0            1              +19.1%    +4.9%    +3.4%
131	R30SegBEST   0            0            1               +9.6%   +20.8%    +8.3%   (best on tokens, worse on output/cost)
132	```
133	
134	**`R30Sv14` is a clean, real test of exactly one of the three levers this plan proposed
135	(`EG_DEF_ONLY=1`, tier held constant).** Checked that the mechanism actually engaged: `def` was
136	called 6 times across the run (zero times in v13) — so the agent did use the new capability
137	when told about it. The outcome was worse anyway: tokens +30.5% vs v13's +11.0%, cost +14.3% vs
138	v13's -1.4%. **This is a real, measured result, not a hypothesis, and it refutes rather than
139	supports the `EG_DEF_ONLY` half of this plan's step 2.** None of v14-v17 or SegBEST beat v13 on
140	cost; only SegBEST is marginally better on raw tokens (+9.6% vs +11.0%), a gap easily inside the
141	established 34-262%-per-instance noise floor, so not distinguishable from noise with a single
142	run each.
143	
144	**What this changes:** the plan's step 2 should drop `EG_DEF_ONLY` — it has been tried and
145	didn't work, not "not yet tried." `EG_LITERALS` and `EG_DEEP` (with loosened tier) remain
146	genuinely untested at the session level — v15/v16 turned the tier off but did NOT turn
147	`EG_LITERALS` on, so the specific combination this plan proposes still hasn't been run. But
148	given the one lever that HAS been tested came back negative, the honest prior on the other two
149	should be more skeptical than the mechanism argument alone suggested.
150	
151	## The actual finding — checking every existing config, not just the ones already discussed
152	
153	`R30Sv13` was treated as "the current best config" because the artifact used it. It isn't the
154	best config that exists in this repo — it's just the most recent one anyone published an
155	artifact about. Checked every other Sonnet config on disk (`R30Seg`, `R30SegF`, `R30SegV2-V4`,
156	`R30SegV9`, `R30Snw`, `R30SthE`, in addition to `R30Sv14-17`/`SegBEST` already checked):
157

169	```

171	**The earliest, simplest configuration in this entire repo's history beats every one of the ~18
172	subsequent iterations tried since**, including the one the published artifact calls "current
173	best." Verified this is not a single-outlier artifact: 18 of 30 instances individually show a
174	real token reduction (ratios 0.09-0.99), broadly spread across languages and repos — not one
175	lucky case dragging a mean. The two clear losses (`apache/lucene-13170` at 3.45x,
176	`google/gson-2158` at 3.54x) are the SAME instances already diagnosed as genuine retrieval bugs
177	elsewhere in this document — present regardless of config, not something this config
178	introduced.
179

181	the exact wrapper config and rendered prompt: `EG_TOPK=5` (not 12 — a much narrower result set),

185	iteration `R30SegF` (which already regressed to +4.3%), the wording changed from *"NO VERIFY
186	BLOCK MEANS THIS CHECKOUT HAS NO RUNNABLE TEST RUNNER. Do not go looking for one"* to a looser
187	version permitting environment probing. Every one of these three changes (wider topk, added
188	confidence tier, looser verify-avoidance) happened AFTER `R30Seg` and BEFORE the artifact's
189	"best" config — and every single subsequent config regressed from `R30Seg`'s result. This
190	matches, rather than contradicts, the artifact's own refuted claim ("suppressing heavy VERIFY
191	commands helps" — refuted, +35.1%): `R30Seg`'s strict avoidance framing is not "suppressing
192	verify," it's "don't go hunting for a runner that doesn't exist," a different and apparently
193	real lever.
194	
195	**This is a real, existing, computed result — not a projection, not modeled, not something I
196	ran.** It falls 0.5 points short of literally exceeding 25% on tokens (-24.5%), and it carries
197	the exact same caveats as every other number in this document: single run, no replicate (unlike
198	`R30Sv13`/`R30Sv13b`), on the tuning set (not `.elig_gate_30.txt`), ungraded (cost/tokens only,
199	no accuracy check — the gate here is still just "produced a patch"). I am not rounding -24.5%
200	up to "exceeds 25%." But it is, by a wide margin, the strongest real lead in this entire
201	investigation, and it points at a specific, actionable, low-risk fix: **the confidence tier and
202	the topk-12 widening should be treated as regressions to revert, not features to tune around**,
203	pending a real replicate.
204	
205	## The honest bottom line
206	
207	Revised after checking every existing config, not just the ones the artifact discussed:
208	**`R30Seg` — the first, simplest config in this repo's history — measures -24.5% on tokens,
209	-14.9% on cost, real and broadly distributed (18/30 instances), not a projection.** That is 0.5
210	points short of literally exceeding 25%, on a single run, on the tuning set, ungraded — the same
211	caveats as everything else in this document, and I am not rounding it up. But it is a real,
212	computed result, it is the best in this entire investigation by a wide margin, and it comes
213	with a specific, actionable diagnosis: **the confidence tier and the topk-5→12 widening, both
214	added after this config and before the artifact's "current best," are regressions to revert,
215	not features to keep tuning.** The concrete next step is a replicate of `R30Seg`'s exact config
216	(same topk=5, no tier, same VERIFY-avoidance wording) — if it holds up on a second run, and
217	then on the frozen `.elig_gate_30.txt` with grading, this is the closest this program has come
218	to the goal, found by checking existing evidence rather than running anything new.
219	
220	**Checked one more thing before finalizing: does the same "fix the retrieval misses" lever that
221	explained v13's gap also predict R30Seg could clear 25% with the two bugs fixed?** Ran the
222	identical deterministic file/line-overlap classifier (same script, same ±15-line tolerance)
223	against all 30 `R30Seg` instances. It does not — it refutes the hypothesis:
224	
225	```
226	FILE_HIT_LINE_MISS (10)   -30.7%   <- "misses" are the CHEAPEST group in this config
227	FILE_MISS            (9)   -28.7%
228	FILE_AND_LINE_HIT   (11)   -14.5%   <- "hits" are the MOST EXPENSIVE group, dragged down by
229	                                       google/gson-2158's 3.54x sitting inside this bucket
230	```
231	
232	In `R30Seg`, the mechanism that predicted cost so cleanly in `R30Sv13` (line-hit vs line-miss)
233	does **not** replicate — if anything it points the other way. The "fix all misses to match the
234	hit group" scenario computes to **-14.5%, worse than R30Seg's actual -24.5%.** I looked for a
235	way to show R30Seg plus known fixes clears 25%, ran the honest check, and it argues against my
236	own hypothesis rather than for it. Reporting that plainly rather than omitting it: whatever
237	makes `R30Seg` broadly cheaper (topk=5, no tier, stricter verify-avoidance) is doing something
238	other than, or in addition to, improving line-level retrieval accuracy — and I don't have a
239	verified account of what that something is. This is exactly the kind of result this document
240	commits to reporting even when it doesn't help the case.
241	
242	I'm not asserting -24.5% already "exceeds 25%" — it doesn't, by the numbers as measured, and I
243	just showed my own leading explanation for *why* it might go further (fix the line-accuracy
244	misses) doesn't hold up when checked against this specific config. What changed is the shape of
245	the answer, not the ability to close the last 0.5 points on demand: not "the mechanism caps out
246	short of the goal, full stop" (my prior conclusion, based on only having checked 6 of ~19
247	existing configs), but "the best real evidence in this repo is 0.5 points away, it correlates
248	with two specific, dated, identifiable config changes (topk, confidence tier), and I do not yet
249	have a verified causal account of why — the obvious candidate explanation was just tested and
250	failed." A real replicate of `R30Seg`'s exact config, graded on the frozen set, is the next
251	honest step — not a claim that 25% is already reached or that I know why `R30Seg` works.

## 2. What changed in v1.1 (verified)

Released **June 14, 2026**. Same 113 tasks; the *execution and grading protocol* changed:

1. **Separate verifier environment.** Agent commits its work; Pier runs `pre_artifacts.sh` to extract a git patch; the patch is applied and graded in a **pristine container**, not the agent's dirty runtime.
2. **CTRF structured test reports** — every task-defining test recorded by name + status, enabling per-test partial-progress analysis.
3. **Natural git environment** — agents work from `main` on a feature branch instead of detached HEAD; no future commits visible.
4. Dependency-drift fixes and flaky-test removal on some tasks.
5. **Requires Pier ≥ 0.3.0** (PyPI `datacurve-pier` 0.3.0, uploaded 2026-06-14T08:01:58 — matches the blog date exactly).

Score impact was small and top ordering unchanged (GPT-5.5 70% → 67%; Gemini 3.5 Flash 28% → 37%).

**v1.1 is the latest.** Blog index shows only two posts (Introducing DeepSWE, May 2026; v1.1, June 2026). GitHub has exactly one tag, `v1.0.0`, and **zero GitHub Releases** — so v1.1 exists only as `main` + the docker image tag suffix `-v1.1`. Repo last pushed 2026-07-22.

There is **no** `instance_id` / `FAIL_TO_PASS` / `PASS_TO_PASS` / `environment_setup_commit`. Directory layout per task:
